title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles.

title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays.

title: Genetic control of active matter
Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
abstract:
Abstract
                  Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li
                    6
                    PS
                    5
                    Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm
                    −2
                    at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm
                    −2
                    at 30 °C and 8 mA cm
                    −2
                    at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

title: Chiral cobalt-catalysed electrochemical enantioselective C–P coupling via phosphinoyl radicals
abstract: The stereocontrolled generation and utilization of phosphinoyl radicals for asymmetric synthesis remain a formidable challenge, stemming from their transient nature and stereochemical unpredictability. Here we show an electrocatalytic strategy that addresses this longstanding challenge via the merger of asymmetric Lewis acid catalysis with anodic oxidation to enable highly enantioselective C–P bond formation. Through a Lewis acid-coupled electron-transfer mechanism, the chiral cobalt catalyst directs radical generation while creating a confined chiral environment that governs stereoselective bond formation. This integrated platform enables intermolecular coupling under mild conditions, providing efficient access to a diverse array of P(V)-stereogenic compounds with excellent enantioselectivity (up to 99% enantiomeric excess) and enabling synthetic diversification. Mechanistic studies, including electrochemical analysis, radical-clock experiments and density functional theory calculations, corroborate the proposed pathway and elucidate the origin of stereocontrol. This work bridges electrochemistry, asymmetric catalysis and radical chemistry, expanding the synthetic toolkit for constructing phosphorus stereocentres.

title: Construction of benzochalcogenaboroles via single-atom editing of boracycles
abstract: Benzoxaborole is arguably the most important boron-based pharmacophore. Since Torssell's 1957 synthesis, hundreds of benzoxaborole derivatives have emerged, including US Food and Drug Administration-approved tavaborole and crisaborole. However, while peripheral modifications are well studied, synthetic challenges leave isoelectronic core modification less explored, despite its potential to enhance potency and reveal unexplored functions. Here we report a challenging ring expansion of benzoboretenes with elemental chalcogens, where benzoboretenes act as a 'diradical reservoir'. This synthetic protocol provides a versatile and modular platform for accessing three previously inaccessible classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeletons, in which the oxygen atom of the benzoxaborole core is formally replaced with Se, S or SO2. Preliminary biological evaluation reveals that this 'O-to-S' modification confers potent ferroptosis-inhibitory activity. Furthermore, its excellent functional group compatibility enables structure-activity optimization, leading to a 20-fold increase in cellular potency. This research not only expands the chemical space of boron-containing pharmacophores via single-atom ring expansion but also exemplifies how skeletal editing can unlock biological activities.

title: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates
abstract: Free-radical polymerization of simple vinyl monomers enables mass production of widely used polymers, but typically affords products that are poorly defined in molecular size and monomer sequence. Despite advances in precision polymerization, chain growth remains probabilistic, precluding molar-mass- and sequence-defined macromolecules. Here we report photoredox decarboxylative addition of bulky α-substituted acrylates, which enables quantitative addition of single building blocks without oligomerization. The α-acyl radical generated upon acrylate addition is irreversibly deactivated by rapid electron transfer within the photocatalytic cycle. A C(sp3)-centred radical is regenerated only after conversion of the terminal ester into a carboxylic acid and subsequent photoredox decarboxylation. Iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition yields vinyl macromolecules comprising residues identical to the repeat units of conventional vinyl polymers, without inseparable oligomeric impurities. Aperiodic vinyl-residue sequences can be assembled rapidly in continuous-flow reactors, offering a route towards fully automated synthesis of synthetic macromolecules and exploration of their sequence-dependent functions. A light-driven reaction scheme links a carboxylic acid to a vinyl compound through a decarboxylated radical intermediate. The resulting product retains the substituents from both starting materials. Iterative single-unit addition and deprotection yield mass-defined and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules. Below, examples of mass-defined and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules illustrate the products: the mass-defined example has a repeated phenyl-bearing unit, while the sequence-defined example contains phenyl, methoxy-substituted phenyl, and fluorine-substituted phenyl groups.

title: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
abstract:
Abstract
                  Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing.

title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V-1 s-1 and submillimetre drift lengths-far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from -17cm (ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects-often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes-and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro
abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1-7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide
                    1–4
                    , yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals
abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30-40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4-32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7-42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker-ejection fraction-although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex
                    1,2
                    . Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools
                    3–6
                    . Type I-F
                    Pseudoalteromonas
                    CAST (
                    Pse
                    CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far
                    7
                    and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution
                    8
                    . However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation
                    9
                    . Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the
                    Pse
                    CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the
                    Pse
                    CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa
                    Pse
                    CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot-superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man's Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but lack topological protection3-5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man's Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6-8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man's Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Heterochromatin typically represses genes
                    1,2
                    , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation
                    3–7
                    . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent
                    8
                    . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly
                    8
                    . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
abstract: Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

title: ‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs
abstract: Awe, anxiety and opportunity: mathematics community shares mixed emotions following the solution of the field’s biggest unsolved problem.

title: Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes
abstract: Economics is the outlier — top prizes in science, engineering and other social sciences go to researchers at a greater variety of institutions.

title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems-a centuries-old practice2,3-causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800-2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48-99) mW m-2-equivalent to 2.7 (1.8-3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing-originating from 0.4-0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52-110) mW m-2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (-9 (-15--2) mW m-2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
abstract: Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol-1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment
                    1,2
                    . How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb-seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
abstract: Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1-7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10-12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of O ( 1 ) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade-TniQ, TnsC and TnsA-TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans 1 , yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5–42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo , as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus ). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo .

title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1-3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features.

title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut-brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop-a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut-brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

title: The leading cities in the world for high-quality research in 2025
abstract: A decade of data on the top-performing science cities in the Nature Index.

title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice
abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

title: Single-Atom Cerium Unlocks Efficient Hydrogen Spillover within Nonreducible Zeolites through a Proton–Electron Relay
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen spillover connects hydrogen activation with spatially separated catalytic functions, yet engineering efficient hydrogen transport through nonreducible zeolites remains an outstanding challenge owing to the absence of intrinsic pathways for coupled proton–electron transfer. Here, we show that isolated cerium atoms incorporated into Pt/USY transform the zeolite from a passive support into an active medium for solid-state hydrogen transport. In situ spectroscopy, isotopic tracing, and theoretical calculations reveal that atomically dispersed Ce species dynamically generate localized hydroxyl groups and oxygen vacancies that cooperatively establish a proton–electron relay, substantially lowering the kinetic barrier for hydrogen migration through zeolitic micropores. The resulting enhancement in hydrogen spillover extends hydrogen delivery to spatially remote Brønsted acid sites, suppresses coke formation, and significantly improves polyolefin hydrocracking stability. These findings establish hydrogen transport as a tunable design parameter in bifunctional zeolite catalysis and provide a general strategy for engineering hydrogen-transfer pathways in nonreducible porous materials.

title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

title: Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Frameworks as Multifunctional Platforms for Synergistic Chemo-Photo-Biocatalytic Enantioselective Synthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a promising platform for the precise customization of multifunctional composites, enabling the optimization of synergistic effects between catalysts and significantly enhancing both stability and catalytic performance. Despite this potential, this idealized system is still in the exploratory stage. Herein, we integrated a chemical catalyst with a photoenzyme-based enantioselective catalytic platform into a single system, achieving the sequential transformation from C2-alkylation to asymmetric Mannich reaction products. A hierarchically porous (HP) UiO-67 material was constructed as the supporting platform. Through a post-synthetic ligand exchange strategy, Pd(II) and Ru(II) catalysts were simultaneously immobilized, while wheat germ lipase (WGL) was encapsulated within the mesoporous channels, yielding the multifunctional catalyst WGL@HP-UiO-67-Pd/Ru. This catalyst afforded satisfactory yields of 62–94% in the C2-arylation reaction and enantioselectivities of 69–93% in the asymmetric Mannich reaction. In this sequential catalytic transformation, the multifunctional catalyst afforded an overall efficiency of 47.6%, corresponding to a 3.8-fold enhancement over the homogeneous catalyst system. These findings provide deeper insight into the role of multifunctional catalysis in sequential reactions and underscore its considerable promise for the asymmetric synthesis of organic compounds and pharmaceutical agents.

title: Fe,Ni Co-modification Balances Activity and Stability in RuO2 for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) needs oxygen evolution anodes that combine high-current-density performance with long-term operational stability, yet RuO2, the most active benchmark oxide catalyst, dissolves under sustained anodic operation. Catalyst development almost always selects compositions by activity measured at 10 mA cm–2 in three-electrode cells, a regime far below device conditions. Here, we synthesize a library of transition-metal-modified RuO2 catalysts and show that this selection criterion fails in an operating electrolyzer. Screening across Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni modifiers identifies RuO2–FeNi as the optimal balance, with a Tafel slope of 47 mV dec–1 and a Ru mass activity of 1357 A gRu–1 at 400 mV overpotential, 14 times that of commercial RuO2, despite the smallest electrochemically active surface area in the series. In a membrane electrode assembly, RuO2–FeNi reaches 1 A cm–2 at 1.82 V in polarization measurements at 80 °C. In a separate 200 h durability test at 250 mA cm–2 and 60 °C, its cell voltage rises by 274 mV, most of it within the first 25 h, whereas RuO2–Fe, which reaches twice the current density at 1.82 V, rises by 560 mV within 64 h under the same protocol. Density functional theory traces the activity of RuO2–FeNi to Fe/Ni co-incorporation, which renders Ru electron-deficient, downshifts the Ru 4d band center, and moderates the adsorption of oxygenated intermediates; higher compositional complexity introduces electronic disorder without further benefit. Intermediate compositional complexity, selected by device-level testing rather than by screening activity, emerges as the design target for Ru-based AEMWE anodes.

title: Highway-Inspired Hollow Fillers to Improve CO2 Transport in Mixed-Matrix Membranes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inorganic fillers play a critical role in mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) to improve membrane separation performance. However, it is faced with a persistent trade-off: low filler loading is insufficient to achieve significant performance enhancement, while high filler loading introduces stress defects that weaken membrane strength. Developing highly efficient porous fillers capable of delivering substantial separation improvements at low loading offers a solution to this challenge. Herein, we report the design of etched KMnF3 (KMnF3-EC) fillers inspired by the Maxwell dispersion theory and highway transport concepts. These fillers possess a hollow core and a highly porous shell, which maximize pore volume per unit mass of filler and create rapid gas transport pathways. Incorporation of KMnF3-EC fillers into Pebax membranes resulted in remarkable gas separation performance at an ultralow filler loading (1.5 wt %), yielding a 120% increase in gas permeability and a 57.1% enhancement in gas selectivity. Owing to such low filler loading, the membranes maintained excellent mechanical properties, with elongation at break exceeding 800% and a Young’s modulus above 100 MPa. Direct benchmarking against commonly used porous fillers revealed that KMnF3-EC improves gas separation performance with an order-of-magnitude greater efficiency. These findings provide a promising strategy for designing advanced fillers that overcome the challenging MMM performance–mechanical strength trade-off, thereby facilitating the development of durable and energy-efficient membrane separation.

title: Ice Plant-Inspired Hierarchical Nanofibrous Film for Outdoor-Stable Passive Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Daytime radiative cooling provides a low-energy approach for passive thermal management. However, existing materials primarily focus on cooling intensity, often neglecting critical issues such as nighttime overcooling, pollutant adhesion, and long-term stability. Inspired by the bladder-like epidermal structures of Mesembryanthemum crystallinum leaves, this work developed a biomimetic nanofibrous film based on poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (P(VDF-HFP)). To translate this natural hierarchical morphology into an effective light-regulating structure, P(VDF-HFP) nanofibers were used as the supporting framework, while TiO2 was introduced as a surface scattering and functional component. Through a precursor-based strategy and electrospinning, a uniform hierarchical inorganic particle/polymer fibrous structure was constructed. This multiscale architecture enhances solar scattering and regulates mid-infrared emission. The film achieves an AM1.5G-weighted solar reflectance of 90.5% over 0.3–2.5 μm, while its infrared emission is mainly concentrated within the atmospheric window. This spectral selectivity supports daytime heat dissipation while limiting radiative heat loss outside the atmospheric window. Outdoor tests demonstrated that the nanofibrous film exhibited a temperature up to 5.8 °C lower than that of a commercial white fabric reference under identical conditions. Moreover, it retained high whiteness after 230 h of UV irradiation and exhibited photocatalytic pollutant-degradation capability. This bioinspired hierarchical design offers a practical strategy for developing flexible radiative cooling materials with high reflectance, selective emission, and environmental stability.

title: Low-Hysteresis and Overshoot-Free Capacitive Strain Sensor for Silent Speech Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional capacitive strain sensors suffer from mechanical hysteresis, signal overshoot, and delayed response due to viscoelastic relaxation in solid dielectric materials. We address these limitations through a synergistic structure–material design combining an auxetic porous conductive framework with a solid–liquid hybrid dielectric. The auxetic architecture reversibly deforms to suppress hysteresis, while the confined ionic liquid eliminates viscoelastic relaxation, enabling rapid, stable signal output with negligible overshoot. In situ scanning electron microscopy characterization reveals dynamic liquid-bridge formation and rupture during deformation, establishing the mechanistic link between multiphase dielectric evolution and capacitance modulation. Our sensor demonstrates exceptional performance: <2% hysteresis, 57 ms response time, negligible overshoot, gauge factor of 3.1, and stability over 8500 cycles. A wearable silent speech recognition system validates its practical applicability, achieving a classification accuracy of 93.9%. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for soft strain sensors with simultaneously suppressed hysteresis, minimal overshoot, and fast response, enabling next-generation wearable electronics and intelligent interfaces.

title: Supramolecular Manipulation of Copper Nanoclusters Boosts Chiral Optical Performances
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance of chiral metal nanoclusters is generally limited by random ligand motion, which induces non-radiative decay and impairs chiral coupling, resulting in low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) and weak intrinsic chirality. Here in this study, drawing inspiration from the art of marionette puppetry, where a puppeteer controls a puppet through strings attached to strategic points, we construct hydrogen-bonded organic superstructures (HBOSs) composed of cyanuric acid and 1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triamine to manipulate chiral glutathione-capped copper nanoclusters (GSH-Cu NCs). The hydrogen-bonding interactions between HBOSs and GSH-Cu NCs act as the "strings" that precisely direct their spatial arrangement and effectively restrain random ligand motion. The manipulation processes harness the orientation of nanoclusters and balanced the electric and magnetic dipoles, therefore boosting the chiral optical performances including increased PLQY to 94.15% and amplified CPL over an order of magnitude to –1.39 × 10–2. Additionally, the composites also exhibit thermally reversible fluorescence between –20 and 20 °C, demonstrating the reversible nature of hydrogen-bonding interactions. The red-emitting GSH-Cu NCs/HBOSs phosphors are integrated with commercial phosphors onto an InGaN chip, yielding white light-emitting diodes that exhibit near-ideal CIE coordinates of (0.33, 0.34) and a high color rendering index of 92.1. Our study offers a strategy to overcome the trade-off between electric and magnetic dipoles which further provides insights for the design of next-generation high-performance optoelectronic devices.

title: Infrared–Thermal Co-driven CO2–Ethanol Coupling to Diethyl Carbonate Enabled by Electron-Rich Lattice Oxygen
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals represents a promising pathway for CO2 mitigation and utilization. The direct synthesis of diethyl carbonate (DEC) from CO2 and CH3CH2OH is particularly attractive owing to its high atom economy. However, the direct thermocatalytic synthesis of DEC remains inefficient because of unfavorable thermodynamics and the substantial kinetic barrier for coupling CO2 with ethoxy species (CH3CH2O*). Herein, an IR-thermal co-driven catalytic strategy was developed over reconstructed CeO2 (CeO2-500), enabling a DEC formation rate of 9.3 mmol g–1 h–1 without any dehydrating agent, representing a 3.1-fold enhancement compared with unreconstructed CeO2. This enhancement is attributed to the reconstruction-induced local defect structures in CeO2, which create an electron-rich lattice oxygen environment that strengthens CO2 adsorption and activation. Meanwhile, local structure modulation enhances IR light absorption and generates mildly oxidative charge carriers, which accelerate CH3CH2O* formation and promote its coupling with activated CO2 to form the key CH3CH2O-CO* intermediate, thereby boosting DEC formation. Thermal energy facilitates the transport of IR-induced charge carriers and lowers the kinetic barrier for DEC formation. This work provides an IR–thermal co-driven catalytic strategy for efficient CO2 conversion into value-added carbonates.

title: Smart pH-Switchable Nanozyme-Hydrogel Platform with Phycocyanin-Stabilized Mn-Doped Prussian Blue for Synergistic Photothermal-Multienzyme Cascade Therapy of Infected Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Infected wound healing remains a major clinical challenge due to persistent bacterial infection, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), prolonged inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration. Here, we develop a smart composite hydrogel (PPB/PB-Mn@PC) by integrating Mn-doped Prussian blue nanozymes surface-modified with phycocyanin (PB-Mn@PC) into a dynamic polyvinyl alcohol/pullulan/borax (PPB) hydrogel. The system features pH-responsive accelerated release of PB-Mn@PC in the acidic infected microenvironment, combined with excellent self-adaptive filling, self-healing, and tissue adhesion properties. The PB-Mn@PC nanozymes exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency under 808 nm laser irradiation and multienzyme-mimicking activities. Notably, their catalytic behavior dynamically switches: predominant SOD/CAT-like ROS scavenging under neutral conditions for cytoprotection, and enhanced POD-like activity under acidic conditions that supports bacterial killing without a proportional increase in freely diffusible ·OH, thereby limiting collateral oxidative burden. In vitro, the composite hydrogel demonstrates excellent biocompatibility, efficient broad-spectrum antibacterial activity (including biofilm disruption), ROS scavenging, and promotion of macrophage M2 polarization. In vivo, in S. aureus-infected full-thickness wound models, the smart hydrogel significantly reduces bacterial burden, accelerates wound closure, enhances re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis, while effectively suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). This work presents a rationally designed smart hydrogel platform that integrates dynamic mechanics, intelligent microenvironment-responsive release, and synergistic photothermal-multienzyme therapy, offering a promising strategy for the efficient management of infected wounds.

title: Sequential Defect Engineering Enables External-Reductant-Free In Situ Formation of Cu2S Electron Reservoirs in a TiO2/SCN/Cu2S S-Scheme Heterojunction for Noble-Metal-Free Photocatalytic H2 Evolution
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Noble-metal-free photocatalytic H2 evolution is often limited by the need for external reductants to generate low-valence cocatalysts and by poorly controlled interfacial charge transport. Here, we establish a sequential defect-engineering strategy that uses trace sulfur in sulfur-doped carbon nitride (SCN) as an intrinsic reductant and sulfur source to construct Cu2S directly on a preformed TiO2/SCN heterojunction. This sequence simultaneously avoids noble metals and external reducing agents while promoting intimate Cu-S interfacial bonding and the formation of oxygen and copper vacancies. The resulting TiO2-SCN-Cu2S S-scheme heterojunction delivers 38.06 mmol g−1 H2 in 6 h (average rate: 6.34 mmol g−1 h−1), 21-fold higher than TiO2-SCN and 1.57-fold higher than a TiO2-SCN-Pt benchmark containing 3.6 wt % Pt, tested at the same total catalyst mass. Experiments, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), and machine-learning trend analysis collectively show that the copper-addition sequence controls copper speciation, defect population, light harvesting, and interfacial charge separation. This work identifies sequentially programmed Cu2S formation and vacancy generation as an integrated design strategy for reductant-free, noble-metal-free S-scheme photocatalysts.

title: Tuning Surface Termination of Perovskite Nanocrystals to Control Interfacial Charge Transfer and Photocatalytic Efficiency
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Efficient extraction of photogenerated charge carriers remains a major challenge in metal halide perovskite nanocrystal (MHP NC) photocatalysis because of rapid electron–hole recombination at the nanocrystal surface. Although interfacial binding between the NC surface and charge-acceptor molecules is known to facilitate charge separation, the influence of nanocrystal surface termination on this process remains largely unexplored. Herein, we investigate how the surface termination of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals (CPB NCs) regulates interfacial binding with para-substituted aniline (PSA) hole acceptors bearing –SH, –COOH, and –NH2 anchoring groups and how these interactions influence photocatalytic performance. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal a complete reversal in hole-transfer efficiency upon changing the surface termination from Pb-rich to Br-rich, demonstrating that surface-dependent preferential interactions govern interfacial charge-transfer dynamics. These findings are further validated through the photoreductive homocoupling of phenacyl bromide via C–C bond coupling, where Pb-rich CPB NCs exhibit significantly superior photocatalytic activity owing to stronger coordination-like interactions with the anchoring groups. Overall, this work establishes surface termination as a critical design parameter for controlling interfacial charge transfer and provides a rational strategy for developing highly efficient perovskite nanocrystal photocatalysts.

title: Intrinsic High-κ Elastic Dielectrics from Dual-Fluorinated Polyurethane Urea Enable Low-Voltage Stretchable Organic Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-voltage operation in intrinsically stretchable transistors fundamentally relies on gate dielectrics that reconcile intrinsic stretchability with a high dielectric constant (high-κ). However, reconciling enhanced dielectric performance with robust mechanical resilience remains a persistent challenge. Here, we report a molecular engineering strategy to synthesize a series of functionalized polyurethane urea (PUU) by rationally incorporating distinct functional groups into the hard-segment domains. Among the synthesized variants, the difluorinated analogue (2F-PUU) achieves an optimal trade-off, combining a high κ of 7.06 at 1 kHz, exceptional stretchability up to 1623%, strain-insensitive dielectric behavior, solvent reprocessability, and an ultralow surface roughness of 0.273 nm. Stretchable organic transistors employing 2F-PUU as the gate dielectric operate at a low voltage of –10 V and sustain stable electrical performance under 50% tensile strain. Moreover, a 5 × 5 transistor array based on 2F-PUU delivers a 100% fabrication yield, with a peak mobility of 0.51 cm2 V–1 s–1 and a maximum on/off current ratio exceeding 104. Collectively, this work establishes a viable molecular design roadmap for intrinsically stretchable high-κ dielectrics, paving the way toward low-power, mechanically durable stretchable organic electronics.

title: Modulation of Oxygen Vacancy Charge-State Evolution via Rare-Earth Praseodymium Doping for Improving the Photostability of Amorphous InZnO Thin-Film Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal oxide thin-film transistors (MOTFTs) used as backplanes for large-area and high-resolution OLED displays require simultaneously high carrier mobility and operational stability. Light-induced instability arising from the generation and persistence of photocarriers in the oxide semiconductor remains a critical challenge. Trace praseodymium (Pr) doping substantially enhances the illumination stability of amorphous InZnO (a-IZO) TFTs while maintaining high electron mobility has been reported, yet the underlying electronic mechanism remains elusive. Here, combining first-principles calculations with experimental investigations, the mechanism of enhanced photostability in Pr:IZO MOTFTs was revealed. We found that redox-active Pr dopants act as dynamic charge buffers to regulate the photoinduced charge redistribution and oxygen vacancy (VO) charge state evolution in a-IZO. The localized Pr 4f electronic states participate in a reversible charge redistribution process during the photoinduced ionization–recovery cycle, which suppresses the evolution of VO toward kinetically trapped charge states, preserves the electronic accessibility of VO related gap states for carrier recapture, and reduces photoinduced lattice reconstruction. Time-resolved transient absorption measurements further confirmed that Pr incorporation accelerates photocarrier relaxation, shortening the characteristic fast decay lifetime from ∼47 to ∼6 ps. These findings establish a direct correlation between localized electronic state evolution and photoexcited carrier dynamics and may provide a new strategy based on redox-active cation engineering to overcome the long-standing mobility–stability trade-off in metal oxide semiconductors.

title: Metallic–Ionic Copper Cooperative Interfacial Engineering Enables Stabler and Fast-Charging Silicon Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon is considered one of the most promising anode materials for next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its exceptionally high theoretical capacity. Nevertheless, its practical use is constrained by coupled mechanical degradation, unstable solid electrolyte interphase evolution, and sluggish charge transport during cycling. Herein, we propose a previously unexplored metallic–ionic cooperative interfacial engineering strategy that fundamentally reconstructs the silicon interface through the synergistic integration of a hydrogen-bonded mucic acid network and hybrid Cu0/Cu+/Cu2+species. Unlike conventional metal modification, the coexistence of metallic and ionic copper forms a multifunctional interface that can simultaneously accommodate stress, improve electron/Li+ transport, and regulate the chemical evolution of the interfacial phase, resulting in the formation of a thin, dense, inorganic SEI rich in LiF, which suppresses the continued decomposition of the electrolyte and interfacial degradation. Benefiting from this integrated regulation mechanism, the optimized Si@MA*Cu anode exhibits an ultralow electrode thickness expansion of only 4.5% after 200 cycles, corresponding to a 97.3% reduction relative to pristine silicon, together with a reversible capacity of 1550.0 mAh g–1 after 400 cycles at 1 A g–1 and a high–rate capacity of 1375.5 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1. Electrochemical tests show faster charge transfer, enhanced Li+ diffusion, and dominant pseudocapacitance, while DFT calculations reveal that hybrid Cu states reconstruct interfacial electronic structure, boost Fermi–level electronic density, strengthen Li adsorption, and lower Li+ migration barriers. This study establishes a paradigm for metal-ion synergy by combining mechanical adaptation, interfacial phase control, and charge transport, providing a general interfacial design principle for developing durable, fast-charging, and high-energy alloy-type battery electrodes.

title: Comparative Study of Naphthalene Diimide Terminal Groups for Buried-Interface Modification in Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract SnO2 serves as a leading electron transport material in n–i–p perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet its practical deployment is constrained by interfacial defects and energy-level mismatch. Herein, two naphthalene diimide (NDI) derivatives—DPNDI with pyridine terminals and NDI-N with dimethylamino terminals—are introduced at the SnO2/perovskite buried interface to investigate the effects of terminal groups on interfacial chemistry, crystallization, and charge dynamics. Theoretical calculations and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm that DPNDI coordinates Pb2+ via pyridine N, while NDI-N coordinates via carbonyl O. Both form a dipole layer that retards crystallization, reduces defects, and minimizes voids and strain. NDI-N has a larger dipole due to intramolecular charge transfer from the dimethylamino groups to the NDI backbone, which improves SnO2 conductivity and reduces the conduction band offset to 0.08 eV, facilitating electron extraction. Consequently, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) increases from 19.88% (control) to 21.81% (DPNDI PSCs) and 24.17% (NDI-N PSCs). Unencapsulated NDI-N devices show superior storage stability, retaining 68.97% of initial PCE after 1000 h in N2 vs 50.22% for control. Under continuous maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in air, however, the encapsulated control device retains only 87.74% of its initial efficiency after 500 h, markedly lower than the 92.67% retained by encapsulated NDI-N devices.

title: An Injectable Hydrogel Integrating Antibacterial and Antioxidant Functions for the Treatment of Periodontitis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by microbial dysbiosis and sustained by a dysregulated host response, in which excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial dysfunction, and persistent inflammation contribute to progressive periodontal tissue destruction.
