Here, we developed LAEPL-SA, an injectable composite hydrogel prepared by conjugating α-lipoic acid (LA) to ε-poly-l-lysine (EPL) and incorporating the resulting LAEPL into a sodium alginate (SA) network. The system was designed to simultaneously reduce the microbial challenge and excessive oxidative/inflammatory injury within the periodontal microenvironment. EPL contributed direct cationic antibacterial activity, whereas LA provided antioxidant and cytoprotective effects associated with reduced ROS accumulation. LAEPL-SA exhibited favorable injectability, self-healing behavior, rheological stability, wet hydroxyapatite-surface retention, and antibacterial activity. Compared with LA-SA, LAEPL-SA showed stronger antioxidant effects and improved protection against oxidative injury. In H2O2-stimulated human periodontal ligament stem cells, LAEPL-SA reduced intracellular and mitochondrial ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, decreased apoptosis, and suppressed inflammatory responses. In a ligature-induced rat periodontitis model, LAEPL-SA reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure, decreased osteoclast activity, and alleviated alveolar bone resorption. These protective effects were accompanied by activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway. Collectively, LAEPL-SA provides a multifunctional local therapeutic platform that integrates antibacterial activity with attenuation of excessive oxidative and inflammatory stress for periodontitis treatment.

title: VEGF-Rich Engineered Apoptotic Extracellular Vesicles Loaded with Quercetin for Androgenetic Alopecia Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is a progressive hair loss disorder characterized by follicular miniaturization, oxidative stress-induced dermal papilla cell apoptosis, downregulated angiogenic genes, and insufficient vascularization in the perifollicular microenvironment. Current pharmacotherapies are limited by transient efficacy and side effects, necessitating novel delivery systems that simultaneously address the vascular insufficiency and oxidative burden to halt and reverse follicular miniaturization. In this study, we constructed genetically engineered apoptotic extracellular vesicles (ApoEV) from adipose mesenchymal stem cells (AMSCs) that were functionalized with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) to promote angiogenesis and loaded with Quercetin (QUE) for antioxidant defense (VEGF ApoEV@QUE). The VEGF ApoEV@QUE significantly promoted human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) proliferation, migration, and tube formation. In addition, it promoted dermal papilla cells (DPCs) proliferation, protected DPCs from oxidative stress by activating the Wnt/β-catenin and AKT/GSK3β signaling pathways. In the AGA mouse model, subcutaneous injection of VEGF ApoEV@QUE accelerated the telogen-to-anagen transition, increased hair follicle density, and enhanced perifollicular vascularization compared to monotherapies. Biosafety analysis revealed no overt systemic toxicity in this short-term model. This study demonstrates that engineering ApoEV to co-deliver surface-anchored angiogenic factors and intracellular antioxidants provides an enhanced dual-action therapeutic strategy for AGA.

title: Development and clinical validation of a multimodal AI framework to predict persistent fever during antibiotic therapy in hospitalized patients with cancer
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Among hospitalized cancer patients, persistent fever despite intravenous antibiotics often triggers treatment escalation and additional diagnostics. Earlier identification of patients at low risk for ongoing fever could support more selective decision-making. We developed and compared multimodal AI frameworks to predict persistent fever at the 48–72-hour reassessment window. Models integrated structured variables, time-series, notes, and chest imaging. Models were developed in a University Hospital Essen cohort and evaluated using holdout validation, two pooled regional hospitals, and MIMIC-IV ICU. A feature-level tabularized multimodal TabPFN model showed consistent discrimination, with AUC 0.84 (95% CI, 0.81–0.86) in cross-validation, 0.82 (95% CI, 0.77–0.87) in holdout validation, and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.74–0.81) in MIMIC-IV; other multimodal strategies showed comparable but more variable performance. Performance was primarily driven by temperature dynamics, while chest-radiograph imaging provided no incremental predictive value. In a clinician validation study, the multimodal model outperformed clinicians (Trial 1 balanced accuracy: 0.77 vs 0.60; Trial 2: 0.79 vs 0.57), while clinician balanced accuracy reached 0.71 (95% CI 0.67–0.75) in the AI-assisted condition, suggesting potential benefit of AI support. Overall, multimodal AI demonstrates potential to support 48-hour antibiotic reassessment and stewardship-oriented decision-making, although further prospective studies are needed.

title: Hydrogen-based green steel corridors: cost saving and emission reduction potentials of emerging trade routes
abstract: Deploying hydrogen-based direct-reduced iron (H 2 -DRI) technologies will be decisive to defossilize the global steel sector by replacing coal-based blast furnaces (BF) in conventional steelmaking. DRI can then either be directly fed into an electric-arc-furnace (EAF) and alternative electric smelting furnaces or transported as cold hot-briquetted iron (HBI) and a green commoditiy to a steel plant. The availability and expansion of low-cost renewable electricity and green hydrogen supply options is the essential and site-specific precondition to deploy H 2 -DRI plants that can be gradually switched from natural gas to hydrogen. However, near-zero emission steel made from H 2 -DRI needs to produced at competitive costs compared to fossil steel regulated under carbon emission pricing schemes. Based on revised green hydrogen cost forecasts in potentially low-cost countries like Australia or Oman, this study reveals the cost competitiveness of emerging green steel corridors built on international partnerships. With green HBI then exported to a representative EAF green steelmaking site, the analysis shows the potential cost savings of importing green HBI from renewable-rich countries when facing a future lack of affordable hydrogen supply options in leading steel countries like Germany or South Korea characterized by a high dependence on energy imports. Overall, low-emission crude steel based on 66 vol% H 2 -HBI imports achieves fossil cost parity in Germany in 2040 at increased carbon prices in the EU, while all 100% hydrogen-based steel scenarios inhere higher costs with a premium of 6%–13% over natural gas-based DRI-EAF crude steel at 828 € t −1 CS (with 0% scrap) at hydrogen costs ranging between 4.14 and 4.94 € kg −1 H 2 . In addition, a cradle-to-gate accounting of greenhouse gas emissions reveals that cost savings from HBI imports potentially come at the expense of up to 50% higher total emissions compared to an integrated H 2 -DRI-EAF plant running on iron ore pellet imports. All 100% H 2 -DRI-based scenarios yield an emission reduction between 42%–57% compared to a domestic benchmarked NG-DRI-EAF scenario at 1293 kg CO 2 (e) t −1 CS. The carbon footprint analysis further highlights the effect of upstream defossilization measures related to iron ore mining, pelletising and transport by rail and ship.

title: Redox-Window-Guided Metal Node Editing of Copper Metal–Organic Frameworks for Recyclable Heterogeneous Cu(I) Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cu(I) catalysts are central to many bond-forming reactions, but integrating Cu(I) sites into recyclable porous solids remains difficult because Cu(I) is easily oxidized, over-reduced, or leached. Here, we report redox-window-guided metal node editing as an oxidation-state-programming strategy that converts hydrolytically fragile Cu(II)3BTC2 into a hydrolytically stable mixed-valence Cu(I/II) MOF catalyst. Phenolic reductants are selected by matching their oxidation potentials to the Cu(II)–to–Cu(I) window of Cu(II)3BTC2, enabling proton-coupled, inner-sphere single-electron transfer at Cu paddlewheel nodes. Hydroquinone gives the most controlled material, [p-Ph(OH)2]-Cu3BTC2, containing 33.4% Cu(I), ship-in-a-bottle [Cu(MeCN)4]+ complexes, mesopores, and enhanced stability under humid, acidic, and basic conditions. As a heterogeneous catalyst for hydrative amide synthesis, [p-Ph(OH)2]-Cu3BTC2 affords 92% yield, negligible Cu leaching, five-cycle recyclability, and the highest turnover number among compared Cu(I) catalysts.

title: Electron-Deficient β-Diketone Ligand Enabled Ni-Catalyzed Remote Dicarbofunctionalization of Alkenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A nickel-catalyzed remote migratory dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes was realized with high efficiency and excellent regioselectivity without the assistance of a directing group. The formation of a thermodynamically stable allyl-metal intermediate and the use of an electron-deficient β-diketone ligand are the keys to the success of these remote diarylation and arylalkenylation. This protocol features a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group compatibility, providing a series of remote diarylated and arylalkenylated hydrocarbons in high yields. Notably, the allyl group represents one of the most synthetically useful handles in synthetic chemistry, and the synthetic values of this process have been demonstrated by the formal synthesis of allocolchicinoids, and by the preparation of a RARγ selective retinoid agonist in a highly efficient and step-economical manner.

title: Cation Pinning toward High-Concentration Formic Acid Fuel Cells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite the high theoretical energy density of concentrated formic acid, direct formic acid fuel cells (DFAFCs) incorporating conventional nanoparticle or emerging single-atom anodes exhibit a precipitous power loss as fuel concentration scales. While CO poisoning is traditionally blamed, we show that this limitation is governed by interfacial acid–base kinetics. By implementing a cation-pinning strategy via rare-earth oxide-modified Rh single-atom sites, we stabilize OH– from water dissociation through interfacial ionic anchoring to trigger localized pH inversion. This modulation leads to the preferential enrichment of interfacial formate, identified here as the primary reactive species. Consequently, Dy2O3–Rh/NC delivers a mass activity 641-fold higher than that of nanoparticle benchmarks. The resulting anode achieves an exceptional peak power density of 375 mW cm–2, surpassing commercial Pd/C across all concentrations. This work establishes precision ionic management as a versatile approach to breaking performance limits in multiphase catalysis.

title: Rh2C3− Cluster-Driven Nitrogen Activation: Trapping a High-Energy Intermediate
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Converting inert and globally abundant molecules such as N2 into useful chemicals is central to sustainable energy and environmental chemistry. Herein, we investigate the gas-phase reaction of the Rh2C3− anion with N2 using mass spectrometry, anion photoelectron spectroscopy, and quantum chemical calculations. The experimental spectra of Rh2C3− and Rh2C3N2− exhibit closely similar features, indicating a preserved electronic core upon N2 attachment. Theoretical analysis further reveals that the end-on N2 adsorption complex is a trapped high-energy intermediate whose subsequent transformation is prevented by an activation barrier that necessitates additional energy input, and that this complex exhibits superior performance in the coconversion of diverse energy-bearing gas molecules. Furthermore, the subsequent application of oriented external electric fields provides a nondestructive and continuously adjustable means of modifying the intrinsic barrier heights, thereby effectively switching the reaction mechanism. These findings elucidate the complex reaction network of Rh2C3− with N2, establish a reliable spectroscopic fingerprint for identifying isomeric intermediates, and provide fundamental insights into electronic control strategies for catalytic nitrogen activation.

title: Ligand-Controlled Chemodivergent β-Methylene C(sp3)–H Heteroarylation of Aliphatic Acids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving ligand-controlled chemodivergence in C–H activation is still difficult because several competing reaction pathways are available when multiple C–H bonds are present. We describe a Pd(II)-catalyzed, chemodivergent β-methylene C(sp3)–H heteroarylation of free aliphatic acids in which two distinct classes of bidentate pyridone ligands each deliver a different product. These two ligands also overcome a long-standing inhibitory effect of heteroaryl iodides, demonstrating the potential of this protocol to serve as a general C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling method using readily available aliphatic acids as the alkylating partner. Mechanistic experiments and DFT analyses reveal that π–π stacking between the quinoline motif and the heteroaryl ring lowers the barrier for rotation of the carbon–palladium bond, favoring protodepalladation to the reductive Heck product, whereas the oxime ether ligand lacks this interaction and steers the key intermediate toward β-H elimination to give the oxidative Heck product.

title: Revisiting the Biosynthetic Cyclization of Indole Sesquiterpene Alkaloids: Proposal of a Spiro -Indolenine Pathway and Synthesis of Prelecanindole
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Indole sesquiterpene and indole diterpene alkaloids constitute a distinctive class of natural products characterized by complex polycyclic ring architectures and diverse potent biological activities. In indole sesquiterpenes, the characteristic indole-containing pentacyclic skeleton is biosynthesized from 3-farnesylindole through epoxidation followed by a sequential cationic cyclization. Although the cyclization enzyme has been identified, the details of its cyclization mechanism remain unclear. Here, we propose a new biosynthetic mechanism involving a spiro-indoleninium intermediate, which contrasts with the long-standing mechanism proposed in the 1970s that proceeds via a tertiary-to-secondary carbocation rearrangement. We demonstrated the feasibility of this new mechanism by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which do not support the conventional mechanism and also by chemical emulation: the putative spiro-indolenine intermediate was synthesized from two fragments through stereoselective cyclopropanation as a key reaction and subsequently converted to prelecanindole, a common biosynthetic intermediate of indole sesquiterpene alkaloids, under mild acidic conditions.

title: Molecular Dipole Engineering of NiO Hole Injection Layers for Suppressed Exciton Quenching and High-Performance Quantum Dot Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT), the most widely used hole injection layer (HIL) in quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs), suffers from intrinsic acidity and hygroscopicity, limiting device stability and long-term performance. To address these limitations, inorganic nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles (NPs) have emerged as a promising alternative HIL owing to their superior chemical robustness and favorable energy levels. However, the practical performance of NiO-based QLEDs remains constrained by surface defect states, including Ni3+ species and oxygen vacancies, which induce interfacial non-radiative recombination and hinder efficient hole injection. Here, we report a self-assembled monolayer (SAM)-assisted interfacial engineering strategy using 4-bromomethyl benzoic acid (4-BMBA) to passivate NiO NP surfaces and optimize the NiO/quantum dot interface. The 4-BMBA SAM simultaneously suppresses defect-mediated exciton quenching, improves energy-level alignment, and facilitates hole injection, resulting in significantly enhanced charge balance. Photoluminescence and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal suppressed non-radiative recombination and prolonged exciton lifetime, while impedance spectroscopy demonstrates reduced interfacial resistance and a lower charge injection barrier. Consequently, the optimized QLEDs exhibit a low turn-on voltage of 2.2 V, a maximum luminance of 54,660 cd m–2, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.34%, and a current efficiency (CE) of 28.89 cd A–1. These results represent one of the highest reported performances among QLEDs employing inorganic HILs for II–VI and III–V colloidal quantum dots. This work establishes SAM-mediated defect passivation as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and charge injection in inorganic HIL-based QLEDs, providing a versatile platform for next-generation high-efficiency and stable quantum dot optoelectronic devices.

title: Atomic-Scale Visualization of MnOH x Reconstruction via Hydrogen Spillover for a Poisoning-Resistant Oxidation Pathway
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen spillover offers a route to modulate oxide surface chemistry, yet how it governs the reaction pathways of oxide-catalyzed CO oxidation remains elusive. Here, we show that hydrogen spillover hydroxylates MnOx on Pt(111) to form the MnOHx overlayer, with dynamically reconstructed triangular domains. High-pressure scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that MnOHx exhibits a distinct CO oxidation pathway without carbonate accumulation at room temperature. Microscopy, spectroscopy, and theory identify bridging hydroxyls within MnOHx interior domains as the key reactive motifs that react with CO. Consistent with this mechanism, hydrogen spillover also enhances CO oxidation over MnOx/Pt nanoparticle catalysts, linking atomic-scale insight to practical catalytic performance. These findings demonstrate that tailoring hydroxyl configurations can suppress poisoning and redirect oxidation pathways, offering a strategy extendable to other low-temperature oxidation reactions.

title: 3D-Printed BiFeO3@TiO2 Heterojunctions with Post-UV Activation for Enhanced Visible-Light Photocatalytic Degradation of Acyclovir
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A method for 3D-printed photocatalytically active hybrid materials is reported. To this end, methacrylate-based resins doped with TiO2 particles decorated with BiFeO3 nanoparticles (BiFeO3 @TiO2) are developed for digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technique. Upon DLP printing, the BiFeO3 @TiO2 particles are embedded in a polymer matrix, deactivating the materials for photocatalytic processes. However, after 24 h post-print UV activation, the resin is locally decomposed, exposing the BiFeO3 @TiO2 particles and thereby activating the materials with respect to their photocatalytic performance. Comprehensive characterization (TEM–EDS, XPS, FTIR, PL, TGA, reflectance) confirms the activation of the material's surface, yielding improved charge-separation efficiency. Under 440 nm irradiation, the UV-activated monolith achieved 71% acyclovir degradation, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.050 h–1, 2.7 times higher than that of unactivated structures and 7.5 times higher than that of a 3D-printed TiO2 (P25) reference sample. The photocatalyst retained 96% of its initial activity after six consecutive 24 h photocatalytic cycles, demonstrating excellent long-term stability. This print–activate strategy provides a practical route for overcoming catalyst encapsulation in DLP-printed photocatalysts and enables reusable visible-light-active monolithic architectures for water-treatment applications.

title: Retained fuel removal from plasma-facing materials: effects of baking methods and hydrogen isotope exchange
abstract: Tungsten (W) is a prominent plasma-facing material for deuterium–tritium (D–T) fusion reactors, yet T fuel retention in W poses critical challenges to safety and operational viability. This study systematically compares three baking methods—vacuum baking, H2 gas atmosphere baking, and hydrogen (H) plasma baking—for removing D retained in W at 513 K, simulating realistic conditions for T removal in reactors. Experimental results demonstrate that D removal efficiencies reach 75% for vacuum baking after 16 h, 83% for H2 atmosphere baking after 16 h, and 99% for H plasma baking after 1 h. The superior performance of H2 atmosphere and H plasma baking is primarily driven by hydrogen isotope (HI) exchange, with efficiency strongly dependent on the concentration of H introduced into W. Higher H concentrations promote more complete exchange, leading to significantly reduced D retention. A multi-isotope Fill Level model was developed to simulate the end-to-end H plasma exchange process. The simulation reproduces the experimentally observed D removal kinetics and the emergence of HD desorption, with the D retention in good agreement with measurements. The pronounced disparity between H2 atmosphere baking and H plasma baking is fundamentally governed by the quantity of H entering W: H plasma promotes significantly greater H ingress, thereby enhancing HI exchange and resulting in a drastic reduction in D retention. This work provides both experimental validation and modeling support for HI exchange as an efficient T removal strategy.

title: A Bioinspired Thiolate-Bridged Diiron System for Functionally Replicating Hydrazine Dehydrogenase and Its Efficient Electrocatalytic Hydrazine Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrazine dehydrogenase (HDH) catalyzes the oxidation of hydrazine (N2H4) to dinitrogen (N2) as the final step of anaerobic ammonium oxidation, an essential process in closing the nitrogen cycle. Despite extensive biochemical studies, the detailed mechanism of HDH at a molecular level remains elusive. An increasing number of studies indicate that the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) is also central to direct hydrazine fuel cells. However, known electrocatalysts for HzOR are predominantly heterogeneous systems, while molecular electrocatalysts are still scarce, especially those inspired by biological HDH. This scarcity not only limits mechanistic understanding but also hinders the development of efficient and tunable catalysts. To tackle these challenging issues, we sought inspiration from the biological HDH system, wherein multiple iron-containing heme subunits cooperatively promote efficient HzOR with the assistance of surrounding sulfur-bearing cysteine residues. Integrating these key features, we selected the thiolate-bridged diiron complex [Cp*Fe(μ-SEt)(MeCN)]2[PF6]2 (1, Cp* = η5-C5Me5) for functionally replicating HDH. Treatment of 1 with N2H4 induces disproportionation to afford the active diazene (N2H2) species, which can be captured by the diiron cooperative platform to yield [Cp*Fe(μ-SEt)2(cis-μ-η1:η1-HN=NH)FeCp*][PF6] (2). In the presence of appropriate electron and proton acceptors, complex 2 undergoes a two-electron oxidation, leading to N2 release and the regeneration of 1. Remarkably, both complexes 1 and 2 serve as efficient molecular electrocatalysts for HzOR. This diiron molecular system not only achieves the functional replication of HDH involving a key N2H2 intermediate but also establishes a bioinspired design strategy for developing multimetal cooperative electrocatalysts toward efficient HzOR.

title: Immobilizing Ionomers by Strong Hydrogen Bonds for Highly Stable Industrial Water Electrolysis at 3.0 A/cm2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Raising the operating current density can effectively reduce the high cost of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), but this approach is limited by rapid electrode degradation. Our previous research identified a critical degradation mechanism in which ionomer migration blocks mass-transport channels in the anode catalyst layer (ACL). Here, we find that each sulfonate group of the ionomer forms only about half a hydrogen bond on the IrO2 surface, indicating a weak catalyst–ionomer interaction. Rather than modifying the IrO2 surface, we propose to introduce additives that provide additional adsorption sites forming stronger hydrogen bonds (SHB) with the sulfonate groups. The resulting SHB-ACL maintains a stable ionomer distribution and pore network even after aging, and exhibits a roughly four fold lower degradation rate over 2500 h at 3.0 A/cm2. Furthermore, the electrode can be readily scaled up to 600 cm2. The improvement stability is at least in part attributable to enhanced interface interaction, although preserved porosity, water/gas transport, and interparticle contacts may also contribute. These findings offer a scalable route toward durable industrial PEMWE devices.

title: Chemical defects in semiconducting polymers and their impact on reproducibility and device performance
abstract: Synthesizing semiconducting polymers often introduces structural defects, altering optoelectronic properties and directly impairing device performance. This Perspective details defect origins, evaluation methods and mitigation strategies, demonstrating how controlling structural variability resolves batch-to-batch inconsistency while unlocking novel materials design opportunities.

title: Electrochemical Allylic Carboxylation of Unactivated Alkenes with CO2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As both alkenes and CO2 are abundant and easily available feedstocks, carboxylation of alkenes with CO2 represents an attractive and sustainable strategy to synthesize value-added carboxylic acids. Despite substantial advances in carboxylation of π-bonds in alkenes, the carboxylation of C–H bonds in alkenes, which preserves the C═C bond in the synthesis of valuable unsaturated carboxylic acids, remains a longstanding challenge, particularly for unactivated alkenes owing to their intrinsically low reactivity. Herein, we report the first electrochemical allylic carboxylation of unactivated alkenes with CO2, providing a direct and selective approach to hard-to-obtain β,γ-unsaturated carboxylic acids. Moreover, this reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and applicability to late-stage diversification. Mechanistic studies indicate that the electrogenerated CO2 radical anion acts both as the carboxylation reagent and the hydrogen-atom abstraction species for the subsequent desaturation process, further uncovering the synthetic utility potential of the CO2 radical anion.

title: Tailorable deep eutectic solvents for sustainable lignocellulose refining: from platform design to value-added products
abstract: Efficient utilization of renewable carbon requires lignocellulosic biorefineries that can deconstruct plant cell walls while preserving the value of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), constructed from programmable hydrogen-bond acceptors and donors, have emerged as tunable media for lignocellulose processing. This review discusses recent progress in the rational design of DESs for lignocellulosic biorefineries, focusing on binary, ternary, hydrated, biphasic, catalytic and biocompatible systems. By regulating acidity/basicity, polarity, hydrogen-bonding ability, viscosity, water tolerance, active sites and phase behavior, DESs can selectively disrupt lignin-carbohydrate complexes, stabilize or functionalize the components, and direct the downstream transformation of the components toward bio-based chemicals and functional polymeric materials. Component-oriented valorization routes are summarized, including cellulose-derived functional materials and platform chemicals, lignin-derived aromatics and functional polymers, and hemicellulose-derived furan chemicals. Key barriers to industrial deployment are also critically examined, including high viscosity, mass-transfer limitations, solvent loss, energy-intensive recovery, feedstock heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Future opportunities are highlighted in artificial-intelligence-guided DESs discovery, novel membrane and electrodialysis DES-recovery technologies, DES-compatible chemo-biocatalysis and closed-loop process integration. Tailorable DESs are expected to evolve from empirical solvent systems into predictive, recyclable and product-oriented platforms for sustainable production of bio-based chemicals, materials and fuels.

title: Dominant role of Southeast Asian emissions in anthropogenic increases in global tropospheric ozone and southward tropical growth, 2000–2019
abstract: Widespread increases in tropospheric ozone (O3) have been reported over the past two decades, with changes in anthropogenic emissions, particularly in Asia, identified as an important driver. Here we use global model sensitivity simulations to quantify changes in global tropospheric O3 burden and associated radiative forcing (RF) attributable to anthropogenic emission changes from 2000 to 2019, and assess the contributions from different Asian regions. Changes in anthropogenic emissions increased the global tropospheric O3 burden by 12.0 ± 0.5 Tg and global mean RF by 0.030 ± 0.002 W m–2 under fixed 2015–2019 meteorological fields. The increase was larger during 2000–2010 than during 2010–2019 and occurred predominantly in the tropics. Southeast Asia was the largest regional contributor over 2000–2019, accounting for 5.7 ± 0.4 Tg of the simulated global tropospheric O3 burden increase and 0.020 ± 0.002 W m–2 of RF. During 2010–2019, the increase in tropospheric O3 burden attributable to anthropogenic emission changes was larger over 0–30°S than over 0–30°N, indicating a southward shift in the tropical response driven primarily by Southeast Asian emissions. East Asia shifted from a major positive contributor during 2000–2010 to a negative contributor during 2010–2019. These results highlight the increasing importance of anthropogenic emissions from tropical Asia in shaping the global distribution of tropospheric O3 and its climate forcing.

title: Impacts of energetic ion on the unstable spectra of kinetic ballooning modes and zonal flow generation
abstract: Global gyrokinetic particle simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between energetic ions (EIs) and kinetic ballooning modes (KBMs) across different toroidal mode number ( ) regimes, encompassing linear dispersion relations, nonlinear wave-particle interactions, and wave–wave interactions. The results demonstrate that EIs exert non-perturbative destabilizing effects on low- KBMs, while stabilizing high- KBMs through thermal ion dilution. These opposing EI effects arise from the different strengths of finite Larmor radius (FLR) and finite orbit width (FOW) effects in low- and high- regimes. Single- and multi- nonlinear simulations reveal strong wave-particle interactions between EIs and low- KBMs, resulting in higher KBM saturation levels and enhanced EI transport. Additionally, although low-density EIs have little direct influence on zonal flow (ZF), they can indirectly increase the spatial scale of ZF in multi- simulations. Since ZF is generated via the beat-driven process and its structure is determined by the pump wave, the EI effects lead to the dominance of low- KBM components, thereby increasing the spatial scale of the ZF.

title: The power of O vacancies in electrocatalysis
abstract: Non-stoichiometric oxide materials are essential to chemistry, but controlling their synthesis towards a tuneable number of unpaired electrons trapped in the oxygen vacancies remains challenging. Now, a new synthetic strategy leveraging template chemicals renders these materials available for electron-driven electrocatalytic selectivity.

title: Binuclear copper enzymes enable selective radical (pseudo)halogenation
abstract: Synthetically valuable new-to-nature reactions in copper enzymes remain largely underexploited in chemical synthesis. Now, the combination of binuclear copper enzymes and a photoredox catalyst can efficiently perform enantioselective decarboxylative (pseudo)halogenation starting from redox-active esters.

title: Comprehensive synthesis of K48/K63 ubiquitin pentamers by graph-empowered automation
abstract:
Abstract
                  Linear, branched and heterotypic ubiquitin (Ub) chains regulate essential cellular processes, yet their structural and functional analysis remains limited by the difficulty of preparing defined, homogeneous samples. Here we establish a fully automated platform for the comprehensive synthesis of all 56 K48/K63-linked Ub tetramers and pentamers, by iterative cycles of K48- or K63-specific chemoenzymatic conjugations of chemically synthesized Ub monomers bearing a fast-cleaving lysine protecting group compatible with folded proteins. A graph-based digital encoding of Ub chain topologies enabled systematic enumeration and filtering of reaction pathways, guiding the selection of synthetic routes. This computational system generates reagent maps and executable code to direct iterative deprotection and conjugation cycles on a standard, laboratory liquid-handling robot. All 14 Ub tetramers and 42 Ub pentamers were obtained with high fidelity, as validated by SDS–PAGE and mass spectrometry. This work establishes a general framework for automated protein conjugate synthesis and provides access to the complete space of K48/K63 branched ubiquitin chains.

title: Departing Pathways in Aza-Diarylethene Photoswitching: Elucidating the Role of the Central Ring Allows Reprogramming of the Photoresponse
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aza-diarylethenes (aza-DAEs) are an emerging class of molecular photoswitches that allow reversible C–N bond formation and cleavage upon irradiation. They not only show high potential as T-type photochromes but also offer exciting opportunities for the exploration of unique reactivity control. Two types of these photoswitches are currently being investigated, which differ substantially in the nature of their metastable states. While classical DAE behavior is found in perfluorinated thiazole derivatives, an unexpected zwitterion formation and concomitant aromatization is observed for nonfluorinated pyrimidine derivatives. The latter offers reversible control over intramolecular charge separation and intrinsic three-state photoswitching. Their metastable state unleashes thiolate reactivity, which can be harnessed, e.g., in photoinitiation applications for smart polymer generation. Despite this promising progress, the reason for the divergent photochemical behavior in aza-DAEs is not yet understood. Here, we show that substitution of the central five-membered ring is responsible for the different photochemical outcomes and nature of the metastable state. Furthermore, our computational results provide systematic insights into the structural factors governing the relative stability of the neutral closed-ring and zwitterionic forms. We then use this knowledge to reprogram thioazole derivatives and render them into zwitterion-forming aza-DAEs. With these results, the predictable and rational design of aza-DAEs is enabled, which can now be radically changed in their photoresponses and tailored to specific desired properties and applications.

title: Strengthening Metal–Oxygen Bonds via Ionicity–Covalency Asymmetric Connection: 4f Electronic Configuration Effect
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise control over the characteristics of metal–oxygen (M–O) bonds by regulating the electron redistribution between the metal and oxygen under perturbation conditions is crucial for maintaining the structural stability of transition-metal oxides. However, its development has always been hindered by the strong coupling between orbital hybridization and charge localization. Herein, by leveraging the strong ionicity of the Ce–O bonds in CeO2, we constructed an ionicity–covalency asymmetric bonding network, in which the ionic Ce–O is atomically coupled with the covalent M–O (M = Ni/Co). The reduced Ce–O coordination in this special structure weakens the O 2p → Ce 4f charge transfer and further elevates the ionic character of Ce–O bonds, thereby activating the reversible 4f electronic configuration transition. Critically, this configuration undergoes reversible transformation under potential fluctuation, reshaping charge redistribution within the M–O bonding motifs and then suppressing irreversible M–O bond degradation. Harnessing this mechanism enables transition-metal oxides to express a robust framework for the whole structure under repeated redox cycling. Incorporating this resulting CeO2/NiCo2O4, a large-scale alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) stack delivers significantly stable operation for over 350 h at 6 A under a 12-h intermittent experimental protocol. This finding offers a fundamental insight into the dynamic charge distribution in M–O bonds under potential perturbation for universal structural protection.

title: Stepwise Assembly of a Lavandulyl Moiety on Flavonoids Enabled by a 2″-Prenyltransferase
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lavandulylated flavonoids contain a characteristic branched C10 moiety, and the enzymatic basis underlying its biosynthesis remains poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the complete biosynthetic pathway of the lavandulylated flavonoid kurarinone from naringenin in the medicinal plant Sophora flavescens. The pathway involves four sequential steps, 8-prenylation, 2′-hydroxylation, 2″-prenylation, and 5-O-methylation, catalyzed by Sf8PT, SfF2′H, Sf2″PT, and Sf5OMT, respectively. Sf2′′PT represents the first characterized flavonoid 2′′-prenyltransferase (PT), catalyzing a second prenylation on the pre-existing prenyl side chain to complete the assembly of the branched lavandulyl moiety. The activity of Sf2″PT strictly depends on prior 2′-hydroxylation, establishing a defined order of enzymatic modifications that enables this noncanonical prenylation reaction. Ancestral sequence reconstruction and mutagenesis demonstrated that an inactive ancestral enzyme could be converted into functional 8PT or 2′′PT variants through one or seven amino acid substitutions, respectively. Collectively, this work establishes the enzymatic basis for stepwise lavandulyl moiety assembly and provides a framework for the enzymatic construction and engineering of branched prenylated natural products.

title: Synthetic Control of Quantum Phases in Organic Conductors: Molecular-Level Disorder Engineering and Pressure-Induced Superconductivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Structural randomness is a dominant factor governing electronic properties; however, the intrinsic effects of a disordered potential remain elusive due to the lack of a synthetic platform capable of introducing purely random potentials without carrier doping or altering the fundamental band structure. Here, we demonstrate the synthetic control of superconducting and insulating phases by exploiting the unique conformational flexibility of molecular conductors. Through precise thermodynamic control during crystal growth, we selectively synthesize the structurally ordered superconductor κ-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ-Br; BEDT-TTF = bis(ethylenedithio)tetrathiafulvalene) and the structurally disordered insulating polymorph, κ″-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ″-Br), possessing the exact same chemical composition. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the metastable nature of κ″-Br, showing a packing arrangement of BEDT-TTF molecules and an electronic band structure nearly identical to those of superconducting κ-Br, but featuring a disordered anion layer. Optical conductivity spectra reveal low-energy excitations without a distinct gap, indicating that the insulating behavior originates from disorder-induced carrier localization. Furthermore, κ″-Br undergoes a pressure-induced insulator–superconductor transition, in stark contrast to postsynthetic X-ray irradiation which induced irreversible structural damage. This work represents the first demonstration of synthetic control of an ordered superconductor and a disordered insulator driven solely by orientational disorder in organic conductors. Our study provides new avenues for manipulating strongly correlated electron systems and for investigating the intrinsic effects of randomness, free from carrier doping or structural perturbation of conducting layers.

title: Hydrogen-Bond Network-Assisted Ethylene and Hydrogen Photosynthesis from Methane over Isolated Ir Active Sites under Ambient Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Direct conversion of methane to ethylene (DCM) is an attractive yet formidable challenge due to the difficult C–H activation and uncontrollable C–C coupling process. Herein, we report a hydrogen-bond network-assisted ethylene and H2 photosynthesis from methane over oxygen-vacancy-enriched TiO2-supported single Ir atoms (Ir1/TiO2–Ov) under ambient conditions. The Ir-induced lattice distortion drives spontaneous hydrolysis under humid conditions, generating a hydroxylated surface that endows coordinatively unsaturated Ir sites to activate the first methane molecule without light irradiation. Upon photoexcitation, surface hydroxyls are oxidized into dangling oxygen species (*O) on Ti sites, which promote the dehydrogenation of *CH3 to *CH2. In synergy with the Ir site, the adjacent *O species activate a second CH4 molecule and finally direct selective C–C coupling to form C2H4. Meanwhile, methane-derived protons migrate through the hydrogen-bond network via a Grotthuss mechanism to produce H2. The Ir1/TiO2–Ov catalyst achieves the production of ethylene (14.3 ± 0.7 μmol•gcat–1•h–1) and H2 (28.4 ± 1.2 μmol•gcat–1•h–1) for at least 210 h at 25 °C and atmospheric pressure under light irradiation. Our findings establish a hydrogen-bond network-assisted strategy for methane C–H activation and selective C–C and H–H coupling.

title: Impact of helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts on magnetohydrodynamic mixed convection in a liquid metal blanket
abstract: On the pathway toward full simulations for a liquid metal blanket, this study extends the work of Chen et al (2022 Nucl. Fusion62 026042) on mixed convection in a full-scale dual coolant lead lithium blanket by considering a more realistic case. In this study, the model incorporates the complex geometry of characteristic sub-components, including helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts (FCIs), to investigate their impacts in several key metrics: (1) Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) pressure drop, (2) electromagnetic coupling, (3) velocity distribution in both the bulk and gap regions, (4) flow behavior in blanket components, and (5) heat transfer. Based on the MHD-UCAS platform, these multi-region, multiphysics direct numerical simulations are performed on a highly refined mesh of cells under conditions relevant to the fusion reactor: the applied magnetic field of 5 T ( ), the PbLi velocity of 0.1 m s–1 in poloidal ducts ( ), and maximum volumetric heating of 30 MW m–3 ( ). The computational results incorporate the influence of the helium cooling channels and the FCIs on electromagnetic coupling, thereby altering the MHD pressure and flow distribution. Simultaneously, the FCIs divide the flow into bulk and gap regions, where localized reverse flow is observed mainly within the gap regions of the rear poloidal ducts. The anisotropic conductivity introduced by helium channels alters the velocity and temperature distributions, further complicating the MHD flow. In addition, localized hot spots exceeding the design temperature limit are found near the top of the U-turn and in the outlet reduced activation ferritic/martensitic steel walls, suggesting that enhanced cooling is required in these locations.

title: Transport due to density gradient driven TEM & UM in advanced tokamak plasma configurations: role of negative triangularity and magnetic shear reversal
abstract: Advanced tokamak configurations can modify microturbulence through changes in magnetic equilibrium, trapped-particle dynamics, resonance conditions. In this work, global gyrokinetic simulations are used to study density-gradient-driven trapped-electron turbulence in tight-aspect-ratio shaped plasmas, focusing on the role of negative triangularity and reversed magnetic shear. In the positive versus negative triangularity comparison, negative triangularity is found to stabilize high- modes and reduce saturated particle diffusivity by approximately . Energy-exchange diagnostics show that this reduction is associated with a weaker participation of weakly trapped electrons, while zonal-flow shearing remains comparable between the two configurations. In the reversed-shear case for positive triangularity, despite larger linear growth rates, the saturated electron diffusivity is reduced by approximately as compared to positive magnetic shear case. This reduction is attributed to the diminished radial support of the perturbation in the reversed magnetic shear region. The combined effect of reversed magnetic shear and negative triangularity is further investigated, revealing that although both independently reduce saturated transport levels, their combination leads to enhanced nonlinear transport.

title: Grain boundary effects on surface modifications of tungsten under fusion-relevant helium plasma irradiation: coarse-grained vs nano-grained microstructures
abstract: Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ∼600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.

title: Polymerizable ionic buffers transform grain boundaries into ion-regulating interfaces in metal halide perovskites
abstract: A polymerizable ionic buffer suppresses ion migration at perovskite grain boundaries through chemical stabilization and physical confinement.

title: Anode-free configurations through separator-mediated interfacial regulation for practical sodium metal batteries
abstract: Functionally engineered separators regulate Na + transport and interfacial chemistry. They homogenize ion flux, stabilize the SEI, and suppress dendrites to improve reversibility, especially in anode-free sodium metal batteries.

title: Reversible liquid-phase lithium transfer across the battery lifecycle
abstract: This Review highlights lithium–arene complexes (LACs) as versatile liquid lithium sources and establishes the PAH/LAC pair as a reversible lithium carrier, enabling lithium extraction and donation across the battery lifecycle.

title: Multi-Anion Competitive Solvation: Unlocking Wide-Temperature Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) promise high energy density and low cost but suffer from irreversible sodium loss, particularly under extreme temperatures where sluggish desolvation kinetics and unstable interfacial chemistry...

title: Being a good scientist in a fast-evolving era
abstract: Science is becoming faster, more crowded, and increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence (AI) and automated experimentation. These developments expand what researchers can attempt, but they also intensify pressure to publish...

title: Experimental and numerical investigation of backstreaming positive ions in an RF-driven negative ion source
abstract: Backstreaming positive ions (BSPIs) are an unavoidable byproduct in high-power negative ion-based neutral beam injection systems, posing a critical challenge to the long-pulse operational stability of ion sources due to the significant heat loads and material erosion they induce. This paper presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation into the generation, spatial distribution, and thermal effects of BSPIs in the dual-radio-frequency (RF)-driver negative ion source at the HONOR test facility of CRAFT. Using a water-flow calorimetry diagnostic system, the dependence of the BSPI power fraction (PBSPI/Pbeam) on key operational parameters was systematically studied. The results show that the PBSPI/Pbeam ratio increases monotonically with the source filling pressure, rising from ∼2.05% at 0.3 Pa to ∼3.15% at 0.57 Pa. A non-monotonic dependence on beam energy is observed, with the ratio peaking at ∼2.65% at 161 keV. This trend is attributed to the competition between the improved geometric transmission efficiency of BSPIs—resulting from reduced beam divergence at moderate energies—and the intrinsic decrease in collision cross-sections at higher energies. Furthermore, the ratio is found to decrease with increasing extracted beam current, which is explained by the space-charge-induced beam divergence that reduces the geometric transmission efficiency through the acceleration grids. Distinct BSPI bombardment traces on the backplate exhibit an array pattern corresponding to the plasma grid apertures. Coupled thermal-fluid-solid simulations, incorporating the measured heat loads, indicate that under typical high-power conditions (190 kV, 16.2 A), the maximum backplate temperature remains well below the material safety limit. This work clarifies the key mechanisms governing BSPI generation and validates the thermal reliability of the backplate design, providing a solid basis for the development of high-power negative-ion-based neutral beam injection (NNBI) systems.

title: Confinement property in the JT-60SA first operation phase
abstract: In JT-60SA, the global energy confinement time has been evaluated to be – s for 1 MA hydrogen discharges and compared with the ITERL-96P(th) scaling. Because local measurements of ion temperature , electron density and effective charge are not available in the first operation phase and the number of discharges and their parameter range are limited, the present results should not be considered definitive. As heating power increased, tends to shorten in the same trend as the scaling. is shorter than the scaling but approaches the scaling with increasing density. For 0.4–0.6 MW ohmic heating plasmas, increases with increasing collisionality and saturates. For 0.6–0.8 MW ohmic heating and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECH) plasmas, continues to increase up to higher collisionality and reaches the scaling. The turbulence simulations with the trapped gyroLandau-fluid model assuming a linear profile show that the dominant turbulence mode is trapped electron modes. The linear growth rate decreases with increasing collisionality and saturates at a low level in the 0.4–0.6 MW ohmic heating plasma, suggesting the transition from the linear ohmic confinement regime to the saturated ohmic confinement regime. For 0.6–0.8 MW ohmic heating and ECH plasmas, the saturation occurs at higher collisionality, indicating that the linear confinement regime extends to higher collisionality. The global particle confinement time excluding recycling contributions, , has also been evaluated to be s, approximately twice , from the frequency responses in a density feedback control experiment. From and the effective particle confinement time including recycling , a recycling coefficient is obtained as . The sub-unity recycling coefficient indicates that wall recycling is insufficient to maintain plasma density, consistent with hydrogen retention due to the first hydrogen discharge with continuous gas injection.

title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: Sustained changes to urban mobility after COVID-19 reinforced socioeconomic inequalities in Argentina, Chile and Colombia
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Urban mobility is central to economic activity, social inclusion and access to services. COVID-19 caused disruptions to mobility globally, yet its long-term impacts in Latin America remain poorly understood. Using > 170 million anonymised and aggregated location records from Meta-Facebook users in Argentina, Chile and Colombia (April 2020-May 2022), we examine changes in overall mobility volume relative to pre-pandemic baselines across socioeconomic and rural-urban gradients. Two years after the pandemic onset, mobility in the highest-density urban cores remained ~ 25–50% below baseline across the three countries, while the top 33% most affluent communities had not returned to baseline. These differences are explained by the scale of the initial mobility shock rather than by subsequent recovery rates. Our findings reveal how a global shock can entrench disparities in human mobility, with implications for urban resilience and planning in unequal nations. Our study underscores the need for proactive policies to prevent long-lasting mobility inequalities.

title: Orangutans face bleak future after Indonesia’s devastating wildfires
abstract: The super El Niño intensified Indonesian fires, which ravaged the habitat of the critically endangered Bornean orangutan.

title: Programming Sodium-Storage Kinetics through Linear Quinone Oligomerization
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quinone-based organic cathodes enable reversible multielectron redox reactions but suffer from dissolution and sluggish sodium-storage kinetics. Here, two structurally homologous linear quinone oligomers, biphenyl–quinone dimer (2BQ) and terphenyl–quinone trimer (3BQ), are compared to elucidate how backbone extension regulates sodium storage. Compared with 2BQ, 3BQ exhibits reduced crystallinity, enhanced electrochemical utilization, a narrower HOMO–LUMO gap, and lower oxidation reorganization energy. Consequently, 3BQ delivers a reversible capacity of 350 mA h g–1 at 0.05C and retains 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 1C, with enhanced rate capability and cycling stability. Operando FTIR and state-dependent XPS reveal reversible C=O/C–O–Na conversion, while density functional theory calculations elucidate an extended multielectron sodiation sequence. These findings establish controlled linear quinone oligomerization as an effective, rational molecular design strategy to reduce apparent dissolution tendency and improve carbonyl-site utilization and sodium-storage kinetics, providing insights into the development of advanced organic cathodes for rechargeable sodium-ion batteries.

title: Liquid Metal Interlayers Enable Zero-Pressure Sulfide Solid Electrolyte Lithium Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal anodes are essential for high-energy-density batteries with solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but the lithium-SSE interface suffers from contact loss and current constriction during cycling. External stack pressure can enhance contact retention but adds system-level limitations and accelerates lithium filament penetration. Here, a room-temperature liquid sodium–potassium (NaK) interlayer is demonstrated to stabilize the lithium–sulfide SSE interface under nominally zero stack pressure by combining stress-free morphological adaptability with Li transport capability. In situ X-ray computed tomography and other analytical methods reveal that the liquid layer reconfigures to preserve interfacial contact during Li plating/stripping. Finite Li solubility in the NaK also creates a dissolved-Li-mediated electrochemical pathway that supports Li stripping from a distant reservoir. The dual mechanical and transport functions of NaK enable stable full-cell cycling (600 cycles, >2 mAh cm–2) with layered-oxide composite cathodes under nominally zero applied stack pressure. These findings highlight a fundamental interfacial design concept based on a compliant interlayer that accommodates morphological evolution while supporting Li transport under minimal mechanical confinement.

title: Targeting chemotherapy-induced CD200 via a nucleoside-enhanced nanocarrier for cancer immunochemotherapy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, yet its efficacy is frequently undermined by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In addition, the immune-related toxicities restrict combination therapy targeting several immune checkpoints. Here, we identify chemotherapy-induced CD200 upregulation as a stress-adaptive resistance mechanism that reinforces tumor immune evasion under treatment pressure. Leveraging a tumor-restricted, nucleoside-enhanced nanocarrier, we achieve spatially selective silencing of tumor-intrinsic CD200, thereby reprogramming the tumor immune microenvironment, enhancing antitumor efficacy, and enabling effective combination with PD-1 blockade. Importantly, this strategy minimizes the colitis exacerbation associated with systemic CD200/PD-1 dual blockade in a DSS-induced susceptibility model, suggesting its potential to preserve immune homeostasis while reducing immune-related toxicity. Together, our findings establish CD200 as a context-dependent immune resistance node and demonstrate a nanotechnology-based framework for precise and safe immune checkpoint modulation.

title: Disagreements in global urban growth projections amplify uncertainties in deforestation and carbon emissions
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global urbanization is profoundly reshaping 21st-century land systems, yet its future trajectory remains highly uncertain. Existing projections exhibit divergent urban growth patterns even under identical socioeconomic scenarios. Here, by synthesizing six urban growth projections, we reveal substantial disagreements in the extent and location of urban growth by 2100. These disagreements are amplified by land-system feedbacks, driving cross-dataset variation in urban-induced deforestation (1.75–4.91 million km2) through direct forest conversion and indirect cropland displacement, assuming lost production is compensated by cropland expansion elsewhere. The associated emissions exhibit an absolute range of 29 to 76 GtCO2 by 2100. Across 100 countries, this range accounts for an average of 3% of unconditional Nationally Determined Contribution emission budgets, reaching 26% in specific countries. Our findings establish cross-dataset disagreement as an important source of uncertainty in land and climate assessments, highlighting the need for robust spatial planning across plausible urban futures.

title: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma is a lethal pediatric brainstem cancer with few effective treatments. Here, we integrate metabolomic, transcriptomic, chromatin, genetic and in vivo analyses to identify a purine-metabolic dependency associated with the H3K27M histone mutation. The histone H3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitution increases Nuclear Factor I transcriptional activity, which promotes coordinated expression of enzymes involved in purine biosynthesis and degradation, including 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase/inosine monophosphate cyclohydrolase and purine nucleoside phosphorylase. Sustained purine degradation limits feedback inhibition of purine synthesis, enabling continued purine production, utilization and catabolism. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of the terminal de novo purine biosynthesis enzyme reduces tumor-cell fitness, slows orthotopic tumor progression and extends survival in mice. These results connect histone-mutation-associated chromatin remodeling to a Nuclear Factor I-regulated, therapeutically targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma.

title: Dynamic B–OH intermediates enable photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into formic acid
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Remediating of flue gas pollutants and the mitigation of carbon emissions represent two interconnected yet often conflicting challenges in environmental management. Here we report a borane-assisted photocatalytic system that achieves synergistic co-conversion of CO2, NOx, and SO2 from flue gas into valuable liquid products-formic, nitric, and sulfuric acids-with near-complete selectivity and high stability. Central to this process is the in situ generation of dynamic B-OH intermediates at the borane-catalyst interface, which serve as proton relays to activate water-derived protons for CO2 reduction while promoting reactive oxygen species for pollutant oxidation. This mechanism enables approximately 77.02% of the hydrogen in formic acid to originate from water. The system demonstrates broad applicability across diverse photocatalysts and borane reagents, and exhibits sustained performance under simulated flue gas conditions. Our work establishes a sustainable and economically viable pathway for integrated carbon and pollutant valorization, offering a scalable strategy toward circular carbon economies.

title: Choline kinase α promotes glycolysis and tumor growth by phosphorylating and activating enolase 1
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tumor cells exhibit aberrantly upregulated glycolysis, in which glycolytic enzyme enolase 1 (ENO1) plays a critical role. However, how ENO1 activity is dynamically regulated in tumor cells remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that hypoxic stimulation promotes the binding of p38 MAP kinase to choline kinase α (CHKα). p38 phosphorylates CHKα at S114, subsequently leading to CHKα to interact with ENO1. Importantly, CHKα functions as a protein kinase and phosphorylates ENO1 Y44 thereby enhancing the metabolic activity of ENO1 to increase glycolysis. Knock-in expression of CHKα S114A or ENO1 Y44F inhibits brain tumor cell glycolysis and proliferation, blunts brain tumor growth in mice with inhibited lactate production, and prolongs mouse survival. In addition, CHKα S114 and ENO1 Y44 phosphorylation levels are positively correlated with each other and associated with poor prognosis in glioblastoma patients. These findings highlight the critical regulation of glycolysis by the noncanonical function of CHKα and underscore the potential to target the moonlighting function of CHKα for cancer treatment.

title: A quasi-particle theory for the dynamics of polycatenated architected materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Architected materials derive unusual mechanical responses from geometry rather than mostly by their chemistry. Polycatenated architected materials (PAMs), composed of interlinked rigid units, have been shown to display hybrid solid–fluid behaviors. Frequency-sweep rheological experiments have revealed a transition from strong shear thinning at low frequencies to pronounced shear thickening above a critical frequency. Because neighboring PAM units are connected, rather than freely rearranging, conventional granular theories do not readily explain their behavior. Here, we develop a one-dimensional analytical model to capture the frequency-response of PAMs based on a quasi-particle description. Quasi-particles are defined as segments of PAMs that are either fully stretched or fully compressed. Modeling their interactions produces an effective viscosity that captures both asymptotic scaling laws and the critical frequency. These predictions agree quantitatively with simulations and experiments. Our results reveal that PAM’s frequency-dependent response arises from competing effects between dissipation and inertia. More broadly, our results establish an analytical foundation for understanding the dynamics of PAMs and provide design principles for tuning their responses.

title: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plant cells are encased in cell walls and are usually thought to behave like stiff, pressurized vessels. When the cell wall is digested, plant protoplasts form spherical shapes, further consolidating this model. Here we show that plant protoplasts can form phytopodia. More precisely, using plasma membrane markers, we reveal that 27 ± 1% of protoplasts from Arabidopsis seedlings show dot-like protrusions and 16 ± 7% of protoplasts show long (typically 1-20 μm, up to 200 μm) protrusions, hence the name “phytopodia”. We demonstrate that this behavior is independent of the plant species, the membrane marker or the osmolyte. Phytopodia can host microtubule bundles, which in turn can impact their shape. Actin is not required for the presence of phytopodia, and consistently, the movement of phytopodia is passive. Phytopodia can form de novo when increasing osmolarity and they can attach to artificial surfaces. Altogether, this calls for revisiting the dynamics and probing ability of the plant cell cortex in different osmotic and mechanical environments.

title: A bacteriocin from the commensal Streptococcus mitis prevents influenza infection-driven pneumococcal lung dissemination
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major public health threat despite widespread use of vaccines and antibiotics. Its synergy with influenza A virus (IAV) often leads to secondary bacterial pneumonia, causing significant morbidity and mortality mainly in vulnerable populations such as children under 5 years old and adults over 65 years old. As pneumococcal pneumonia is preceded by nasopharyngeal colonization, preventing colonization represents a promising intervention strategy. While current interventions are somewhat effective, their impact is limited by serotype replacement and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show that colonization with the commensal S. mitis strain F22Ad significantly reduces pneumococcal density in the nasopharynx by day 10 post-infection and prevents dissemination to the lungs following IAV infection. This protective effect depends on bacteriocins encoded at the blp1 locus. Among these, Bac2v1 alone or in combination with Bac1 significantly reduces pneumococcal colonization. Notably, Bac2v1 exerts broad, serotype-independent inhibitory activity, impairing the growth of diverse epidemiologically relevant pneumococcal strains. These findings establish two precision-based, serotype-independent approaches to target pneumococcal colonization: using S. mitis F22Ad as a live biotherapeutic or administering a bacteriocin mixture produced by this strain. Both approaches have the potential to prevent pneumococcal disease and complement existing strategies.

title: The nature of the phase transition in VO2 B-phase and a quantum entanglement perspective
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The well-known metal-to-insulator transition in rutile/monoclinic VO2 has been understood as a correlation-enhanced Peierls phenomenon. The lesser-known B-polymorph exhibits a similar resistivity jump, assumed to arise from an analogous transition. However, unlike rutile/monoclinic VO2, here the transition is isostructural, with dimers persisting both above and below the transition, challenging established interpretations. Here, we show that the phase transition in the B-polymorph is qualitatively different. Despite high conductivity and finite spectral weight at the chemical potential, the high-temperature phase lacks standard metallic screening and Drude peaks. Our theoretical analysis reveals that while the low-temperature insulating phase is driven by both Peierls and Mott physics, the high-temperature state is an anomalous insulator whose apparent metallicity arises from incoherent in-gap states that mimic a metal. We relate this unusual growth of incoherent states to temperature-dependent intra-dimer charge transfers. Finally, we propose a unified framework using an Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-like quantum-entanglement measure to characterize and distinguish between different VO2 phases hosting dimers.

title: Learning beyond rigid manipulation with hybrid soft-rigid robots
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rigid-soft robot hybrids promise to unite the precision and repeatability of rigid manipulators with the compliance and adaptability of soft structures. Yet, full-fledged rigid-soft manipulators remain largely unexplored, in part because the intelligence required to exploit this combination is still missing. Here, we introduce a hybrid robotic system obtained by the series interconnection of a rigid arm and a soft manipulator, and systematically examine its ability to perform both established and previously inaccessible manipulation tasks. We show that a tailored imitation learning algorithm–generally applicable to this class of hybrid systems–leverages the complementary roles of rigid precision and soft embodiment to acquire manipulation skills and generalize them in a single shot across task variations. As a result, the system matches or exceeds the performance of rigid robots in classical tasks such as stacking, while enabling qualitatively new behaviors, including grasping objects through narrow openings.

title: Impact-stiffening materials modulated by host–guest interactions in polypseudorotaxanes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The development of high-performance impact-stiffening materials is critical for applications spanning personal protection to military defense. Conventional designs of such materials relying on strong noncovalent interactions often face a strength–toughness trade‑off. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a strategy that utilizes the dynamic threading–dethreading kinetics of host–guest complexes in polypseudorotaxanes to fabricate impact‑stiffening materials. Unlike binding‑strength‑governed designs, this approach is governed by kinetic mismatch between the dethreading time of the macrocycle and the external deformation time. This kinetic control decouples the static compliance from the dynamic stiffening threshold, enabling pronounced impact‑stiffening even with a modest solution‑phase binding constant. Under low shear rates, the macrocycles gradually slide from the polymer backbone, preserving flexibility. Upon high-speed impact, the dethreading of host–guest complexes cannot occur within the ultrashort loading window of deformation, kinetically freezing the network and increasing the storage modulus by 48‑fold (0.1–100 Hz, 25 °C). The material also exhibits self-healing, reprocessability, and strong adhesion. This work demonstrates rate-dependent host–guest disassembly as a design principle for adaptive impact-protective materials.

title: Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing
abstract: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. Percolation in a thin platinum interfacial layer and grain boundaries in a polycrystalline hafnium oxide matrix spatially confine active metal-ion migration; this guided transport substantially improves device uniformity. Purpose-designed programming protocols enable tuning of relaxation time over two orders of magnitude. A prototype hardware system integrating a 28 × 14 array of tailored diffusive memristors and a memristive system-on-chip implements the hierarchy-of-time-surfaces algorithm, achieving 91.14% recognition accuracy on a downsampled neuromorphic-MNIST dataset. These results demonstrate a scalable approach towards robust and energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware for next-generation artificial intelligence.

title: Daily briefing: A guide to the Riemann hypothesis
abstract: Get to grips with the famed conjecture, and hear mathematicians’ reactions to its proofs. Plus, the benefits of eating with other people.

title: Coupled hydrogen spillover and CO2 activation sites in high-entropy catalysts for CO2 reduction
abstract: Converting CO2 into useful chemicals via reverse water-gas shift reaction offers a promising route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, catalysts often struggle to coordinate hydrogen and CO2 activation while remaining stable under demanding reaction conditions. The present work developed high-entropy oxides with Li and Al dual-atom doping to promote cooperative alloy-oxide interfaces with coupled H2 and CO2 activation sites, thereby enabling fast, selective, and stable CO production. These findings provide a general strategy for integrating multiple functions into robust catalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Extending frequency metrology to increasingly complex molecules: SI-traceable sub-Doppler mid-IR spectroscopy of trioxane
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bringing increasingly complex polyatomic molecules within reach of precision measurement experiments opens new prospects ranging from Earth sciences and astrophysics, to metrology and quantum sciences. Here, we demonstrate sub-Doppler mid-IR spectroscopic measurements of, to our knowledge, the largest molecule to date, 1,3,5-trioxane, (H2CO)3, in its ν5 CO stretching mode. To this end, we use an ultra-high-resolution ~10.3 µm spectrometer based on a sub-Hz quantum cascade laser remotely calibrated against state-of-the-art primary frequency standards via a metrology-grade fibre link. We perform saturated absorption spectroscopy at low pressure with ~100 kHz resolution. This allows measuring the absolute frequency of hundreds of rovibrational transitions at unprecedented statistical and systematic uncertainties for such a complex species, as low as 4.6 kHz and 6.2 kHz respectively. In addition to providing new spectroscopic information on trioxane, our work extends frequency metrology methodologies to ever larger molecular systems, confirming the potential of our technologies for bringing increasingly complex species within reach of ultra-precise measurement experiments.

title: Chromosome ‘glue’ could boost fertility by stabilizing ageing eggs
abstract: A system tested in mice mimics a protein that declines with age and could help to improve fertility treatments in future.

title: Hybrid simulations of nonlinear zonal flow generation by multi- n toroidal Alfvén eigenmo...
abstract: In burning plasmas, zonal flows (ZFs) excited by toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) play a crucial role in improving energy confinement.
