title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

title: Covalent–Ionic Bonding Regulation Enables Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of High‐Voltage O3‐Type Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Ni–Fe–Mn‐based O3‐type layered oxides are attractive cathode materials for sodium‐ion batteries, but their high‐voltage operation suffers from the coupling between phase transitions and lattice oxygen instability. In this work, guided by hard and soft acids and bases (HSAB) theory, we propose a covalent–ionic dual‐pathway decoupling strategy to stabilize high‐voltage O3‐type layered cathodes. The incorporation of Mg, Ti, and F constructs a rigid architecture in which a covalent Ti─O framework reinforces the transition‐metal octahedral skeleton to suppress detrimental phase transitions, while localized Mg─F ionic coordination stabilizes lattice oxygen through localized electrostatic anchoring to mitigate irreversible oxygen release. Through multiscale structural and spectroscopic analyses, we verify that this bonding regulation suppresses the O3→P3→OP2 multiphase evolution and lattice oxygen escape. The modified cathode maintains 76.32% capacity retention over 400 cycles at 1 C and exhibits robust cyclability across −10°C to 50°C; the assembled full cells achieve a reversible capacity of 166.27 mAh g −1 with an energy density of 330.22 Wh kg −1 at 0.1 C, and an initial capacity of 143.74 mAh g −1 with 72.06% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C. This work demonstrates a bonding‐regulation paradigm that decouples chemo‐mechanical degradation in high‐energy‐density layered oxide cathodes.

title: Synergistic Water‐Deficient Inner Helmholtz Plane and Asymmetric Dual‐Site Nonmetal Catalysts Enable Stable Ah‐Level Aqueous Zn–I2 Batteries at Elevated Temperatures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT At elevated temperatures, intensified water‐induced side reactions and iodine dissolution severely hinder the development of aqueous zinc–iodine batteries. Herein, a marginally hydrophilic and conductive modification layer with a hexagonal layered structure is constructed to stabilize the anode interface. This approach establishes a water‐deficient inner Helmholtz plane and reduces the fraction of weak hydrogen bonds, thereby suppressing spontaneous Zn dissolution and water decomposition. Concurrently, interfacial electronic structure regulation increases the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction and promotes uniform Zn deposition along the Zn‐(002) crystal plane, effectively inhibiting dendrite growth. These effects are corroborated by theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations. Furthermore, asymmetric dual‐site nonmetal single‐atom–cluster structures are introduced into the cathode host to enhance iodine adsorption and accelerate conversion kinetics, thereby mitigating iodine dissolution. Benefiting from this synergistic design, the assembled coin‐type battery delivers a discharge capacity of 95 mAh g −1 after 60 000 cycles at 8 A g −1 . A sub‐ampere‐hour‐level plastic‐cased battery employing a high‐loading cathode with a theoretical areal‐capacity of 5.6 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates strong practical potential by maintaining excellent cycling stability at 3 C and at 50°C. An Ah‐level pouch battery also exhibits stable operation at 50°C.

title: Interface Engineering to Unlock Multi‐Electron Sn+/S2− Redox Reaction and High Lithium Anode Utilization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) offer high theoretical energy density, yet their practical viability is impeded by sluggish cathodic redox kinetics and uncontrolled anodic dendrite growth. Here, we address these challenges by a dual‐interface engineering strategy that exploits halogen anion migration to in situ construct phase‐separated localized electrochemical microreactors (LEMRs) at both electrodes. At the cathode, an in situ‐formed Li 6 PS 5 Cl/LiCl/Li 2 S‐LiI internal LEMR activates the S 2− /S n+ ( n ≥1) multi‐electron redox reaction beyond the conventional S 2− /S 0 redox reaction while maintaining structural integrity. Concurrently, at the Li anode, an interfacial LiCl/C@LiI/LiCl‐LiI anode LEMR confines Li plating/stripping within the LEMR to suppress lithium dendrites. This dual‐LEMR architecture enables the optimized cells to deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 450 cycles at 3.6 mAh cm −2 and 80% after 70 cycles at a high areal capacity of 7.5 mAh cm −2 under a low N/P ratio of 0.78, and to achieve an ultra‐high areal capacity of 32.8 mAh cm −2 . This work highlights the potential of anion chemistry as an effective interface engineering strategy to overcome the kinetics and stability limits of all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, and provides a versatile framework for advancing high‐energy ASSLSBs.

title: Antigen‐Presenting Microrobots Program CAR‐T Cell Function
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical forces are emerging as key regulators of T‐cell function, yet how active motion‐ derived mechanical cues from artificial antigen‐presenting cells (aAPCs) influence T‐cell activation and fate remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop self‐propelled antigen‐presenting microrobots (CytoBots)—gas‐driven magnesium microparticles functionalized with anti‐CD3 and anti‐CD28 antibodies—that actively navigate suspension environments and mechanically engage T cells. Unlike immotile aAPCs, CytoBots generate motion‐dependent, force‐bearing stimulation that enhances T‐cell activation. Single‐cell force spectroscopy shows that CytoBots double receptor–ligand binding strength and extend bond lifetime threefold, supporting a role for motion‐enhanced mechanical interactions in T‐cell activation. CytoBot stimulation is associated with enhanced proximal T‐cell signaling, increased phosphorylation of AKT and mTOR, and metabolic changes characterized by elevated mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis‐associated activity. These responses accompany the enrichment of stem‐like and central memory T‐cell populations. In humanized tumor models, CytoBot‐expanded CAR‐T cells exhibit superior cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy. These findings establish microrobotic antigen‐presenting interfaces as a generalizable strategy for programming immune cell function through dynamic mechanotransduction, opening new opportunities for next‐generation cell therapies.

title: Electron Bridge Effect Enhanced Tandem Catalysis for Efficient Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) offers a promising route for wastewater remediation and ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis under mild conditions. However, the activity of NO 3 RR is hindered by the high activation barrier of nitrate (NO 3 − ), as well as the low generation efficiency and restricted migration of active hydrogen (H ads ). The development of electrocatalysts that combine efficient synergistic active sites, rapid electron transfer, and unimpeded H ads migration pathways is crucial for enhancing NO 3 RR performance. Here, we report a molten salt etching strategy to successfully prepare a ternary metal boride MoCoB electrocatalyst. In this catalyst, Mo site can efficiently adsorb and activate NO 3 − , while Co site is responsible for H 2 O dissociation and H ads supply. Meanwhile, B site builds an electronic bridge to enhance the electron transfer and proton migration between Mo and Co sites. Benefiting from the synergistic mechanism of electron bridge effect‐enhanced tandem catalysis, MoCoB achieves an NH 3 yield rate of 61.89 mg h −1 mg cat −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 98.73%. Furthermore, a Zn‐NO 3 − /ethanol hybrid battery assembled with MoCoB cathode demonstrates high power density and durable long‐term cycling stability, and the production of high‐value ammonium acetate. This work provides guidance for designing efficient NO 3 RR electrocatalysts and offers insights into reversible zinc‐based battery.

title: Low‐Temperature‐Locked Crystallization Enables Stress‐Relaxed Antimony Selenide Thin‐Film Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Absorber quality is critical to the performance of thin‐film photovoltaics, particularly for antimony selenide (Sb 2 Se 3 ). Due to its quasi‐one‐dimensional crystal structure, the migration, rearrangement, and orientation evolution of Sb 2 Se 3 chains play a pivotal role in determining crystallization and microstructural behavior. However, rapid heating (as with conventional thermal annealing) typically induces competitive chain orientation and nonuniform stress relaxation. This results in defect generation, orientational disorder, and complex crystallization pathways that severely constrain device performance. To address these issues, we propose a low‐temperature pretreatment to precisely regulate the crystallization kinetics of Sb 2 Se 3 absorbers. Low‐temperature pretreatment applied to amorphous Sb 2 Se 3 films prior to annealing effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and structural disordering, while preserving short‐range ordered chain segments as structural motifs for subsequent crystallization. During the subsequent annealing process, progressive stress relaxation facilitates chain reorientation and crystal reconstruction, thereby influencing local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, promoting grain growth, and enhancing preferential orientation. This progressive ‘low‐temperature‐locking stress‐relaxation‐oriented reconstruction’ process markedly reduces residual stress and defect density, while improving charge transport and suppressing non‐radiative carrier recombination. As a result, our pretreated device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 9.78%. This strategy offers a general route to fabricating high‐quality, low‐stress, low‐defect chalcogenide films for efficient and stable photovoltaics.

title: SEI Evolution on Siloxene Anodes in Solid and Liquid Electrolytes via an Ion‐Sieving/Electron‐Conducting Interfacial Layer
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes suffer from severe volume expansion and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which limit their use in both liquid and solid‐state batteries. Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based LP@SONS, is constructed by anchoring polypyrrole nanoparticles and lithiated‐Nafion onto siloxene nanosheets. This architecture combines electron‐conducting pathways with a Li + ‐selective ion‐sieving layer, homogenizing Li + flux, restricting anion/solvent penetration, and buffering strain. The stable and compositionally identical platform enables direct comparison of SEI evolution in liquid and solid electrolytes. In liquid cells, the SEI grows in a bulk‐permeated (3D) manner, whereas solid electrolytes confine growth to a planar solid–solid contact, yielding a LiF‐rich, planar‐confined (2D) SEI that passivates rapidly. Remarkably, LP@SONS promotes thinner, more uniform, LiF‐rich interphases in both systems. As a result, it delivers high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling in liquid and solid‐state batteries, with only ∼5% thickness expansion after 100 cycles. This work clarifies how electrolyte contact geometry governs SEI dimensionality and offers an interfacial engineering strategy for high‐capacity anodes.

title: Single‐Atom Based Dual‐Metal‐Active‐Site Catalysts for N2 Conversion to Ammonia and Urea Synthesis: Geometric Coupling, Electronic Polarization, Reaction Partitioning, and Intermediate Steering
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT N 2 conversion is increasingly recognized not as a simple activation process of an inert molecule, but as a coupled reaction network that requires synchronized N 2 adsorption, electron/proton transfer, intermediate hydrogenation, C─N coupling, product release, and side‐reaction suppression. Single‐atom catalysts provide atomic precision, well‐defined coordination environments, and tunable electronic structures, but their isolated active centers often struggle to satisfy the multiple and sometimes conflicting requirements of complex N 2 conversion. Single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts are therefore emerging as cooperative catalytic architectures that integrate an atomically dispersed metal single atom with a second metal site in the form of an isolated atom, cluster, or nanoparticle. This review establishes a structure‐function framework for understanding these catalysts, focusing on dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. Recent advances in ammonia and urea synthesis are discussed to reveal how dual sites regulate N 2 activation, proton supply, intermediate evolution, and selective C─N bond formation. Particular attention is given to metal‐metal interactions, support‐mediated charge redistribution, hydrogen transfer, and pathway‐dependent intermediate binding. Finally, key challenges, including precise dual‐site construction, quantitative synergy identification, and practical compatibility, are highlighted to guide the rational design of next‐generation dual‐site catalysts for sustainable N 2 conversion.

title: Dark Horse Absorbers for Indoor Photovoltaics: Toward Cheaper, Safer, and More Stable Alternatives
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have emerged as a promising solution for powering low‐power electronic and Internet of Things (IoT) devices by harvesting energy from artificial light sources. The development of low‐cost, non‐toxic, and stable absorber materials is central to enabling sustainable and scalable development of indoor PVs. Among various candidates, chalcogenide and kesterite absorbers such as Se, Sb 2 S 3 , Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 , GeS, Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 and Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 have recently attracted attention due to their earth abundance, environmental benignity, and suitable optoelectronic properties for indoor light harvesting. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported Indoor PV devices based on these absorber materials. Beyond comparing reported device performances, it critically examines the relationships between their fundamental optoelectronic properties, absorber processing, defect and interface engineering, device architecture, stability, sustainability, and demonstrated integration with IoT applications. Although research on these systems remains at an early stage, rapid progress has been achieved, highlighting their strong potential for next‐generation indoor energy harvesting. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions to guide the development of efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable Indoor PVs for powering low‐power electronics and IoT devices.

title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Commodity feedstock‐derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs) are a new class of allenic monomers stereoelectronically intermediate between butatrienes and allenes. While their butatriene character drives the C5 ring‐opening polymerization (C5‐ROP), the complementary allene‐type polymerization mode remains elusive. Herein we report this new pathway for VDCPs. Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring‐retaining polymerization (C2‐RRP), yielding pendant alkylidenecyclopropane moieties. Computations ascribe this reactivity to strain‐release alkene coordination, which further enables one‐pot diblock copolymerization with conventional allenes.

title: An Expandable Library of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐polymer‐electrolytes (SPEs) offer alternatives to next‐generation solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries, promising advantages in mechanical‐compliance, processability, cost‐effectiveness, and safety. While tremendous efforts have generated diverse SPEs since 1970s, SPE‐practicality remains limited by the trade‐offs among ion‐conductivity, high‐voltage stability, and Li 0 ‐electrolyte compatibility. Here, we establish the first SPE library covering 12 SPEs across five polymer families, which allows us to collect large datasets on chemistry, interfacial, and electrochemical properties that unveil their hidden connections. Correlation analysis of these descriptors reveals binding‐strength between polymer and Li + , subtle variations in polymer molecular structure, and solid‐electrolyte‐interphase composition as dictating factors. Also discovered is that the standard deviation of coulombic‐efficiency rather than its average value governs the battery cycling stability. The SPE library can be rapidly expanded through two structural engineering pathways: grafting diverse functional segments onto backbones and constructing compositionally‐complex SPEs. As a proof‐of‐concept, we fabricate several such SPEs and find improved high‐voltage stability through gradually increasing the complexity of the polymer matrices. A terpolymer‐based acrylates SPE exhibits outstanding Li 0 plating/stripping over 1800 h, stable cycling in LiCoO 2 ||Li battery with 100% capacity retention and an average coulombic‐efficiency of 99.91% ± 0.09% over 100 cycles. This work provides a transformative framework to design the future polymer materials.

title: Ferroelectric‐Field Gating Suppresses the Outward Migration of Active Oxygen Intermediates in Li‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Li‐rich layered oxides deliver high capacities through cation–anion co‐redox chemistry. During high‐voltage charging, however, peroxide/superoxide‐like O─O intermediates migrate down their concentration gradient from oxygen‐redox‐active regions toward particle surfaces, accumulating at the interface. This accumulation accelerates irreversible O 2 evolution and structural degradation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity fading. Here, we construct a spontaneously polarized ferroelectric LiNbO 3 interfacial layer that generates a built‐in electric field to regulate oxygen redox in Li‐rich cathodes. This electric field suppresses concentration‐gradient‐driven migration and interfacial enrichment of charged active oxygen intermediates, limiting O 2 evolution and preserving a uniform surface‐to‐bulk distribution of oxygen electronic states at high delithiation. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 310 mAh g −1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.97%, and 79% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, this strategy enables Li‐metal pouch cells to achieve an energy density of 620 Wh kg −1 and graphite‐based pouch cells to maintain stable operation over 2000 cycles. This work establishes ferroelectric‐field regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox chemistry in Li‐rich cathodes.

title: Membrane‐Fusion Navigated Cell Membrane Anchoring Enhances Pyroptosis for Photoimmunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyroptosis, a membrane disruptive and highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death, remains underexploited in cancer photoimmunotherapy due to the lack of general design principles beyond photosensitizer engineering. Here, we establish a membrane confined strategy that directly programs pyroptotic execution by targeting the plasma membrane as the primary reaction interface. A membrane fusogenic liposomal system enables precise anchoring of a caged perylene bisimides (PBI) onto the cell membrane, bypassing complex molecular modification. Upon light irradiation, PBI undergoes photocyclization to generate an active photosensitizer (CBI) and a protonic acid in situ. This dual output synergistically amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) production within a confined lipid environment, promoting lipid peroxidation, GPX4 downregulation, and membrane destabilization. Consequently, pyroptosis is efficiently triggered alongside ferroptosis, leading to enhanced tumor cell killing and immune activation both in vitro and in vivo. By shifting the design paradigm from molecular optimization to cell membrane control, this work reframes the plasma membrane from a passive barrier into an active reaction platform, providing a general and modular strategy for programmable pyroptosis‐based photoimmunotherapy.

title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction Coupled With CH3OH Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Paired photoredox catalysis enables co‐valorization of CO 2 and small molecules to high‐value chemicals via concurrent oxidation and reduction half‐reactions. However, most systems feature decoupled half‐reactions with no intrinsic substrate‐product interplay, merely utilizing electrons and holes separately, and failing to realize convergent chemical synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate a tandem photoredox‐photothermal catalytic system for efficient ethylene glycol (EG) synthesis, comprising (i) the photoredox catalysis of CO 2 reduction integrated with C─C coupling of methanol (CH 3 OH) to EG over Cu‐doped Zn 0.75 Cd 0.25 S catalysts, and (ii) the photothermal conversion of syngas to CH 3 OH over commercial CuZnAl catalysts. Of note, the CH 3 OH formed in situ via CO 2 reduction can feed into the pool of oxidation substrates, while the co‐generated syngas (ideal H 2 /CO ratio ≈ 2) is further converted to additional CH 3 OH and then recirculated as a supplemental oxidation substrate. Such a tandem catalytic design achieves high atom‐ and redox‐economy for EG synthesis, delivering an exceptional apparent quantum yield of 24.1%, outperforming those previously reported for CH 3 OH coupling to EG under an inert atmosphere. This work highlights the promise of orchestrating photoredox‐based closed‐loop catalytic architectures for value‐added C 2+ chemical synthesis with high efficiency and selectivity.

title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A nonenzymatic desymmetrization of acyclic meso ‐1,3‐diols by Si─O coupling with a hydrosilane is reported. The C s ‐symmetric diols undergo enantioselective monosilylation with a Cu─H/( R , R )‐Ph‐BPE catalyst system. The choice of hydrosilane was critical for suppressing undesired bissilylation, with a tertiary homobenzylic silane providing the best results. A series of simple alkyl‐substituted 1,3‐diols was converted into the corresponding silyl ethers with high enantiomeric ratios, with an unsubstituted methylene unit in the 2‐position identified as the most favorable scaffold for efficient and selective desymmetrization. Further modifications of the obtained enantioenriched products additionally emphasize the synthetic value of the reported methodology.

title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalysts for the ring‐opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of sulphur‐containing monomers are almost invariably inherited from all‐oxygen chemistry, where performance tracks the barrier of the rate‐determining propagation step. We show that this transfer fails. The activity of Cr(III), Co(III) and Zn(II) complexes of a common salicylimine scaffold cannot be explained by computationally tracking monomer insertions and metal activity is better predicted off‐cycle. A revised experimentally supported computational hypothesis implicates metal thiolates, generated by side‐reactions at the chain end, to deactivate the catalyst by either binding too tightly to or reducing the metal centre. The resulting computational descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, are distinct from Lewis acidity and chemical hardness, and predicted Al(III) to be competent. Al(III) catalysis delivers recyclable sulphur‐containing copolymers with a high apparent weight of M n = 238.6 kg/mol. This unlocks previously underexplored processing methods for these types of materials such as melt‐spinning and scCO 2 ‐foaming. Our results suggest new structure–activity design rules for sulphur‐containing polymerisation catalysis which are urgently required to obtain technologically useful materials.

title: Nitrogen‐Rich Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Reversible Lithium Deposition in Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Poor lithium reversibility and sluggish interfacial kinetics limit the areal capacity and rate capability of anode‐free lithium batteries. A nitrogen‐rich covalent organic framework (COF) as an interphase layer promotes uniform lithium deposition, enabling plating/stripping at 20 mAh/cm 2 in Li/Cu cells and anode‐free full‐cell operation at 4.1 mAh/cm 2 , as reported by Z. Ouyang, S. Zheng, S. Li, et al., Angewandte Chemie Novit 2 (2026): e70027.

title: Isolation of Open‐Shell Vinylidene Complexes of Iridium, Ruthenium, and Osmium
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐shell vinylidene complexes are prone to undergo fast, ligand‐centered radical reactions. Herein, we describe the synthesis of paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with terminal N‐heterocyclic vinylidene ligands. Under inert conditions, these complexes remain stable over extended periods, allowing for isolation on a preparative scale and crystallographic analyses (for Ir and Ru). The results of computational investigations, EPR spectroscopic, and reactivity studies imply that the radical is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.

title: Chemoselective On-Resin Synthesis of Imide and Thiosuccinimide Functionalized Peptides: Enabling Tunable Retro-Thia-Michael Bioconjugations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report a site-selective synthetic methodology for accessing 5- and 6-membered imide and thiosuccinimide functional groups on-resin via Fmoc solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). The formation of these heterocyclic frameworks is enabled by a modified Corey–Nicolaou activation strategy, which is kinetically favored via a 5/6-exo-trig cyclization according to Baldwin’s rules. The incorporation of the versatile 2-pyridyl thiosuccinimide moiety, acting as a masked maleimide, facilitates chemoselective aqueous solution-phase bioconjugations via a retro-thia-Michael pathway. This platform accommodates a broad scope of peptide modifications, including intramolecular cyclization, peptide stapling, small-molecule/peptide conjugation, and biocompatible protein conjugation. Furthermore, the resulting thiosuccinimide constructs can undergo controlled hydrolysis to yield stable acyclic thioether-linked conjugates, providing uniform peptide derivatives that are highly resistant to subsequent retro-thia-Michael degradation.

title: Regioswitchable and Enantioselective Dialkylation of Alkenes: Modular Access to Chiral β- and γ-Amino Esters
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalytic alkene difunctionalization is a powerful strategy for the rapid assembly of complex molecular architectures and has wide applications in synthetic chemistry. However, selective construction of two distinct alkyl–alkyl bonds across the C═C bond in alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Existing methods heavily rely on directing group strategy or specific ground-state radical traps, and the regio- and enantioselective dialkylation of alkenes remains elusive. Furthermore, a method enabling the simultaneous access to two regioisomers in an enantioselective manner has not yet been devised. Herein, we present a regioswitchable and enantioselective alkene dialkylation via photoredox/nickel dual catalysis. This approach provides a unique technique for the modular and practical synthesis of optically pure natural and unnatural β- and γ-amino esters, cornerstones of chemistry and biology. This method utilizes readily available and abundant unactivated alkyl halides and protic C(sp3)–H bonds as coupling partners, demonstrating broad substrate applicability as well as excellent regio- and enantioselectivity. The key to the success lies in the ingenious utilization of the rate difference in the generation of alkyl radicals between alkyl iodides and alkyl bromides via halogen-atom transfer. Furthermore, the synthetic practicality of this regiodivergent protocol has been demonstrated in the enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

title: Disulfide-Bridged Pyrene−Dicyanoisophorone Dyad for Cross-Validated Dual-Channel Fluorescent Detection of Dithiothreitol in Biological Fluids
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 1,4-Dithiothreitol (DTT) is a potent reducing agent widely used in biochemical, pharmaceutical, and analytical workflows. However, residual DTT can interfere with downstream analyses and compromise product integrity, highlighting the critical need for reliable detection methods in complex biological matrices. Conventional quantification techniques often suffer from operational complexity or insufficient sensitivity, whereas existing fluorescent probes are typically hindered by background interference, poor selectivity over abundant biothiols, and single-channel responses that limit analytical reliability. Herein, we present NIR-SS-PY, a novel dual-channel fluorescent probe integrating a dicyanoisophorone-based ratiometric near-infrared (NIR) signal and a pyrene-based turn-on signal upon DTT-mediated disulfide cleavage. The NIR channel exhibits a self-referenced ratiometric fluorescence response (I661/I605), whereas the pyrene channel provides an independent turn-on fluorescence output (I382). The integration of these complementary signaling modes enables rigorous cross-validation of the analytical readout, effectively overcoming severe background interference in biological samples and significantly enhancing measurement fidelity. Notably, NIR-SS-PY exhibits preferential selectivity for DTT over biologically abundant thiols. Its practical utility was successfully demonstrated through spike-recovery assays in human serum and artificial urine. These findings establish NIR-SS-PY as a robust, high-fidelity sensing platform for the reliable determination of residual DTT in complex biochemical and biopharmaceutical samples.

title: From Localized Mn Defect to Oxygen Loss: The Interplay of Jahn–Teller and Pseudo–Jahn–Teller Distortions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing structurally robust layered manganese-based cathodes is pivotal for sodium-ion batteries, yet inhibiting their lattice collapse remains an ongoing challenge. Here, we unravel a previously overlooked degradation mechanism in Na-birnessite, revealing that the localized Pseudo–Jahn–Teller (PJT) distortion exerts a much more catastrophic and dominant impact on framework failure than the traditionally emphasized cooperative Jahn–Teller (JT) effect. We show that during desodiation, the coexistence of structural Mn vacancies and crystal water triggers a strong Mn4+-related PJT distortion, accelerating irreversible oxygen loss at unexpectedly low voltages. To circumvent this vulnerability, we synthesize a Mn-vacancy-suppressed Na0.62Cu0.1Mn0.9O2·0.35H2O cathode. The substantial reduction of Mn vacancies breaks the critical electronic-vibrational coupling pathways, successfully mitigating the localized PJT modes and securing excellent cyclability (80% retention over 1000 cycles). When coupled with a hard carbon anode, the practical viability of this design is fully demonstrated. This discovery shifts the research focus from macro-JT suppression to local-PJT mitigation, establishing an essential guideline for designing degradation-resistant intercalation electrodes.

title: Nucleotide-Resolved Conformational Analysis of Nascent RNA Chains within the Bacterial Transcription Elongation Complex by MAS-DNP Solid-State NMR
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In all kingdoms of life, multisubunit RNA polymerases transcribe DNA to RNA. Both genomic DNA and newly transcribed RNA play key roles in transcription initiation, elongation, and termination. For example, a stretch of uridine residues at the 3′-end of the nascent RNA chain serves as a trigger to terminate transcription, release the nascent RNA chain, and disassemble bacterial transcription elongation complexes (ECs). It has remained unclear how the transcript can trigger termination if polyuridine stretches are synthesized. Here, we establish an approach that combines site-selective 13C/15N labeling of uridines with magic-angle-spinning dynamic nuclear polarization (MAS-DNP) NMR to probe the nascent transcript residue by residue within a reconstituted, stalled Escherichia coli transcription EC. We read out the 3′-terminal U-tract in the free RNA and in complexes stalled at two registers to investigate conformational heterogeneity in the rU–dA hybrid duplex. Our results suggest that the internal uridines adopt a stable A-form (C3′-endo) conformation in the hybrid duplex. This conformation remains unchanged within the EC, whereas the 3′-terminal residue is selectively perturbed within the complex. Solid-state NMR data collected on tailored isotopically labeled ECs resolve single-residue differences in conformation inside an assembled transcription EC, opening a route to study the nascent RNA at sites relevant to pausing and termination by MAS-DNP.

title: Expanding antimicrobial chemical space by engineering drug safety
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) infections are a major health threat. Although advances in high-throughput screening, genome mining, and machine learning have accelerated antimicrobial discovery, insufficient separation between antibacterial efficacy and host toxicity remains a bottleneck to the clinical development of new antimicrobial compounds. Here, we establish a generalizable, two-component strategy to engineer drug safety and mobilize otherwise inaccessible chemical space for antimicrobial therapy, using calicheamicin, a potent cytotoxin with unacceptable host toxicity, as a proof of concept. First, we engineer a conditionally active drug conjugate that limits calicheamicin activity to infected tissue, thereby reducing systemic toxicity. Second, we engineer a self-resistance enzyme from Micromonospora echinospora, the natural producer of calicheamicin, as a long-circulating antidote to neutralize calicheamicin outside infected tissue, further reducing off-target toxicity. The conjugate exhibits activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens upon exposure to a protease present within the infected microenvironment. When delivered with the antidote, antibacterial efficacy is maintained while off-target toxicity is reduced in mouse models of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial pneumonia. We anticipate that our dual strategy, which engineers drug safety rather than selecting for it, provides a generalizable framework for mobilizing promising but toxic compounds as antimicrobials.

title: Transcriptional nodes governing diversity and effector rewiring of a plastic liver invariant natural killer T cell ecosystem
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells are thought to exit the thymus as terminally differentiated subsets that seed tissues with fixed effector biases. However, the composition, regulatory architecture and plasticity of tissue-resident iNKT cell compartments remain ill-defined. Here, we chart the cellular diversity and transcription-factor (TF) circuitry of mouse liver-resident iNKT (LiNKT) cells and delineate intrahepatic differentiation at steady state and following repeated intravascular αGalCer/CD1d stimulation. Single-cell profiling identifies eight subsets with distinct transcriptional signatures—LiNKT2 (IL-4/IL-13-biased), LiNKT17 (IL-17A-biased), LiNKTR1 (TR1-like, IL-10-biased), and five NKT1-like (IFNγ-biased) states including LiNKT1.1, LiNKT1.2, LiNKT1.3, Klrg1lowCx3cr1low Effector and Klrg1highCx3cr1high Effector populations. Trajectory and compositional analyses reveal that iterative stimulation expands LiNKT2 and drives their conversion into LiNKTR1, while LiNKT1.1 seeds Effector and Klrg1⁺Cx3cr1⁺ Effector states, revealing local specification layered atop thymic priming. Conditional deletion across seven signature TFs associated with each subset maps subset dependencies and fate transitions: BCL-6 and TCF-1 sustain global iNKT output and, together with T-BET, license all NKT1-like states. BCL-6, ID3, and IRF4 drive Effector LiNKT1; BCL-6 and c-MAF specify LiNKT17; BLIMP-1 promotes LiNKT2 and, with c-MAF and IRF4, enforces LiNKTR1 specification. BLIMP-1 and ID3 oppose each other in LiNKTR1 versus Effector LiNKT1 differentiation. Thus, the hepatic iNKT compartment emerges as a TF-wired, plastic network in which local cues and subset-specific TF combinations govern lineage progression, nominating actionable nodes for tuning liver inflammation and repair.

title: A membrane-active cationic supramolecule to treat both fungal and bacterial keratitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rising antimicrobial resistance (AMR) underscores the urgent need for new antimicrobial strategies. We report here a membrane-active cationic supramolecule and its strong therapeutic efficacy against both fungal and bacterial keratitis in animal models. The lead Y8 design displayed broad-spectrum activity against various fungal pathogens, with low-µM MIC90, rapid action kinetics, and resistance evasion. Mechanistically, it disrupts the fungal cytoplasmic membrane and interacts with the cell wall glucan. Y8 is ocular compatible and, more importantly, shows higher/comparable efficacy to voriconazole, natamycin and amphotericin B in treating Candida, Fusarium and Aspergillus keratitis in mice or rabbits, respectively. It further displays strong activity against pathogenic bacteria, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with markedly better treatment outcomes than vancomycin in a mouse MRSA keratitis model. Overall, here we demonstrate a safe, potent, and cross-kingdom antimicrobial strategy, which may potentially contribute to the frontline infection management and AMR crisis mitigation.

title: Oxygen-Stabilized Barium Manganese Nitride Framework Enables Low-Temperature Ammonia Decomposition
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rational design of stable active sites from earth-abundant elements is essential for replacing precious metals and advancing low-temperature ammonia decomposition for hydrogen delivery. Early 3d transition metals are attractive because of their abundance and low cost, yet their strong nitrogen binding often hinders catalytic turnover. Here, we report a novel oxynitride, Ba6Mn2N6O, in which lattice oxygen coordinates with Ba to stabilize an active barium manganese nitride framework comprising isolated [MnN3]δ− units and electron-confined Ba6 cavities. These Ba6 cavities promote NH3 adsorption and activation, lattice nitrogen enables N–N coupling, and redox-active Mn centers mediate electron transfer from N to H. This cooperative mechanism enables MgO-supported Ba6Mn2N6O to outperform leading nonprecious-metal catalysts and many Ru-based catalysts at 450 °C, while reducing transition-metal costs by 2–4 orders of magnitude relative to Co and Ru. This work demonstrates the potential of rationally engineered, earth-abundant active sites to migrate the reliance on Ru and advance ammonia as a global-scale hydrogen carrier.

title: Antibody-Guided Photocatalytic Cross-Linking Enables Targeted Protein Structure Elucidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The structure and dynamics of proteins underlie virtually all biological processes, and there is a growing need for methods that can interrogate protein conformations in complex mixtures. Chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) addresses this need. Still, it relies on untargeted, diffusible cross-linkers that react with any accessible residue, limiting both selectivity and effective use of cross-linking capacity. Here, we report an antibody-guided, photocatalytic cross-linking platform that enables targeted structural elucidation of proteins of interest within complex samples. We developed HyProX, a trifunctional histidine-specific cross-linker that combines two hydrazide groups to trap light-induced histidine intermediates and a phosphonic acid handle for enrichment. Building on LUX-MS photocatalytic proximity labeling, singlet oxygen generators (SOGs) conjugated to antibodies locally convert histidines on the target protein into short-lived endoperoxide intermediates, which HyProX selectively captures to form His–His cross-links in a strictly light-dependent manner. Using model peptides, we demonstrate efficient formation of cross-linked products and show that HyProX forms a C–N bond that undergoes preferential collision-induced dissociation (CID), releasing signature fragment pairs that MS3 can directly sequence. Applying antibody-guided HyProX cross-linking to human transferrin in a multiprotein mixture and human serum yields an increase in cross-linked spectral matches and higher unique cross-link coverage for the target protein compared to untargeted conditions, with all observed cross-links mapping on the known crystal structure. Together, these results establish antibody-guided, photocatalytic His–His cross-linking with HyProX as a conceptually new XL-MS platform that provides spatiotemporal control, residue selectivity, and an intrinsic MS-based decross-linking readout for targeted protein structure analysis in complex biological mixtures.

title: Augmenting the extrapolation capability of disruption prediction to extended parameter regimes by predict-first neural network
abstract: The prediction, mitigation, and avoidance of disruptions are critical prerequisites for ensuring the safe operation of future fusion reactors. While machine learning-based disruption prediction techniques have achieved high accuracy in recent years, their application to a new device demands strong extrapolation capability across parameter regimes. This capability is essential to maintain robust algorithm performance as the operational space of the device expands, while it is also a main shortcoming for most machine learning techniques. This study evaluates the extrapolation capability of a disruption prediction algorithm using multiple subsets of experimental data from HL-3 tokamak, divided by key plasma parameters, yielding three key findings. Firstly, the area under the receiver-operator characteristic curve (AUC) of a standard deep learning algorithm trained on the subset with low parameters degrades to around 0.750, 0.666, and 0.540 when extrapolated to three progressively distant extrapolation regimes. However, the predict-first neural network (PFNN) maintains an AUC of about 0.873, 0.823 and 0.701. Secondly, the algorithm’s accuracy shows a clear contrast in degradation behaviour: when extrapolating along electromagnetic parameters like plasma current, performance declines slowly and continuously; when extrapolating along energy-related parameters like stored energy, performance remains initially stable but deteriorates abruptly beyond a certain threshold. Finally, after rigorously accounting for the impact of parameter regime extrapolation and adjusting the algorithm deployment strategy, deep learning proved effective in protecting the device during HL-3’s high-current and high-beta commissioning phases. This study provides valuable experience for implementing disruption prediction algorithms on new devices and is expected to offer practical reference for the initial operation of future fusion facilities like ITER.

title: Anyone can be the best depending on how structural variant callers are evaluated
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are medium- and large-scale genomic alterations that shape phenotypic diversity and disease risk. Numerous methods have been proposed for discovering SVs, however their benchmarking has been inconsistent across studies, often resulting in contradictory findings. We evaluate the performance of several SV discovery methods for detecting unbalanced SVs from long-read sequencing data and observe substantial variation in performance and ranking depending on the choice of ground truth, reference genome, and genomic regions used for evaluation. Our results indicate that these discrepancies largely arise from inconsistencies among SV callsets used as ground truth, ranging from consortium-curated benchmarks to callsets derived from high-quality assemblies. These discrepancies call for additional caution in downstream analyses and in drawing conclusions based on predicted SVs. Our findings underscore the complexity of evaluating SV detection methods and highlight the need for careful consideration and field-standard practices when reporting performance metrics.

title: Changing mercury exposure in the Yukon Watershed linked to traditional diet shifts and permafrost thaw
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rapid Arctic warming is disrupting ecosystems and traditional subsistence resources, and simultaneously may release toxic mercury into aquatic ecosystems. Together, these changes threaten food security and public health. In the Yukon River Basin of Alaska, many Indigenous communities that traditionally rely on subsistence fishing are facing precipitous declines in salmon populations. Alternative protein sources can contain up to eight times more mercury, with burbot, northern pike, and beluga being major dietary mercury contributors. More reliance on these proteins could increase mercury exposure, while permafrost thaw is projected to increase mercury concentrations in fish by 21–175% by 2100. Here, we combine diet surveys and subsistence harvest data to develop a hypothetical dietary mercury model. Dietary shifts and permafrost-driven increases in fish mercury could increase mercury intake up to 486%, potentially exceeding public health guidelines and highlighting the vulnerability of Arctic food systems to interacting environmental and ecological change.

title: Integrated simulation and instability analysis of drift wave turbulence for the hot ion mode on HL-3 tokamak
abstract: A hot ion mode with , , and fusion triple product has been achieved on HL-3. Integrated One Modeling Framework for Integrated Tasks (OMFITs) modeling across three time slices (pre-H-mode, H-mode, L-mode) reproduces experimental profiles and reveals two distinguishing physics features. First, the internal transport barrier (ITB) foot extends beyond , in contrast to conventional strong reversed shear regimes where the barrier is confined within ; here it is sustained by the strong flow shear, the decisive stabilization mechanism. Second, the complete H–L back transition exhibits pronounced ITB hysteresis: the edge transport barrier collapses while the core ITB persists with only 4% width reduction and 3.6% stored energy loss, indicating strong core-edge decoupling. Toroidal rotation dominates the radial electric field ( kV m in H-mode, exceeding the diamagnetic term by a factor of 3–6), with its peak aligned with the ITB mid-radius. Within the ITB, shear surpasses the ion temperature gradient (ITG) growth rate, suppressing ion transport to near neoclassical levels; at the foot ( ) an ITG to electron temperature gradient transition occurs near . A scan confirms the radial contrast and opposite growth rate scalings. These results establish a validated simulation platform for the HL-3 hot ion mode and support the planned deuterium–tritium campaign.

title: Optimized finite- β tokamak-stellarator hybrid configurations achieved by planar dipole-f...
abstract: Tokamak-stellarator hybrids seek to combine tokamak-like compactness and confinement with stellarator-like externally generated rotational transform and steady-state operation. In this work, we build on the recent tokamak-stellarator hybrid study using planar dipole-field coils (PDCs) (Yu et al 2026 arXiv:2605.03599), in which the fixed-position, programmable coils on an axisymmetric winding surface generate flexible three-dimensional shaping fields. Using free-boundary optimization of coil currents and plasma-equilibrium parameters, we construct optimized vacuum and finite- configurations. The vacuum cases show controllable external rotational transform and magnetic well. The finite- cases accommodate various density, temperature, and pressure profiles, producing quasi-axisymmetric (QA) equilibria with bootstrap-current profiles self-consistent with the generalized Redl closure, favorable Mercier stability, and reduced demand for external current drive. Re-optimization enables a scan with moderate PDC-current changes and access to different field-period QA branches. At large rotational transform, a toroidally omnigenous (TO)-like configuration exhibits more favorable infinite- ideal-ballooning behavior than a QA reference with matched profiles, even though ballooning stability is not directly optimized for. These results demonstrate that PDCs provide a flexible platform for achieving optimized finite- hybrid configurations.

title: Molecular basis for thermoresponsive protein condensation in plants
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plants continuously experience temperature fluctuations that shape their physiology, development, and survival. Yet, how plants sense and adapt to elevated temperatures at the molecular level remains only partially understood. Here, we uncover a sequence-encoded mechanism by which plant proteins directly sense temperature through condensation. Focusing on prion-like low-complexity domains (PLCDs) in Arabidopsis thaliana, we combine cellular imaging, quantitative biophysics, and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to show that numerous PLCDs undergo reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST)-type phase transitions. We find that PLCDs that are sufficient and necessary for condensation confer thermoresponsive variability to full-length proteins. Sequence analysis and simulations reveal that thermoresponsiveness is encoded in compositional heuristics, with sufficient PLCDs enriched in aliphatic and aromatic residues, enabling accurate prediction and rational tuning of condensation thresholds. Engineered variants with altered sequence composition exhibit predictable shifts in thermoresponsive condensation, confirming a direct, sequence-level encoding of temperature sensitivity. Our findings establish LCST-driven phase transitions as common amongst plant PLCD-containing proteins and provide a molecular framework for designing synthetic biomolecules with programmable temperature responses.

title: An all-in-one wearable platform offers continuous assessment and early diagnosis of acute kidney injury for outdoor workers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Outdoor workers are at a significantly higher risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). Efficient noninvasive monitoring of physiological changes plays a crucial role in the proactive assessment of AKI risk. Here, we introduce an all-in-one wearable platform that presents a class of translational technologies of multimodal sensors, multifunctional materials, snap-on modular electronics, and an AI-based predictive model for continuous renal function assessment and AKI risk. The wearable patch is designed to simultaneously measure temperature, skin hydration, cardiac activities, physical activities, and blood oxygen saturation, and to detect continuous changes in serum creatinine, the clinical standard for diagnosing AKI. The self-supervised learning framework integrates a clinically informed pretext deep learning task to extract features indicating the worker’s physiological change over time. An in vivo study involving 110 outdoor workers demonstrates that the real-time collection of multiple physiological parameters combined with integrated AI can facilitate early diagnosis of AKI with modest discrimination (AUC 0.60).

title: Buried stochastic interfaces enabling depth-multiplexed optical physical unclonable functions
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) convert irreproducible physical disorder into device-unique responses for hardware authentication. However, many optical PUFs rely on surface- or near-surface-accessible features, coupling optical readability to vulnerability to inspection, replication, and data-driven inference. Here we introduce optically hidden silicon PUFs that encode physically protected entropy at buried membrane–cavity interfaces and enable its readout through depth-selective optical gating. Annealing of high-aspect-ratio hole arrays produces multilayer silicon architectures with device-specific buried interfacial roughness concealed beneath a planarized, optically featureless surface. Spectro-angular- and polarization-selective illumination enables deterministic readout across eight buried interfaces in the primary configuration. The responses exhibit an inter-device Hamming distance of 0.5011 ± 0.0060 (mean ± s.d.), depth-plane discrimination accuracies of 98.9−99.4%, and 0.080% generated-response acceptance under a challenge-held-out best-of-Ksearch = 64 spoofing evaluation at a fixed impostor false-positive rate of 10−3. Redundancy-aware depth multiplexing yields a pairwise-redundancy-screened, spatial-predictability-adjusted effective pre-ECC response budget of ~0.74×108 bits per 200×200μm2 pattern while retaining wafer-scale manufacturability. These results establish buried-interface depth multiplexing as a scalable route to physically protected optical authentication.

title: Rigidity-driven molecular assembly for high-efficiency flexible perovskite/CIGS tandems
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Monolithic flexible perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells (TSCs) are pivotal for next-generation flexible photovoltaics, owing to their high power-to-weight ratio and mechanical compliance. However, their development is constrained by the challenge of depositing high-quality hole-selective contacts (HSCs) onto intrinsically rough CIGS bottom cells. Conventional molecular interlayers often exhibit poor packing on such surfaces, leading to interfacial defects that compromise both efficiency and stability. Here, we report Py6, a rigid molecule engineered with an enforced vinylene (C = C) bridge to ensure molecular planarity and extended π-conjugation. This structural rigidity fosters a highly ordered nanoscale assembly that effectively templates the growth of dense, void-free perovskite layers while optimizing interfacial energetic alignment. Consequently, our champion flexible TSC achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 28.21% (0.0749 cm2, certified 27.58%), while large-area devices (1.010 cm2) reached 25.63%, with a certified PCE of 25.19% and a certified stabilized PCE of 25.16%. Furthermore, the resulting devices exhibit exceptional durability, retaining 93.8% of their initial PCE after 400 hours of continuous 1-sun operation and 94.2% after 5000 rigorous bending cycles. Our rigidity-driven molecular design overcomes the critical interfacial bottlenecks of non-planar photovoltaics, providing a robust pathway for high-performance, mechanically resilient flexible tandem technologies.

title: Control of out-of-plane anti-damping spin torque with a canted ferromagnetic spin source
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: To achieve efficient anti-damping switching of nanoscale magnetic memories with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy using spin-orbit torque requires that the anti-damping spin-orbit torque have a strong out-of-plane component. The spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current produced by a ferromagnetic layer are candidate mechanisms for producing such an out-of-plane anti-damping torque, but both require that the magnetic moment of the spin source layer be canted partly out of the sample plane at zero applied magnetic field. Here we demonstrate such a canted configuration for a ferromagnetic SrRuO3 layer, and we characterize all vector components of the torque that it produces, including non-zero out-of-plane anti-damping torques. We verify that the out-of-plane spin component can be tuned by the orientation of the magnetic moment, with significant contributions from both the spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current.

title: Dual-comb photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy of optomechanical dynamics in gas-filled microstructured hollow-core fibers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Absorption-driven photoacoustic interactions in gas-filled hollow-core fibers enable strong optomechanical coupling between gas molecules and the micro-structured cladding, offering a sensitive platform for trace-gas detection and characterization of the microstructure. Here, we report dual-comb photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy for scan-free measurement within the dual-comb bandwidth and time-resolved interrogation of gas-cladding optomechanical dynamics in an anti-resonant hollow-core fiber. Two electro-optic frequency combs generate multi-heterodyne beats that drive photoacoustic excitation and cladding-supported acoustic resonances. The resulting photoacoustic response encodes molecular absorption into the acoustic amplitude, while the resonance frequency and linewidth of the acoustic modes reveal mechanical properties. Exploiting the resonantly enhanced photoacoustic interaction, ultrasensitive trace-gas detection at parts-per-billion level is achieved. Furthermore, millisecond-resolution probing of acoustic resonance dynamics enables real-time characterization of transient pressure changes inside the fiber. These results establish a versatile platform for time-resolved optomechanical spectroscopy in microstructured photonic devices, enabling simultaneous chemical sensing and dynamic mechanical characterization.

title: Room-temperature continuous-wave mid-infrared microdisk laser on InP enabled by InAs quantum dots
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mid-infrared photonics is important for gas monitoring, non-invasive medical diagnostics, and free-space optical links. Realizing high-density photonic integrated circuits in the short-wave mid-infrared (SW-MIR, 2–3 μm) requires compact, efficient microscale lasers that can be integrated on standard platforms. Conventional quantum-well microcavity lasers cannot sustain efficient operation as cavities shrink because lateral carrier diffusion and surface recombination impose a fundamental limit on the threshold, while Auger recombination and thermal carrier leakage losses severely compromise thermal stability in the SW-MIR window. Here, we demonstrate that the strong carrier localization in self-assembled InAs quantum-dot (QD) gain medium circumvents these limitations. A five-stack InAs/InP QD active region achieves room-temperature continuous-wave single-mode lasing in a suspended 5.5 µm microdisk at 2.064 µm. The device also sustains lasing up to 110 °C under pulsed excitation. Temperature-dependent spectra and electronic structure analysis reveal ground-to-excited state dynamics and suppression of thermal carrier leakage. These results demonstrate the potential of QD gain media for compact SW-MIR light sources on InP and Si photonic platforms.

title: Identification and functional characterization of bacterial bilirubin vinyl reductase across vertebrate gut microbiomes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gut bacteria reduce bilirubin to urobilinogen, allowing it to be excreted through feces and urine, but studies have long noted a heterogeneous mixture of partially reduced bilirubin-derived intermediates, suggesting that multiple enzymes are involved. Here we identify bilirubin vinyl reductase (BilV), an Old Yellow Enzyme family reductase encoded in the genomic neighborhood of the known bilirubin reductase (bilR). Using heterologous expression and LC–MS/MS, we show that BilR acts on the methine bridges in the bilirubin reduction pathway; co-expression with BilV enables vinyl-group reduction and complete conversion to urobilinogen. In bacterial genomes, bilV co-occurs primarily with the bilR-insertion subtype and is largely absent alongside bilR-short. Analysis of 1,197 gut metagenomes across 14 vertebrate species reveals that this differential co-occurrence shapes pathway availability across hosts: carnivores and omnivores carry balanced bilR and bilV, whereas avian microbiomes, dominated by bilR-short, are depleted for bilV. These findings establish that bilirubin reduction to urobilinogen involves two enzymes with complementary regioselectivity, revising the previous model, and that their distribution across vertebrate gut microbiomes varies in relation to host bile pigment chemistry.

title: Nitrogen-Doped Carbonized Polymer Dots Ion Source Endowing Cyclodextrin MOFs for Room-Temperature Chemiresistive CO2 Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Monitoring dissolved carbon dioxide (CO2) concentration in seawater is vital for marine environmental protection and climate governance assessment. It has been found that the γ-cyclodextrin metal-organic frameworks (CD-MOFs) assembled with small-molecule ion sources suffer from inferior stability due to the poor stability and the limited number of effective functional groups of small-molecule ion sources. Instead of small-molecule ion sources, nitrogen-doped carbonized polymer dots (N-CPDs) were employed as ion sources to construct ion conduction channels of the hydrogen-bonding network in this work. The as-prepared MOFs assembled with N-CPD ion sources possess superior comprehensive performance to those using small-molecule ion sources, including a competitive practical limit of detection (pLOD) of 500 ppb, high sensitivity (Rg/R0 = 2.82 toward 1000 ppm CO2), short response/recovery times (120 s/121 s), and over 56-day long-term stability. Moreover, its unique CO2 sensing mechanism of a hydrogen-bonding network constructed by N-CPD ion sources and CD-MOFs was investigated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The strategy universality of introducing N-CPD ion sources has also been verified by adopting five kinds of N-CPDs. It is worth noting that this chemiresistive CO2 sensor has successfully been applied to preliminarily detect the CO2 concentration of seawater samples collected from the Greater Bay Area of China. This work developed a universal strategy of employing N-CPDs as OH− ion sources to obtain high-comprehensive-performance room-temperature chemiresistive CO2 sensing materials.

title: Borophene-Gold Nanohybrid Immunosensor for In Situ EV Lysis and Cancer Biomarker Detection by Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived biomarkers provide valuable molecular information for early cancer detection and disease monitoring, yet their analysis typically requires labor-intensive EV isolation and chemical lysis, limiting access and increasing assay complexity. Here, we present a label-free, non-faradaic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (nf-EIS) biosensor based on liquid-phase-exfoliated borophene (BP) integrated onto gold electrodes for direct detection of circulating and EV-derived biomarkers in serum. BP-Au interface provides an electrochemically active, high-capacitance sensing surface via interfacial charge transfer and orbital interactions, while electron-deficient boron sites enable direct coordination with glutaraldehyde and stable antibody immobilization without insulating linker layers. To improve biomarker accessibility, we investigated two reagent-free electric-field (EF) strategies: post-capture EV permeabilization and direct high-frequency (HF) EF treatment of serum. Direct HF EF treatment temporarily permeabilized EV membranes, quickly transporting biomarkers to the sensor, enhancing target capture and nf-EIS response. Compared to EV isolation, serum HF EF treatment reduced assay time to 45 min and improved biomarker recovery. The platform achieved limit of detection ranging from 0.02 to 0.57 pg/mL for five clinically relevant EV biomarkers (TSG101, GM2AP, MUC1, MUC5AC, and EGFR). Clinical evaluation of serum samples from healthy subjects (n = 20) and lung cancer patients (n = 20) showed improved sensing performance, increasing ROC-AUC values from 0.870−0.984 to 0.985−1.000 and sensitivity by up to 16.7% following HF EF-treatment. These findings demonstrate that integrating BP-enabled signal amplification with EF-assisted EV biomarker release provides a rapid, reagent-free, and isolation-free nf-EIS platform for sensitive, multiplexed liquid biopsy, with potential for early cancer detection and decentralized clinical diagnostics.

title: Epigallocatechin Gallate-Functionalized Dual-Adjuvant Nanoplatform Elicits Potent Antitumor Immunity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Innate immune signaling is critical for maximizing the effectiveness of tumor vaccines, especially in boosting the performance of checkpoint inhibitors. To elicit robust immunostimulatory responses, we identified a dual-adjuvant platform leveraging an epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)-functionalized hollow mesoporous silica nanoparticles (HMSNs) for the co-delivery of the Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist CpG and the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist MSA-2 (C/M@HMSN@EGCG). The dual agonists co-loaded in HMSN (C/M@HMSN) complementarily and synergistically enhanced IL-12 and type I interferon (IFN-β) secretion, and dendritic cell maturation. Moreover, incorporation of EGCG on C/M@HMSN further promoted antigen cross-presentation, which is associated with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and inflammatory modulation. In vivo, the C/M@HMSN@EGCG nanoadjuvant efficiently migrated to draining lymph nodes and elicited robust antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses. In both prophylactic and therapeutic melanoma models, the nanoadjuvant based vaccine significantly inhibited tumor growth. Notably, the nanoadjuvant upregulated PD-L1 expression, and when combined with PD-L1 blockade, it further boosted antitumor efficacy, immune memory and significantly prolonged the survival of mice without causing apparent systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study establishes an EGCG-functionalized dual-adjuvant nanoplatform that integrates efficient lymph node delivery with synergistic TLR9/STING activation to enhance antigen presentation and antitumor immunity, providing a promising strategy for cancer vaccination and combination immunotherapy.

title: Electric vehicles as mobile energy carriers: An activity-based agent-based model of residential PV origin energy flows and V2G
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is turning transportation management into a coupled mobility and energy planning problem. Public EVCS deployment affects travel behavior, parking duration, and local electricity demand, while EV batteries may also provide flexible storage through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation. However, the extent to which EVs can redistribute residential photovoltaic (PV) energy depends not only on charging infrastructure but also on daily activity schedules, state-of-charge conditions, dwell times, and station-side constraints. This study develops an activity-based agent-based model to evaluate EVs as mobile carriers of residential PV-origin energy in an urban charging system. The model links home charging, activity-based travel, public charging, V2G discharge, stationary battery energy storage systems, and charging station feasibility constraints. The framework is applied to Eindhoven, the Netherlands. Results show that EVs can acquire substantial residential PV-origin energy through home charging, but consume only about 6% of it during daily travel. Most PV-origin energy remains stored in EV batteries when vehicles arrive at non-home locations, creating technical potential for redistribution. However, activity context is the dominant bottleneck limiting V2G opportunities, indicating that urban V2G potential is shaped less by infrastructure availability alone than by when and where eligible EVs are parked during daily routines.

title: Learning convex voltage constraints for transmission–distribution coordinated dispatch: A decoupled input convex neural network

Scenario-adaptive Shapley allocation of multi-market benefits in renewable energy base-transmission systems through sparse interaction learning
System-level optimization of seawater-based water supply and cooling for large-scale green hydrogen and ammonia production under variable renewable operation
abstract: As green hydrogen and ammonia projects expand in arid coastal regions, coupled demands for process water (PW) and cooling water (CW) increasingly constrain cooling system (CS) selection and water supply infrastructure sizing. To address this research gap, a transferable methodology for designing and techno-economically evaluating cooling and water supply systems for large-scale seawater-based production is presented. It combines time-resolved renewable power and ammonia production modelling, CS performance models, water treatment plant (WTP) sizing, PW and CW storage simulation, and cost assessment. It is applied to the 1.5 GW Phase 1 Murchison Green Hydrogen Project in Western Australia as a case study, using hourly ERA5 climate data for 2015–2024. The investigated CS options include once-through seawater cooling (OTSC), dry cooling (DC), wet cooling towers (WCT), and adiabatic hybrid coolers (AHC). Storage-based optimization substantially reduced the required peak treatment capacities, lowering WTP capacity by 12.4% (to 273 m 3 /h) for PW and CW capacity by 20.6% (to 1,127 m 3 /h) for WCT, and 63.0% (to 636 m 3 /h) for AHC. These reductions translated directly into lower PW-related capital expenditure, operational expenditure, and levelized cost of water (−8.7%, −4.2%, and − 7.3%, respectively). On an integrated cost basis, WCT achieved the lowest levelized cost of cooling (5.96 USD/MWh th ), below DC (38.0%), AHC (44.7%), and OTSC (73.6%). A simplified cost-allocation sensitivity showed that neglecting water treatment and marine infrastructure requirements can alter the CS ranking. The analysis further indicated that CS and water supply make a non-negligible contribution to the total levelized cost of hydrogen, accounting for 2.0–7.4%.

title: Unlocking public EV charging flexibility for grid balancing: A year-long empirical assessment of unidirectional and bidirectional smart charging in Prague
abstract: The transition of imbalance settlement in the Continental Europe synchronous area to 15-minute market time units, together with rising shares of variable renewable generation, raises the operational value of sub-hourly demand-side flexibility. Electric vehicles at public charging stations are an attractive source, yet empirical estimates of the balancing value of public smart charging remain scarce. This paper quantifies the technical potential of aggregated public smart charging in Prague to absorb the 15-minute system imbalance of the Czech transmission system operator ČEPS, using a full year of real charging-session data: 286,492 sessions across 1051 charging points. An ex-post optimization on a session-level flexibility envelope evaluates four configurations: the unidirectional (V1G) and bidirectional (V2G) operating modes, each under two user-comfort scenarios in which the delivered energy is preserved exactly (S1) or relaxed to the greater of 80% of it or 30 kWh (S2). The fleet’s uncontrolled load is removed first, so the same energy is re-timed, not added. Public V1G absorbs 4.44% of the imbalance energy under S1 and 4.85% under S2; V2G absorbs 7.09% and 7.64%. Bidirectional operation increases the absorbed energy by more than half, whereas relaxing comfort adds only about half a percentage point, so the bidirectional-infrastructure axis carries far more value than the user-incentive axis. These figures are a best-case ceiling computed with hindsight, not an operational forecast; valued at Czech final settlement prices, the V2G potential is a gross avoided balancing cost of up to about EUR 480,000 per year.
