Understanding the Connection between the Redox Reversibility of Pt−O Species and the Oxygen Reduction Reaction Activity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Platinum surface oxides─adsorbed OH and O species (Pt─OH/Pt─O)─are central to the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet whether they serve as reaction intermediates or site-blocking poisons, and how their redox dynamics govern ORR activity, remain debated. In this study, Pt(111) single-crystal and polycrystalline platinum electrodes are examined by cyclic voltammetry and rotating disk electrode methods to establish how the reversible interconversion of Pt─OH and Pt─O under an inert atmosphere relates to ORR performance. The rate at which Pt─O is reduced slows as oxide coverage grows, but this process can be made faster by adsorbing organic modifiers; 7-ethyltheophylline (ETP) and 3-methyl-3H-imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (3MIP) both move the Pt─O reduction feature under Ar to 0.90 V. Although the oxygen intermediates formed during O2 reduction are not exactly the same as those generated by anodic oxidation under Ar, the two appear structurally related, with the latter behaving as surface poisons. A metric termed ORR scan reversibility, defined as the gap in current density between forward and reverse scans at a given potential, is used to quantify the degree to which Pt−O coverage suppresses ORR performance. By speeding up Pt−O reduction, ETP and 3MIP simultaneously improve scan reversibility and ORR activity. ETP decreases the current density gap by a factor of ∼190 on Pt(111) (from 190 to 1 μA cm−2) and by one-half on polycrystalline platinum (from 1580 to 860 μA cm−2). Theophylline (TP), which facilitates Pt─O formation instead of its reduction, also narrows the scan-to-scan gap but yields no activity gain, indicating that the reduction rather than formation of Pt─O is the decisive step in controlling ORR performance. These findings offer a quantitative basis for describing how Pt oxidation relates to ORR and point to molecular modification as a route to reducing performance losses caused by oxide formation on fuel-cell cathodes.

title: When hydrogen is not fully flexible: Implications for sector-coupled energy models
Recent Advances in Polymer Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries: From the Perspective of Molecular Structure Design
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Global industrial upgrading, accelerating electrification, and the rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence-powered data centers are driving a sustained increase in electricity demand, intensifying the need for energy-storage technologies that combine high energy density with strong safety. To this end, high-voltage solid-state polymer lithium-metal batteries have attracted increasing attention. However, their development is strongly limited by the insufficient oxidative stability of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). Recent studies suggest that the oxidation behavior of polar functional groups is closely related to the electronic properties and bonding configurations of the polymer, making these features important intrinsic factors in determining the oxidative stability of polymer electrolytes. From this perspective, tailoring the molecular structure of polymer electrolytes has emerged as an effective approach for improving their stability under high-voltage conditions. These design approaches include electronic regulation through substituent effects, designing polar functional groups with enhanced intrinsic oxidative stability and ionic conductivity, optimization of vulnerable sites and polymer backbones, and rational integration of multiple functional units. Beyond intrinsic structural regulation, intermolecular interactions can further stabilize reactive polar sites, while interfacial design can suppress continuous electrolyte decomposition by controlling reaction pathways and passivation behavior. This review integrates molecular design with complementary stabilization strategies to provide insights into high-voltage failure mechanisms and guide the rational development of next-generation high-voltage SPEs.

title: Model-based prediction of temperature evolution in solid-state batteries with minimal experimental data: A case study on composite cathodes under thermal ramp
abstract: While solid-state batteries (SSBs) are presumed to be safer than conventional LIBs, recent studies suggest that they can undergo a quicker and more severe thermal runaway than LIB cells. We have developed a modelling framework to investigate safety of SSBs by linking material-scale measurements to electrode- or cell-scale thermal behaviour. The proposed framework directly incorporates differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) heat flow measurements obtained at a single heating rate as a time-dependent heat source to simulate the temperature evolution of electrodes and cells under prescribed thermal ramp conditions. With minimum experimental data and computational fitting efforts, our model allows for consistent thermal-safety comparisons across cell formats and rapid screening of SSB materials. We implemented our model for cathode composites of SSBs, consisting of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 and eight different oxide- and sulphide-based solid electrolytes, exposed to a thermal ramp and simulated their temperature evolution. The simulations were run in three representative formats for SSBs: coin, single-layer pouch, and multilayer-pouch cells. The results show that the temperature increase in sulphide-based cathode composites is significantly higher than that of oxide-based composites. Among the different formats, the temperature increases considerably higher in cathode composites with multilayer-pouch format, compared to others. The model was also applied to two 24 Ah LIB cells under a 150 °C oven test, whose temperature evolution results has been reported in the literature. The simulated temperature evolution showed good agreement with the experimental measurements and the corresponding kinetic-based model under the investigated thermal conditions, demonstrating the capability of the simplified approach to translate calorimetric heat generation data into full-cell thermal behaviour and its potential applicability to battery systems with different chemistries.

title: Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

title: Geopolitical risk and energy transition in the European Union: Can institutional quality mitigate geopolitical shocks?
Geopolitical exposure in cross-border electricity transmission: Evidence from Baltic desynchronization and interconnection disruptions
The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Steric Hindrance-Governed Configurational Evolution in Cellulose-Derived Sustainable Multicolor Carbon Dots: Application in Smartphone-Assisted Portable Nitrite Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Renewable biomass is a promising precursor for sustainable carbon dots (CDs), yet the controllable synthesis of multicolor emissive CDs remains a major challenge. Herein, we proposed a steric hindrance-mediated strategy to achieve the multicolor emission of cellulose-derived CDs via employing three phenylenediamine isomers, including o-phenylenediamine (OPD), m-phenylenediamine (MPD), and p-phenylenediamine (PPD), as dopants during the hydrothermal process of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). Changing the dopant from OPD to PPD was beneficial in reducing steric hindrance between the dopants and CMC and thus contributed to the increased percentage of conjugated sp2 carbon (from 3.36% to 13.58%) and graphitic N (from 5.54% to 11.09%) in the three CDs. The synergistic effect of enlarged conjugated structure and enhanced graphitic N content narrowed the energy gap of three CDs from 2.89 to 2.81 eV and further to 2.76 eV, enabling them to emit blue (430.8 nm), green (505.1 nm), and yellow (522.5 nm) fluorescence, respectively. Owing to the high quantum yield of 20.0% and long-wavelength fluorescence, the green-emitted CDs were employed as a sensitive fluorescent probe for nitrite detection with a detection limit of 0.42 µM. Moreover, a paper-based sensing platform was constructed by chemical grafting of the CDs onto filter paper for portable analysis with smartphone assistance. This work not only established a rational strategy for engineering the fluorescence properties of CDs derived from biomass but also revealed the potential influence of dopant molecular geometry on the carbonization and nitrogen-doping processes in polymeric precursor systems.

title: Phase-Engineered Cobalt Molybdate for Highly Selective Visible-Light Photocatalytic Oxidation of Glycerol
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Glycerol, a significant by-product of biodiesel production, has prompted increased interest in the catalytic processes that convert it into valuable products. Considerable efforts have been made to identify effective catalysts and technologies to transform glycerol into various fine chemicals. One promising method is photocatalytic glycerol oxidation using renewable solar energy, which allows reactions to occur under milder conditions. However, the presence of three hydroxyl (–OH) groups in glycerol leads to multiple reaction pathways, producing various products like 1,3-dihydroxyacetone, glyceric acid, lactic acid, and formic acid. Therefore, developing photocatalysts that can selectively direct these reactions toward specific desired products is very crucial. In this study, well-defined nanorods of cobalt molybdate, CoMoO4 (β phase), were synthesized via a simple hot-injection-based method (N2 atmosphere) using ethylene glycol as a structure-directing agent, followed by calcination under N2 atmosphere, which then converted into irregular-shaped nanocrystals of CoMoO4 (primarily α phase) by mechanical hand grinding for over a minute. Afterward, the α- and β-phases of CoMoO4 nanostructures were evaluated for photocatalytic glycerol oxidation under one-sun and natural sunlight at ambient conditions. Interestingly, among them, the α-phase of CoMoO4 nanostructures exhibited superior photocatalytic performance over the β-phase, achieving ∼98% selectivity for glyceric acid with a product yield of 0.71 mmol·h–1·g–1. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of glycerol oxidation with a cobalt molybdate (CoMoO4)-based photocatalyst, which exhibits remarkable selectivity toward glyceric acid. In contrast, the benchmark P25 TiO2 photocatalyst remains inactive under identical conditions. To understand the reasons behind the superior photocatalytic performance of the synthesized α-phase of cobalt molybdate over the β-phase, density functional theory (DFT) was carried out. The DFT analysis confirmed that the α-phase of cobalt molybdate exhibits superior catalytic activity and thermodynamic stability. This is evidenced by increased orbital overlap and a subtle shift in the d-band center, which enhances adsorbate–surface interactions and thus catalytic activity. Additionally, the more negative Gibbs free energy of glycerol on the α-phase confirms its preferential binding and enhanced stabilization of intermediates. These findings demonstrate that simple cobalt molybdate nanostructures, reported here for the first time as photocatalysts, can efficiently and sustainably convert glycerol into valuable products under ambient conditions, without relying on noble metals or carbon- or titanium-based nanocomposites.

title: Fully Synthetic Extracellular Vesicle-like Lipid Nanoparticles Recapitulate the Tumor Accumulation of Native Vesicles in NRAS-Mutant Melanoma
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract NRAS-mutant melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer for which early detection and tumor targeting remain major clinical challenges. Although liposome-based nanotechnologies have been widely explored for cancer diagnosis and therapy, their tumor accumulation still largely relies on the enhanced permeability and retention effect, which is heterogeneous and often limits efficient penetration into solid tumors. In contrast, extracellular vesicles (EVs) exhibit efficient tumor penetration and intrinsic homing to their tumor of origin, but their clinical translation is hindered by challenges in scalable production and purification. To address these limitations, we engineered a fully synthetic EV-like nanoplatform that exhibits the tumor tropism of EVs derived from NRAS-mutant melanoma. EVs isolated from MUG Mel-2 NRAS-mutant melanoma cells and FOM-101 healthy melanocytes underwent comparative lipidomic and proteomic profiling to identify tumor-specific membrane signatures. Based on these data, we engineered synthetic liposomes that recapitulate the lipid composition of melanoma-derived EVs and incorporated selected tumor-associated proteins to reproduce EV biological function. The resulting EV-like nanoparticles showed favorable physicochemical properties, successful protein incorporation, and efficient internalization in NRAS-mutant melanoma cells. In vivo biodistribution studies in BALB/c nude mice bearing human melanoma xenografts demonstrated that EV-like nanoparticles reproduced the tumor accumulation of native EVs after intravenous administration. Nanoparticles mimicking the melanoma EV lipid composition accumulated in tumors even without protein enrichment, identifying lipids as active determinants of tumor homing, whereas physicochemically comparable conventional liposomes accumulated mainly in the liver. Protein incorporation, in particular CD98, further enhanced tumor accumulation and improved the tumor-to-liver distribution. Our findings demonstrate that this EV-inspired nanoplatform serves as a proof-of-concept tumor-homing system for NRAS-mutant melanoma, establishing a foundation for future therapeutic drug loading and targeted delivery applications.

Wavelength-Switchable Bidirectional Photoelectric Plasticity in In2Se3 Nanoparticle-Modified In2O3 Nanowires for Neuromorphic Vision
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic vision systems require dynamic and multispectral visual processing capabilities to operate in complex environments. However, most optoelectronic synapses still exhibit either a fixed-polarity photoresponse or weak wavelength selectivity, which limits their potential for advanced neuromorphic vision. Here, we report a wavelength-dependent bidirectional optoelectronic synapse based on In2Se3 nanoparticle-modified In2O3 nanowires. We introduce In2Se3 nanoparticles, which are prepared through a facile and scalable liquid-phase exfoliation method, and first employ them to modulate the photoresponse in synaptic devices. The resulting heterostructure broadens the UV spectral response into the visible region and enables bidirectional photocurrents. Positive photocurrents are observed under 365, 455, and 520 nm illumination, whereas a negative photocurrent appears under 640 nm excitation. The measurements are consistent with a qualitative picture in which conductance-enhancing photocarrier processes compete with trapping-related changes in effective channel transport or contact resistance, with their relative contributions depending on the excitation wavelength. In addition to typical synaptic behaviors, the device combines temporal memory and a wavelength-dependent bidirectional response to enable the accumulation of information across sequential optical inputs, which is used in a proof-of-concept simulation of temporal visual preprocessing for varying camouflage scenes. This work provides a materials strategy for wavelength-selective bidirectional optoelectronic synapses and illustrates their potential for temporal visual preprocessing through proof-of-concept simulations.

title: Tumor Type−Dependent Cancer-Associated Fibroblast Activation and Extracellular Matrix Remodeling in Three-Dimensional Bioprinted Co-Culture Tumor Spheroid
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key stromal regulators of tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Activation of CAFs varies across tumor types. Comparative platforms for evaluating these differences under controlled conditions remain limited. Here, a three-dimensional bioprinting-assisted agarose microwell platform was developed to quantitatively assess tumor type-dependent CAF-like activation in co-culture spheroids. Spheroids composed of MRC-5 fibroblasts and cancer cells (A549, HepG2, and PANC-1) were reproducibly generated with defined cell composition. Co-culture with cancer cells induced CAF-like activation across all three models, as confirmed by increased α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression and elevated transforming growth factor-β secretion. Collagen I and Collagen IV immunostaining showed that extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling was most pronounced in PANC-1 spheroids, consistent with the desmoplastic characteristics of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. In contrast, HepG2 co-culture spheroids exhibited the greatest increase in interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-8 secretion, suggesting a stronger inflammatory component of fibroblast activation. Gemcitabine dose−response analysis showed higher AUC values under co-culture conditions across all three cancer models, indicating an overall reduction in GEM efficacy. The magnitude of the altered GEM response varied among the cancer models alongside distinct patterns of stromal activation. These findings indicate that this platform enables systematic evaluation of tumor type−dependent stromal responses and provides a quantitative framework for tumor microenvironment-informed preclinical drug screening.

title: Stress-Redistributing Elastomer-Infiltrated Porous OMIEC Networks for Mechanically Robust Organic Electrochemical Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stretchable organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) require mechanically robust organic mixed ionicelectronic conductors (OMIECs) that can maintain stable ion-electron coupling under large mechanical deformation. However, although porous OMIEC architectures are advantageous for enhancing ion transport and deformability, they remain mechanically vulnerable because deformation-induced stress concentrates at pore-interconnecting regions, triggering crack initiation and propagation. Here, we develop an elastomer-infiltrated porous semiconductor (EIPS) strategy to reinforce mechanically fragile OMIEC films through the formation of an interpenetrating semiconductor-elastomer network. Ordered porous OMIEC films are constructed via a hydrophobic-additive-assisted breath-figure assembly, followed by elastomer infiltration to enable efficient mechanical load transfer and stress redistribution throughout the porous framework. Finite-element analysis reveals that elastomer infiltration homogenizes tensile stress distribution, reduces stress concentration at pore walls, and delays crack evolution during deformation. Consequently, the crack-onset strain increases substantially from 14.0 ± 4.2% for bare porous OMIEC films to 44.0 ± 4.2% for EIPS films, enabling EIPS OECTs to remain operational at a maximum tested tensile strain of 80%. Furthermore, the EIPS-based OECT platform demonstrates reliable bioelectronic functionalities, including non-invasive glucose sensing and electrophysiological signal monitoring, under mechanically deformed conditions. These results establish elastomer infiltration as an effective interface-engineering strategy for constructing mechanically resilient OMIEC architectures and advancing robust stretchable organic bioelectronics.

title: Metamaterial Absorbers Based on Deep Learning Inverse Design and MXene Ink
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional metamaterial absorber design suffers from reliance on manual experience, lengthy optimization cycles, and high computational costs. This paper proposes an intelligent method that integrates deep learning-based inverse design with MXene ink. First, by building a ternary MXene/PEDOT:PSS/CB conductive network, a functional ink was created that combines high conductivity with compatibility for screen printing, making high-precision manufacturing of complex metamaterial structures possible. Second, a dataset mapping structural topology to electromagnetic response was built through automated CST simulations, and a deep-learning surrogate model combining a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention mechanism was adopted. By extracting spatial topological features from the encoded metamaterial structure and using the SE module to amplify key feature channels, the model achieved high-precision electromagnetic response prediction (R2 = 0.93). Third, coupling this surrogate model with a genetic algorithm (GA) enabled automated inverse optimization, yielding an optimal structure with a −10 dB zero-order specular reflection band from 5.1 to 14.0 GHz and a minimum reflection loss of −20 dB. Experimental samples fabricated via screen printing demonstrated a measured −10 dB specular reflection band from 6.2 to 15.6 GHz, providing preliminary experimental validation of the proposed design strategy. Owing to this versatile design, our study offers a promising route for creating low-cost, high-performance electromagnetic absorbers.

title: Homocysteine Thiolactone-Derived Polymeric Ionic Liquids for Nanoparticle Stabilization: Unlocking Synergistic Antimicrobial Effects
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study reports the synthesis, chiral resolution, and functionalization of homocysteine thiolactone-derived polymeric ionic liquids (PILs), prepared in racemic and enantiopure forms and subsequently employed as stabilizing matrices for silver and gold nanoparticles (AgNP-rac-PIL and AuNP-rac-PIL). The chiral PILs exhibited higher glass transition temperatures and distinct thermal and structural organization compared to the racemic analogue. AgNP-rac-PIL composites formed uniform ∼5 nm nanoparticles with strong polymer–metal interactions, whereas AuNP-rac-PIL required higher polymer ratios to generate monodisperse ∼6 nm nanoparticles. FTIR, NMR, thermal analysis, and XRD confirmed coordination-driven stabilization of both metals, with more extensive binding observed for AuNP-rac-PIL. Biological evaluation revealed that AgNP-rac-PIL significantly enhanced antibacterial activity relative to the neat PIL, displaying synergistic effects particularly against E. coli and S. aureus. In contrast, AuNP-rac-PIL showed limited enhancement and behaved primarily as a polymer carrier. Checkerboard assays demonstrated pronounced synergy between rac-PIL and ampicillin and between AgNP-rac-PIL and ampicillin at low concentrations, consistent with complementary mechanisms involving increased membrane permeability and β-lactam-mediated inhibition of cell-wall biosynthesis. Overall, these findings highlight AgNP-rac-PIL composites as promising antimicrobial platforms and demonstrate the potential of combining PIL-based materials with conventional antibiotics to enhance therapeutic efficacy.

title: Gastric Fluid-Triggered Double-Network Hydrogel Tape with Enhanced Wet Adhesion for Gastric Perforation Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogel adhesives have emerged as a highly promising material in the field of gastric perforation repair due to their ease of use, ability to rapidly close wounds, and excellent biocompatibility. However, the uniquely harsh acidic environment of the stomach (pH ≈ 1.2) significantly compromises the adhesion performance of conventional hydrogel bioadhesives, often leading to rapid failure and limiting their clinical applicability for gastric injury repair. Here, we developed a sodium alginate/polyacrylamide/chitosan (SPAC) hydrogel tape. Upon contact with gastric fluid, the acidic environment promotes structural reorganization of the SPAC hydrogel tape, leading to the formation of a denser and reinforced network structure. This enhances its adhesion strength and mechanical strength, thereby reducing the adverse effects of the extreme gastric acid environment on the hydrogel. Furthermore, the SPAC hydrogel exhibits excellent adhesion and mechanical properties, as well as good biocompatibility. A mouse model of gastric perforation has demonstrated that this hydrogel can suppress inflammatory responses and promote angiogenesis to facilitate tissue regeneration, providing a highly promising platform for the treatment of gastric perforation.

Cost-carbon preference reversals between new and second-life batteries in stationary storage: a long-horizon comparative framework
abstract: This paper develops a transparent, replacement-aware framework for comparing new battery systems (NBS) and second-life batteries (SLBs) in stationary-storage portfolios over a 30-year horizon. Five fixed portfolio compositions, three utilization profiles, and three grid‑carbon trajectories are evaluated using asset-side cost and carbon metrics. Unlike a pointwise techno-economic or environmental comparison, the framework is organized around the identification of conditional preference boundaries and the assessment of their robustness. The deterministic reference cases are complemented by alternative degradation and operation-and-maintenance formulations, a corrected replacement-threshold analysis, alternative first-life carbon-allocation and end-of-life conventions, two-parameter interaction maps, and a 10,000-sample simultaneous uncertainty analysis. The economic preference pattern remains unchanged across the tested structural formulations: SLB has the lowest asset-side levelized cost of storage under low and medium utilization, whereas NBS becomes preferable under high utilization. Under simultaneous uncertainty, the frequency with which SLB attains a lower asset-side cost decreases from 67.49% under low utilization to 40.66% under high utilization. The environmental ranking is more sensitive to the adopted accounting boundary. The reuse-oriented cutoff convention favors SLB across much of the reference space, but the preference can reverse when part of the first-life manufacturing burden and the end-of-life treatment of retired cohorts are included. The main contribution is therefore an integrated framework for identifying and robustness-testing economic and environmental preference boundaries between NBS and SLB, rather than prescribing a universally superior storage technology.

title: Umbilical cord structure shapes feto-maternal heat transfer across mammals
abstract: The umbilical cord varies widely across placental mammals, yet the functional consequences of this structural diversity remain unclear. We compared cord anatomy across 130 mammal species, reconstructed ancestral states, and combined multimodal imaging with physics-based modeling of oxygen and heat transfer. Reconstructions indicate that the ancestral umbilical cord was uncoiled, with three vessels and an allantoic duct; the human combination of coiling with loss of the duct is rare. Across species, vessel number, duct persistence, and cord length increase with birth weight. Modeling predicts that oxygen delivery remains near maximal across architectures but that placental heat loss depends more strongly on umbilical flow and on cord length and coiling, suggesting more efficient cooling in larger mammals. Microscopy and ultrasound imaging reveal geometric vessel layouts, including a human triple helix, consistent with configurations predicted to reduce intervessel heat shunting. As fetuses must dissipate heat through the mother, these results link cord morphology, evolution, and fetal thermal resilience.

title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus
                    Orthopneumovirus
                    ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the
                    SH
                    viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

title: Multimodal robotic matter enabled by unified magnetic control primitives
abstract: Robotic matter seeks to achieve collective functionality through interactions among modular units governed by global control signals. A persistent challenge is identifying control frameworks that are simultaneously scalable and deterministic. Here, we introduce a unified magnetic control paradigm that enables multimodal robotic matter using a minimal set of global-field primitives. We show that combinations of rotating and pulsed uniform fields, together with controlled field gradients, are sufficient to generate diverse behaviors—including multimodal locomotion, deterministic bottom-up assembly, and rapid, reversible shape morphing in origami-inspired modular robots. Each module incorporates permanent magnets with prescribed chirality and magnetic moment, encoding mechanical and magnetic asymmetries that map global field inputs to predictable forces, torques, and deformation pathways. Using a programmable three-dimensional Helmholtz coil system, we demonstrate four locomotion modes (rolling, steering, sliding, and walking), hierarchical assembly of three-dimensional robotic architectures, and millisecond-timescale transitions among discrete stable states, with applications to origami state machines and global shape change for navigation through confined spaces. By unifying locomotion, assembly, and reconfiguration within a single control framework, this work establishes a generalizable approach to magnetic robotic matter in which multifunctional collective behaviors emerge from a minimal set of control primitives.

title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep
abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual–auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory–visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

title: Historical evidence that wildfire frequency modulates debris-flow hazards through sediment-supply limitation
abstract: Southern California is an epicenter of postwildfire debris flows. In this region, steep topography, frequent fire, heavy rainstorms, and large populations along the wildland-urban interface conspire to produce costly debris flows. Wildfire frequency in the region has tripled in recent decades, causing concern about escalating debris-flow hazards. Here, we investigate how wildfire frequency affects the magnitude of postfire erosion by analyzing long-term debris basin records. We identify two contrasting erosional styles. In steep catchments, erosion exhibits a binge-purge behavior: Erosion for 3 years following fire exceeds background rates by ∼17×. In contrast, in low-sloping, soil-mantled catchments, sediment export following fire only exceeds background rates by ∼1.5×. Critically, in the steep catchments, debris-flow volumes decline when wildfires recur more frequently than the ∼30-year interval characteristic of the past century. This observation suggests a sediment-supply limitation in which more frequent wildfire may reduce, rather than amplify, some of Southern California’s most severe debris-flow hazards.

title: Life-saving cancer drug pumped out by a plant
abstract: In a proof-of-concept study, scientists have coaxed a tobacco-related plant to synthesize the chemotherapy drug paclitaxel.

title: Brain area’s mysterious role in speech decoded at last
abstract: Wernicke’s area is known for processing spoken words, but brain recordings reveal that it also makes a crucial contribution to a related cognitive task.

title: Ultra-generalized hologram synthesis via domain-adaptive wavefront learning
abstract: Deep learning–based computer-generated holography is essential for creating lifelike three-dimensional (3D) visuals in extended reality and immersive human-digital interaction. However, current data-driven approaches predominantly rely on a 3D-solution search strategy that couples scene representation with physical parameters. This paradigm leads to physical overfitting, restricting models to fixed wavelengths and depths and preventing generalization across diverse 3D data formats. Here, we report a 2D-solution search technique, wavefront-aware neural encoding (WNE). This method is a universal framework that overcomes these limitations via domain-adaptive wavefront learning. By compensating for feature distribution shifts induced by varying data formats and physical parameters, WNE maps various wavefronts into a unified feature domain compatible with a frozen, pretrained encoder. This mechanism enables ultra-generalized hologram synthesis: A single pretrained network can encode high-fidelity phase-only holograms for diverse 3D representations, from conventional layer-based data to emerging Gaussian splatting. Outperforming previous analytical and neural encoding methods in image quality, WNE establishes a robust, plug-and-play engine for diverse holographic applications.

title: Creating Biomimetic Ionic Channels in COF‐Based Electrolytes for Large‐Deformation Electrochemical Actuation Under Ultralow Voltage
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical actuators for real‐world applications impose high requirements on the ion transport efficiency of the electrolyte membranes. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), with their long‐range ordered structures and customizable functional groups, hold great promise as the next‐generation ion‐transport units. Inspired by the ion channels in biological membranes, we propose a novel solid‑state electrolyte membrane featuring stable COF‐based ionic channels. COF materials possess the precise hexagonal nanostructure (diameter 2.5–3.3 nm) capable of accommodating large‑sized cations, which endows the electrochemical actuator with high capacitance (88.9 mF cm −2 ) and ionic conductivity (5.4 mS cm −1 ). Based on its favorable mechanical stability, the actuator exhibits a high peak displacement of 24.9 mm at 0.1 Hz, up to 0.89% bending strain, a broad frequency range (0.05–35 Hz), and excellent durability (3 H. Furthermore, leveraging the ultralow‑voltage actuation characteristic, various integrated actuation units with high spatial degrees of freedom are developed by incorporating Bluetooth wireless control modules. This study offers a theoretical basis and a case reference for developing COF‐based high‐performance actuators, providing insights for the future design of soft actuators with functional materials.

abstract: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

title: Molecular resolution fluorescence imaging: from Abbe to Ångström
abstract: This Review highlights how optical strategies, fluorophore photophysics, labeling chemistry, sample preparation and image analysis advance fluorescence microscopy towards molecular resolution and Ångström-scale precision.

title: Uterine-derived anisotropic compressive force specifies the anterior-posterior axis orientation in the mouse embryo
abstract: The establishment of the anterior-posterior (A-P) axis is a fundamental process in embryonic patterning. In mice, directional migration of the anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) determines the A-P axis, yet the cues directing migration remain elusive. Here, we show that anisotropic compression directs AVE migration toward the minor-axis end of the deformed embryo, using ex utero culture with controlled compression and in utero pharmacological manipulations of uterine mechanics. This compression induces localized accumulation of basement membrane (BM) components, including COLLAGEN IV, which directs the AVE toward the minor-axis end. Mathematical modeling demonstrates that BM density-dependent AVE-BM adhesion accounts for the observed AVE dynamics. Our findings reveal that the maternal mechanical environment provides directional cues for cell migration, bridging tissue-scale mechanics and biochemical patterning during body axis specification.

title: DAS reveals continuous, multicore architecture of the Alpine Fault, New Zealand
abstract: The Alpine Fault accommodates much of the relative motion between the Australian and Pacific plates in southern New Zealand and is expected to produce large earthquakes in coming decades. How slip evolves and what ground motions are produced during the next rupture are expected to depend strongly on the continuity of principal slip zones and overall fault width. Despite extensive study, the along-strike structure of the fault and its continuity across segment boundaries remain poorly constrained. Here, we use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) along a 30-kilometer fiber-optic array crossing the Alpine Fault to record fault-zone guided waves (FZGWs) from local earthquakes. The FZGW observations, supported by numerical modeling and passive seismic imaging, reveal up to six narrow (∼10 meters) fault cores embedded within a 200-meter-wide low-velocity zone interpreted as the fault’s inner damage zone. The principal fault core feature persists for ∼180 kilometers along strike between the Central and South Westland segments, crossing a pronounced geometric and kinematic boundary. The inferred damage zone width is consistent with empirical scaling for large-displacement faults. These results demonstrate that DAS can resolve fault-zone architecture at previously inaccessible scales and bridge geological and geophysical inferences, providing constraints on fault continuity, slip localization, and the potential for multisegment rupture in mature plate-boundary systems.

title: Mantle redox states reveal contrasting styles of late Archean lithospheric subduction
abstract:
Lithospheric recycling has operated through most of Earth’s history, likely involving subduction since the late Archean. However, the thermal structure and geometry of such subduction systems remain poorly constrained. Here, we quantify the oxygen fugacity (
                    f
                    O
                    2
                    ) of mantle sources modified by recycled supracrustal materials in the North China Craton. By integrating mantle
                    f
                    O
                    2
                    estimation, thermodynamic simulation of lithospheric structures, and other geological constraints, we infer two styles of lithospheric subduction with contrasting slab-dip angles. The dominant style shows shallow slab-dip angles, a more reduced arc mantle and a thick overriding lithosphere. The subsidiary, localized style exhibits relatively steep slab-dip angles, a more oxidized mantle source and a thinner overriding lithosphere. In contrast to the prevalence of steep subduction on the modern Earth, flat (or shallow) subduction profoundly shaped the distinctive tectonic evolution of the early Earth, whereas the localized development of steep subduction may have enhanced mantle oxidation and strengthened coupling between Earth’s deep interior and surface environments.

title: Magnetic proximity effect in nanoparticle–molecule hybrids enables room-temperature circularly polarized luminescence
abstract: Achieving room-temperature circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from achiral emitters is challenging because it usually requires elaborate molecular chirality engineering. Now magnetic proximity effects in nanoparticle–molecule hybrids enable field-tunable CPL through interfacial spin transfer, offering a route to molecular chiroptics and spintronic applications.

title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
abstract:
Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high-
                    Z
                    interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

title: Lanthanide and Carbon Dot Hybrids (Ln&CDs) for Sensing: A Unified Structure–Synthesis–Application Framework and Rational Design Toolbox
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide ions possess sharp emission, large Stokes shifts, and long fluorescence lifetimes, yet suffer from low absorptivity and severe aqueous quenching. The integration of lanthanides and carbon dots (CDs) combines their respective merits and overcomes individual drawbacks, endowing the hybrid with synergistic optical properties and versatile functions. However, a comprehensive understanding of the structure–property–function relationships in Ln&CDs remains lacking. This review systematically categorizes and summarizes the electronic configuration characteristics, specific sensing properties, and mechanisms of action of core lanthanide elements such as La, Ce, Eu, Tb, and Gd. It focuses on recent advances in Ln&CDs for fluorescence sensing, with an emphasis on underlying mechanisms such as energy transfer, surface coordination, and ratiometric signal regulation. Particularly, based on the three structural binding modes of Ln‐CDs, Ln@CDs, and Ln/CDs, it examines the patterns by which different preparation methods regulate the microstructure and sensing performance of the materials. The relationships between structural design, photophysical properties, and sensing performance are systematically discussed. In addition, representative applications in environmental monitoring, food safety, and biomedical applications are summarized. These insights are expected to accelerate the development of next‐generation intelligent sensing systems.

title: Xeno‐Free Peptide‐Functionalized Hydrogels Support hiPSC Encapsulation and In Situ Differentiation Into Cardiomyocytes With Enhanced Structural Maturation
abstract: ABSTRACT While defined synthetic substrates can replace Matrigel for human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) culture and hiPSC–derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC‐CM) production, existing approaches culture cells on two‐dimensional surfaces and yield structurally immature cardiomyocytes, limiting their use in disease modeling and regenerative medicine. Here, we developed a xeno‐free, fully defined cyclic RGD (cRGD)‐functionalized alginate platform in which we encapsulated hiPSCs to support their expansion and in situ cardiac differentiation. cRGD functionalization was essential for hiPSC survival and pluripotency, with maximal support achieved at a low ligand density (25 µM). In the presence of cRGD, hiPSC encapsulation into softer gels made from lower molecular weight alginates led to enhanced hiPSC expansion and improved cardiogenesis. Strikingly, differentiation in situ within 3D gels led to hiPSC‐CMs with higher structural maturity, including a markedly increased proportion of cardiomyocytes positive for the structural maturation markers Desmin and MYH7. Finally, after enzymatic retrieval from hydrogels, cardiomyocytes derived from softer gels formed tissue‐engineered myocardium with superior contractile stress compared to tissue fashioned from hiPSC‐CMs derived from more rigid gels. Together, these results demonstrate the promise of this defined, tunable platform for biomanufacturing of structurally more mature cardiomyocytes from hiPSCs.

title: Self‐Propelling Nitric Oxide‐Releasing Nanoraft for Nonpharmaceutical Amelioration of Vascular Dementia
abstract: ABSTRACT Vascular dementia (VD) has emerged as a growing global health concern, posing substantial threats to human well‐being. Currently, there are no effective pharmacological treatment strategies available for VD. This disease is primarily attributed to cerebrovascular dysfunction, including thrombosis and severe hypoperfusion. In this study, we rationally design the self‐propelling nanorafts aimed at improving cerebral blood supply for VD therapy. These biocompatible nanorafts, denoted as CBNRs, are co‐assembled from the pyroelectric covalent organic frameworks (TPAD‐COFs) and the nitric oxide (NO) donor (BNN6), exhibiting exceptional pyroelectric/photothermal conversion efficiency, thermally activated NO release, and controllable motion under near‐infrared (NIR) laser irradiation. In both thrombus and VD animal models, the engineered self‐propelling nanorafts exerted synergistic therapeutic effects: NO‐propelled penetration into blood clots in combination with pyroelectric/photothermal thrombolysis induced by NIR laser irradiation, thereby achieving effective thrombolysis and restoring blood flow. Furthermore, the vasodilatory effect of NO enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of CBNRs. As anticipated, the engineered nanorafts markedly mitigated cerebral white matter lesions and reduced hippocampal neuronal cell death. Additionally, behavioral and cognitive impairments in VD model animals were significantly alleviated after administration with NO‐driven pyroelectric nanorafts. This study presents a paradigm for developing self‐propelling nanorafts as an effective therapeutic intervention for VD.

title: AI‐Based Generative Search for New Altermagnetic Candidates With Large Spin Splitting
abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnets combine zero net magnetization with momentum‐dependent spin splitting, yet materials exhibiting sizable spin splitting remain scarce. Herein, a high‐throughput discovery workflow is presented that integrates diffusion‐based crystal generation with targeted screening and first‐principles validation to identify new altermagnet candidates beyond existing databases. Starting from 51 200 generated structures, candidates are downselected using an artificial intelligence‐based classifier, composition filters, novelty and uniqueness checks, and a symmetry‐compatibility test. The altermagnetic ground state is then validated through density functional theory (DFT)+ total energy comparisons among competing magnetic configurations. This workflow yields eight new altermagnets and their spin splittings are quantified and benchmarked against 90 known altermagnets from MAGNDATA, identifying () and () as particularly strong candidates. Thermodynamic stability and tolerance‐robust novelty assessments suggest that the final candidates include (meta)stable and potentially synthesizable phases. Phonon and elastic‐stiffness calculations further support dynamical and mechanical stability for most of the candidates. These results demonstrate that integrating generative models with targeted screening and DFT validation enables efficient discovery of nontrivial altermagnets.

title: Reconciling the surface and bulk oxygen vacancies in ITO for efficient inverted perovskite solar cells
abstract: Indium tin oxide is not merely a passive transparent substrate in inverted perovskite solar cells but actively participates in buried-interface formation through its oxygen-vacancy chemistry. By reconciling surface and bulk oxygen vacancies in ITO, this work couples robust self-assembled monolayer anchoring with favorable interfacial energetics, enabling efficient and stable devices through transparent-electrode defect engineering.

title: Dynamic stress release via a mechano-photoisomerizable molecule for robust flexible perovskite/organic tandem solar cells
abstract: We developed a dynamic reversible stress-release strategy based on a mechano-photoisomerizable spiropyran molecule (SPMA) for mechanically robust flexible perovskite/organic TSCs. SPMA simultaneously induced the preferential (100) orientation, reduced intrinsic lattice strain, and facilitated continuous external stress dissipation. The resulting flexible perovskite/organic TSC achieved a record efficiency of 25.87% (certified 25.29%) and excellent mechanical stability.

title: GDF15 impacts chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss through distinct mechanisms
abstract:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by anorexia, cachexia, and inflammation, which collectively contribute to poor clinical outcomes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a pivotal role for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) in CKD morbidities. Deteriorating renal function and clinical disease status correlates with GDF15 levels in plasma and kidneys of CKD patients. In a mouse CKD model, GDF15 levels are elevated and

                    ) mice recapitulate these phenotypes. Metabolic cage studies reveal that the weight loss-protection effects are primarily attributed to increased food intake. Intriguingly, pair-fed

Transcriptome analysis suggests that GDF15 may act through both GFRAL-dependent mechanisms on food intake and GFRAL-independent mechanisms that primarily modulate inflammation and metabolic pathways. A monoclonal antibody that neutralizes circulating GDF15 markedly restores food intake and preserves body weight, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting GDF15 in CKD-associated weight loss. Together, these findings demonstrate GDF15-GFRAL as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated weight loss and suggest GFRAL-dependent, food intake-mediated actions of GDF15 and food intake-independent effects that may contribute to renal inflammation and metabolic regulation.

title: Peptide‐Engineered Aqueous Circularly Polarized Luminescence via Supramolecular Self‐Assembly: Design Strategies, Mechanistic Insights, and Biomedical Prospects
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials hold considerable promise for biomedical applications, yet their practical translation requires both high CPL performance and favorable biological properties. Peptides offer a promising platform for meeting these demands through their intrinsic chirality, sequence programmability, stereochemical diversity, and hierarchical self‐assembly, which enable the tailoring of chiral organization and luminescence across multiple length scales. Here, we review recent advances in peptide‐based supramolecular CPL systems in aqueous environments, encompassing dispersed assemblies and hydrogels. We first discuss the design strategies and underlying mechanisms of peptide‐based aqueous CPL systems via supramolecular self‐assembly. Then we highlight current limitations and challenges for rational material design. We finally propose three emerging biomedical prospects and critically examine the challenges in translating peptide‐based aqueous CPL from a material property into functional biological outputs. By highlighting key opportunities and unresolved questions at the interface of chiroptical materials and biomedical applications, this review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of peptide‐based aqueous supramolecular CPL systems, with particular emphasis on molecular design strategies, chirality‐transfer mechanisms, and the potential translation of these systems into CPL‐enabled biomedical applications.

title: Oligodendrocyte ER-phagy restricts excessive myelination by degrading sphingolipid synthases
abstract: Myelination is critical for nervous system function. Numerous signaling pathways have been identified that promote myelin sheath growth, disruption of which can lead to hypomyelination. However, the negative regulators of myelin sheath expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–phagy as a cellular brake on central nervous system myelination that restricts myelin sheath thickness during brain development. ER-phagy is active in oligodendrocytes during myelin membrane expansion and limits the abundance of ER-resident sphingolipid synthases, including ceramide synthase 2 (Cers2). Impairment of ER-phagy accumulates ER, elevates sphingolipid production, drives excessive myelin thickening, and alters social behavior after prolonged juvenile social isolation. Genetic deletion of Cers2, which synthesizes long-chain ceramides essential for sphingolipid biogenesis, rescues the hypermyelination phenotype caused by ER-phagy disruption. Together, our findings establish that ER-phagy–sphingolipid axis represses myelin growth and reveal a mechanistic link between ER homeostasis and myelin production by oligodendrocytes, providing insight into the cellular mechanisms underlying pathological hypermyelination.

title: Peroxynitrite‐Activated Afterglow Imaging of Oxidative Stress in Freely Moving Alzheimer's Disease Mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxidative stress is an important biomarker for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet sensitive and reliable monitoring of oxidative stress in awake, freely moving animals remains a major challenge. Here, we report a peroxynitrite (ONOO − )‐activated afterglow probe, TD‐PON NPs, that monitors oxidative stress in the brains of freely moving AD mice with high sensitivity (limit of detection, 4.6 nM). In TD‐PON NPs, the initiator TD generates singlet oxygen under irradiation, which together with ONOO − activates the afterglow substrate PON to emit bright luminescence. The resulting afterglow enabled imaging through chicken tissue at depths up to 4.0 cm, rapid signal acquisition within 89 ms, and activation under ultralow irradiation power densities down to 0.18 mW/cm 2 . We demonstrate its applicability for distinguishing ONOO − levels between healthy and APP/PS1 AD mice, and tracking an age‐dependent increase of ONOO − in AD mouse brains. Furthermore, the rapid afterglow acquisition of TD‐PON NPs enabled ONOO − mapping in freely moving APP/PS1 AD mice and revealed that anesthesia attenuates brain oxidative stress signals, showing that excitation‐decoupled activatable afterglow probes can report oxidative stress faithfully in awake animals.

title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants’ uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

title: Ultralow‐Temperature Direct Growth of High‐Quality Multilayer h‐BN Films on Diverse Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN) has emerged as a promising dielectric for next‐generation electronics, yet its direct growth on non‐catalytic substrates typically requires prohibitively high growth temperatures. Here, we report a universal O 2 ‐plasma pretreatment strategy combined with plasma‐enhanced chemical vapor deposition that enables direct growth of high‐quality multilayer h‐BN films at ultralow temperatures on diverse dielectric substrates. The O 2 ‐plasma converts the inert substrate surface into an O‐functionalized state, substantially lowering the nucleation barrier and allowing crystallization at temperatures as low as 150°C and even at room temperature on sapphire. At 300°C, the optimized h‐BN films exhibit a narrow Raman full‐width at half‐maximum of 26.7 cm −1 and excellent dielectric performance. The resulting h‑BN/polymer/h‐BN composites function as efficient thermal spreaders, provide robust thermo‐oxidative protection at 400°C, and maintain stable dielectric properties up to 350°C. This work establishes a versatile surface‐engineering route for integrating 2D dielectrics into temperature‐sensitive and flexible electronic platforms.

title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
abstract:
Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4
                    +
                    tumor cells, with CD8
                    +
                    T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8
                    +
                    T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8
                    +
                    T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8
                    +
                    T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8
                    +
                    T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

title: Resolving topological obstructions to vectorial structured field control
abstract: The use of structured matter, such as optical retarders, for vectorial control is a well-established and widely used technique in modern optics, and has driven continued advances in the manipulation of complex, spatially varying vectorial fields. However, achieving arbitrary field conversion typically requires the use of cascaded elements, as intrinsic physical and fabrication constraints fundamentally limit individual devices to a restricted subset of transformations. This results in an overall continuous transformation potentially failing to be continuous at the level of the parameters of the cascade, leading to detrimental engineering consequences such as the introduction of complex, discontinuous aberrations that disrupt important topological properties of the underlying light and matter fields. In this work, we establish a mathematical framework for analyzing the topological difficulties that emerge in the decomposition of an overall transformation into individual layers, and for determining the minimal depth required to overcome them. The strategy introduced provides a general pathway for optimizing designs for vectorial field control and matter field generation, with particular importance for the manipulation of topological phases in optical polarization fields, such as Stokes skyrmions, where continuity is of vital importance.

title: Deciphering the Electron‐Donating Effect in Cosolvent Chemistry to Engineer Weak Interactions for High‐Performance Aqueous Potassium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous potassium ion batteries (APIBs) are ideal grid‐scale energy storage candidates due to their safety and eco‐friendliness, but their application is limited by defective electrolyte stability. The cosolvent strategy is attractive but lacks fundamental insights into how solvent properties correlate with electrochemical performance, leaving electrolyte design largely experience‐dependent. Herein, we propose an electron‐donating ability‐guided cosolvent screening principle to tailor components' electrostatic interactions. Weakly electron‐donating cosolvents attenuate cation–solvent coordination, promoting an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase on the anode while suppressing transition metal dissolution at the cathode. Additionally, weakened hydrogen bonds of water–solvent effectively strengthen O─H bonds, thereby inhibiting water decomposition. These multiple optimizations yield a non‐flammable electrolyte with a low concentration of 3.9 mol kg −1 and a 3.9 V electrochemical stability window. This designed electrolyte enables the simultaneous compatibility of a high‐capacity Mn‐rich Prussian blue cathode and KTi 2 (PO 4 ) 3 anode for the first time. The assembled full cell delivers a high energy density of 124 Wh kg −1 , an average discharge voltage above 2 V, stable cycling for 65 000 cycles, and operation from −40°C to +60°C. A 2.3 mAh cm −2 pouch cell achieves 5000 stable cycles with 81.5% capacity retention at 3 C, paving a promising way for developing practical APIBs.

title: Misremembered social networks are predictions of the future in disguise

title: TREX1 and TREX2 3′ → 5′ DNA exonucleases enhance the fidelity of translesion synthesis by DNA polymerase θ
abstract:
A multiplicity of translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases (Pols) promote replication through DNA lesions in an error-free or error-prone manner. Among these Pols, Polθ operates in an error-prone manner. However, Polθ conducts TLS in human cells in a much more error-free manner than implicated from the high error-proneness of the purified Pol. To resolve this incongruity, here we show that the TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonucleases are integral components of TLS mediated by Polθ. In TREX1- or TREX2-deficient cells, Polθ-dependent TLS becomes nonoperational and chromosomal instability rises similar to that in Polθ-deficient cells. Consequently, similar to that in Polθ

                    mice,
                    
                      trex2
