                    mice exhibit increased susceptibility to ultraviolet-induced skin cancers. Furthermore, our findings that in the absence of TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonuclease activities, Polθ-mediated TLS manifests high mutagenicity, and an increase in the diversity of misincorporated nucleotides demarcate a crucial role of these exonucleases in the removal of Polθ misinsertions and, thereby, in enhancing Polθ TLS fidelity and the consequent genome stability.

title: Soft Crosslinked‐Interface‐Enabled Excellent Strain Tolerance Capacity for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Emerging skin‐like flexible electronics are essential elements of soft wearable and biomedical equipment. Traditional physically stacked configurations of electronic devices tend to interlayer separation under high‐degree or cyclic deformations, attributed to the mismatch of mechanical properties between adjacent semiconductor layers, which causes device instability and failure. Here, we present a universal soft crosslinked‐interface strategy to notably improve the strain tolerance capacity for flexible electronics, which involves the establishment of a dissipative interfacial covalent‐crosslinking network between adjacent semiconductor layers. By incorporating the crosslinkable fluid plasticizer polyurethane acrylate (PUA) and polyethylene glycol dimethyl diacrylate (PEGA) into the poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) hole transport layer (HTL) and Super Yellow (SY) emissive layer in flexible polymer light‐emitting diodes (PLEDs), an in situ interfacial crosslinked network is achieved via thermal treatment, enabling high interfacial toughness to suppress delamination and delocalization of strain. This interface functions as a mechanical anchor with an adhesion strength of ∼382 kPa, markedly enhanced relative to the control. These interfacial networks substantially improve charge injection to enhance the electroluminescence performance (∼65%) with a maximum brightness of ∼30 000 cd m −2 . Finally, flexible PLEDs based on this architecture demonstrate ultra‐ stable mechanical and optoelectronic performance under applied mechanical stress. Therefore, establishing crosslinked interlayer interfaces is a universal strategy to fabricate flexible electronic devices.

title: Continuously aligned biomimetic sites in MXene membranes for rapid lithium extraction
abstract:
Efficient separation of lithium ions (Li
                    +
                    ) from magnesium ions (Mg
                    2+
                    ) remains a central challenge for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brines due to their similar physicochemical properties. Inspired by biological ion channels, biomimetic membranes have been explored to improve Li
                    +
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    separation. However, most biomimetic membranes focus primarily on introducing recognition sites while overlooking the structural features of biological channels, particularly the continuous arrangement of coordination sites that facilitates efficient ion transport. Here, inspired by the continuous carbonyl coordination structure of the KcsA ion channel, 4-formylbenzo-15-crown-5 ether was periodically grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) chains and integrated with MXene nanosheets to construct two-dimensional interlayer channels with continuously aligned crown ether recognition sites. This architecture shifts Li
                    +
                    transport from random diffusion to successive site-to-site hopping, reducing the effective transport energy barrier. The resulting biomimetic MXene membrane achieves a Li
                    +
                    flux of 0.12 mol·m
                    −2
                    ·h
                    −1
                    with Li
                    +
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    selectivity of 109 and performs effectively across various salt lake brines.

title: Unseen but not unheard: Animal-borne audio recorders reveal missing interactions between seabirds and untracked vessels
abstract: Quantifying interactions between marine megafauna and vessels is key to assessing the ecological impacts of commercial fishing and shipping. Automatic identification systems (AIS), by publicly tracking global vessel activities, have enabled animal-vessel interactions to be identified at scale. However, the extent of these interactions is inevitably underestimated due to “unseen” vessels that lack AIS or have gaps in coverage from technical issues or intentional disabling. Using animal-borne audio recorders on three seabird species (northern gannet, Balearic shearwater, and Westland petrel), we investigated whether acoustic detection of vessel sounds could reveal a more complete picture of interactions. We found that a striking proportion of vessel audio detections (gannets, >32%, estimated 57%; shearwaters, >12%, estimated 20%) could not be matched with AIS-tracked vessels, suggesting substantial potential for bycatch risk from unseen fishing. Our approach is computationally lightweight, applicable to pre-existing datasets, and transferrable to non-seabird taxa. Acoustic detection could improve future assessments of animal-vessel interactions and unseen vessel activities to support marine conservation.

title: Climate change signals for adaptation action
abstract: Signals of climate change measured in physical and ecological systems are salient for adaptation, but are not currently directly usable. This Perspective aims to better connect early warning signals of climate change with the needs of adaptation planning and decision-making.

title: Frequent co-occurring atmospheric phenomena amplify precipitation extremes
abstract: Observations and simulations show that concurrent atmospheric phenomena (CAP) dominate the greenhouse gas-driven amplification of extreme precipitation from 1980 to 2020. This increased frequency of CAP-related precipitation extremes accounts for 56–70% of extreme precipitation increases projected for 2060–2100 in Northern Hemisphere hotspots, driven by oceanic high-pressure anomalies that strengthen land–sea pressure gradients, alongside enhanced moisture convergence.

title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
abstract:
Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the
                    mdx
                    mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

title: A precipitation threshold delineates contrasting controls on global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization
abstract:
Nitrogen fertilization is a major driver of soil acidification globally, yet its independent effects on soil pH and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly resolved. Here we isolate the contribution of nitrogen fertilization by compiling the largest paired experimental dataset to date, consisting of 3564 paired soil pH observations under control and nitrogen fertilization treatments across seven major ecosystem types worldwide. By constructing robust machine-learning models, we predict global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization (pH_T) and quantify fertilization-associated pH change under a standardized hypothetical fertilization scenario. Under this scenario, we estimate that 96.27% of global soils undergo acidification, with a mean pH decline of 0.34 units. Critically, we identify a precipitation threshold at ∼900 mm year
                    −1
                    that separates two distinct regimes in the relationship between precipitation and pH_T: climate-driven leaching and buffering in drier regions versus soil-mediated internal regulation in humid regions. This threshold demonstrates that the association between precipitation and pH_T is not uniform across the global precipitation gradient but varies markedly among hydroclimatic regions. Our results provide a global outlook on soil pH responses to nitrogen fertilization, supporting acidification risk early warning, precision fertilizer management, and sustainable agricultural development.

title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss
abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic’s fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave–mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

title: Molecular locking of lithium ions for improved efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells
abstract: Spiro-OMeTAD is a common hole-transporting material in n–i–p perovskite solar cells but suffers from instabilities caused by mobile lithium dopant ions. Pan et al. incorporate a molecular locking additive in Spiro-OMeTAD, enhancing both the efficiency and stability of devices.

title: Regulation of proton transference for stable and efficient reactive capture of CO2 from air
abstract: Direct air capture integrated with electrosynthesis to produce fuels and chemicals is hindered by high energy consumption and limited operational lifetimes. Here the authors identify proton management as crucial for stability and achieve 1,000 h of stable operation by using gas-fed hydrogen oxidation at the anode, which maintains ideal ion transport and enhances CO production.

title: A Semi-single-crystal Architecture Bridging Polycrystalline and Single-Crystal NCM Cathodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polycrystalline NCM cathodes offer high electrode density and favorable kinetics but suffer from intergranular cracking, whereas single-crystal cathodes improve structural durability at the expense of packing efficiency and transport kinetics. Here, we introduce a semi-single-crystal NCM622 architecture that bridges these competing characteristics by assembling ∼2 μm single-crystalline primary particles within a conventional ∼6–7 μm secondary-particle framework. Retaining this framework preserves high electrode density while reducing the internal grain-boundary network. The enlarged primary particles exhibit reduced intraparticle crystallographic heterogeneity, accompanied by more homogeneous local lattice evolution and suppressed intergranular cracking during high-voltage operation. Consequently, Semi-single achieves superior cycling stability relative to Poly while maintaining comparable relative rate retention at 4.3 V. This architecture offers a structural strategy for balancing mechanical durability, electrode packing, and rate capability without requiring the aggressive pulverization associated with conventional single-crystal cathodes.

title: A flexible fiber–based artificial chemical postsynapse
abstract: Most artificial synapses, which are designed to communicate with biological neural systems and exhibit neuron-like functions, rely primarily on electrical signals. Biotic-abiotic neural interfaces that use artificial synapses to communicate with biological synapses via chemical neurotransmitters while exhibiting synaptic plasticity are of great interest. Here, we present an artificial chemical postsynapse that directly interfaces with biological systems through dopamine (DA) neurotransmitters and demonstrates synaptic plasticity–like behavior. The artificial postsynapse of a flexible fiber–based organic electrochemical transistor (F-OECT) with a capacitive-like charging gate electrode, which combines volumetric charge storage and DA-sensing functionalities, can detect pulsatile DA release and transduce these sensing signals with plasticity-like behavior. The F-OECT synapse emulates key synaptic functions observed in biological synapses by responding to pulse-like DA release from dopaminergic cells. We also implanted fiber-based artificial postsynapses into a mouse brain to study their basic interaction with DA release and to evaluate biocompatibility.

title: Tuning microswimmer motility by liposome encapsulation: A membrane clutch enables controlled swimming and cargo transport
abstract:
Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. Nevertheless, the underlying motility mechanisms from a hydrodynamic perspective are often unresolved, and reliable velocity control remains challenging. In the present study, we use our previously introduced biohybrid system termed the chlamylipo, in which the motile alga
                    Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
                    is encapsulated within a giant liposome, as a model system to investigate how liposome encapsulation regulates microswimmer motility under controlled perturbations. From a fluid mechanical perspective, we establish a deformation-velocity expression that incorporates liposome radius, beating frequency, and membrane protrusion. We further show that motility can be reversibly switched by incorporating light-responsive lipids, with the liposome acting as a “clutch” that modulates membrane protrusion. To demonstrate its transport function, we further show cargo loading, carrying, and triggered release. These results show that liposome encapsulation can convert a motile microorganism into a controllable carrier, with the membrane acting as a clutch that regulates swimming and, therefore, cargo transport.

title: Multimodal Microscopy-Guided Charge Dynamics Modulation via Perovskite Heterointerface Design for Efficient Printable Mesoscopic Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hole-transport-layer-free printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (p-MPSCs) with carbon electrodes offer scalable fabrication, yet their performance is hindered by inefficient hole extraction across thick (∼3 μm), field-free porous scaffolds. Moreover, directly resolving how carriers navigate these buried mesoscopic networks has remained an experimental challenge. Here, we engineer a type-II perovskite/perovskite heterointerface within the p-MPSC via a quantum dot dispersion post-treatment and employ multimodal microscopy—combining hyperspectral, photoluminescence lifetime, and carrier diffusion imaging—with device simulations to map internal carrier dynamics. Rather than acting merely as a conventional back-surface barrier, the heterojunction dictates charge extraction through its exact spatial depth: positioning the heterointerface precisely at the boundary between the illuminated and unilluminated regions maximizes hole separation and transport. This microscopy-guided spatial engineering yields a champion power conversion efficiency of 21.8%, establishing both direct mechanistic insight and a quantitative design principle for next-generation p-MPSCs.

title: An Amorphous Phosphate-Based Chloride Electrolyte for Low-Stacking-Pressure All-Solid-State Sodium Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional inorganic solid electrolytes (SEs) rarely combine sufficient deformability for stable interfacial contact in composite cathodes with high ionic conductivity and low cost, hindering the development of stable all-solid-state sodium batteries (ASSSBs). Herein, we propose a facile chlorination-tailored strategy to overcome this limitation and obtain a low-cost, deformable, amorphous phosphate-based chloride solid electrolyte, Na3Zr2Si1.6PO4Cl14.4. Utilizing SiCl4 as an efficient chlorinating reagent, we transform the rigid oxide units [PO4] into flexible [POxCl4–x] units, accompanied by the generation of [SiClzO4–z]. Owing to the enhanced rotational probability of the chlorinated structural motifs, Na3Zr2Si1.6PO4Cl14.4 delivers a high Na+ conductivity of 2.02 mS cm–1 at 30 °C and a low modulus of 1.8 GPa. The constructed deformable and fast Na+-conductive network within the Na2Fe2(SO4)3-based composite cathode enables an ASSSB with a 4.5 V cutoff to stably operate for over 2000 cycles under a 5 MPa stack pressure.

title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
abstract:
Helicobacter pylori
                    infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
abstract:
Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca
                    2+
                    -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca
                    2+
                    to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca
                    2+
                    cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics
abstract:
Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

title: Global iodine emissions remain near constant over the 21st century
abstract: The reaction between atmospheric ozone and ocean iodide releases gaseous iodine into the atmosphere, destroying ozone and nucleating aerosol particles. The current paradigm is that iodine emissions will substantially increase over this century, with implications for climate, air quality, and human health. Using advanced predictions of ocean iodide concentrations and the iodine emissions function, we re-evaluate this understanding. Rather than increasing through 2100, we find minimal change (−3%) in global iodine emissions compared to present day, predominantly due to a sea surface temperature driven decrease in the iodine emissions function together with relatively unchanged sea surface iodide concentrations. However, emissions increases remain in the critical Arctic region (+143%), resulting in an additional 9 ppbv of springtime surface ozone loss across the region. Our results highlight that predictions of future atmospheric iodine depend on the assumed climate-induced changes in oceanic iodide, in addition to changes in emissions driven by anthropogenic ozone and sea-surface temperature.

title: Surface-passivated high-entropy oxide-derived catalysts for stable dry reforming of methane
abstract:
Dry reforming of methane (DRM) enables the co-valorization of CO
                    2
                    and CH
                    4
                    into syngas, yet the development of sintering- and coking-resistant catalysts that suppress CH
                    4
                    cracking while accelerating coke gasification without compromising reaction efficiency remains a major challenge. Here, we address this challenge by employing surface-passivated catalysts derived from high-entropy oxides (HEOs) for stable DRM operation. Alkaline earth metal cation (M
                    2+
                    )-doped HEOs were designed to function without pretreatment and exhibited resistance to sintering and coking. This robustness arises from the in situ exsolution of NiCuCo alloy nanoparticles encapsulated within a multifunctional BaCO
                    3
                    overlayer, enabled by HEO-stabilized Ba incorporation and Ba-mediated surface reconstruction during DRM. This adaptive architecture passivates deep CH
                    4
                    cracking, promotes CO
                    2
                    activation, accelerates coke gasification, and thereby sustains catalytic efficiency and durability. Comprehensive spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction analyses revealed the structural dynamics and mechanistic pathways governing catalyst evolution under DRM conditions.

title: Evolution of trans-regulatory architecture and gene expression dosage compensation after genome duplication
Signals of rapid genetic change in reef coral over time and following mass mortality
abstract:
Future coral reef persistence amidst accelerating climate change depends on rapid adaptive capacity. Sixteen years (2003 to 2019) of genetic data (
                    N
                     = 903) spanning mass mortality events uncovered polygenic signals of evolution and population structure in one Great Barrier Reef coral species (
                    Acropora tenuis
                    ) and a similar but nonsignificant trend in another (
                    Acropora millepora
                    ). Random forest revealed larger genetic shifts postbleaching compared to other time points, which was further supported by critical transitions in 34 years of remotely sensed thermal data (1985 to 2018). Concordant signals across multiple genomic ordinations confirmed significant shifts postbleaching. Specifically, three genetic variants contributed significantly to key random forest splits over time in
                    A. tenuis
                    . Significant genome-wide covariance in allele frequencies suggests shifts due to selection, not drift. This suggests that coral gene pools are changing, and measurable evolution can happen over subdecadal timescales, giving hope for coral resilience amid the ongoing climate crisis. However, we caution against overoptimism, and stress emissions must be urgently reduced.

title: Rapid intensification of summer convective precipitation in New England
abstract: Anthropogenic warming is intensifying precipitation extremes, yet how subdaily convective rainfall responds in historically stratiform-dominated midlatitude regions remains poorly constrained. Using four decades of hourly station observations and reanalysis data, we show that summer convective precipitation has intensified across much of New England and surrounding regions from 1980 to 2020, with high-intensity events increasing in higher latitudes. Extreme convective rainfall scales at ∼13 to 14% per degree Celsius, nearly twice the Clausius-Clapeyron rate and significantly faster than stratiform precipitation. This intensification is accompanied by shorter event durations, increased moisture convergence, enhanced convective instability, and reduced antecedent soil moisture. Our results indicate a warming-driven shift toward convective dominance linked to changes in midlatitude circulation, reduced meridional temperature gradient, and land-atmosphere coupling, placing New England within an emerging poleward extension of the summer convective regime.

title: Hardware-encoded modality separation for multimodal sensing and artificial perception
abstract: Human skin achieves robust perception by distributing modality-specialized receptors that preferentially encode mechanical and thermal cues. Yet, soft and flexible tactile sensors often suffer from cross-sensitivity, where stretching, bending, and temperature variations generate overlapping electrical readouts that undermine reliable multimodal measurement and downstream artificial intelligence–based interpretation. Here, we present a multimodal piezoresistive platform based on doped silicon nanomembranes that leverages their crystallographic anisotropy and a bilayer differential architecture for front-end modality separation. By integrating [110] longitudinal/transverse gauges with [100] reference gauges that exhibit reduced piezoresistive sensitivity but comparable temperature coefficient of resistance, together with a bilayer differential layout, the platform compensates thermal drift and decouples stretching from bending at the hardware level. Experimental and theoretical analyses establish a quantitative framework for separating modality-specific responses under combined stretching, bending, and temperature stimuli. Integrated into a flexible, wireless platform, the decoupled signals enable real-time transmission and deep learning–based interpretation, allowing accurate identification of geometrically similar objects with distinct thermal or mechanical properties. These results highlight the feasibility and need to co-design front-end sensing architectures and learning models to achieve robust, high-accuracy multimodal decoupling in real-world conditions.

title: Spaceflight reshapes Alzheimer’s disease–associated molecular programs in human brain organoids
abstract:
Spaceflight provides a unique environment to study neural responses relevant to neurodegenerative diseases. Here, human cortical organoids derived from induced pluripotent stem cells that carry familial Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mutations in APP,
                    PSEN1
                    , and
                    PSEN2
                    were cultivated at the International Space Station alongside Controls for 40 days. Multiomic profiling, integrating transcriptomics and proteomics, revealed a coordinated shift in neuronal and cellular states during spaceflight. Spaceflight was associated with changes in amyloid-β processing and tau phosphorylation, although the magnitude of these responses varied across genetic backgrounds. Pathway analysis identified increased synaptic and neurotransmission-related signatures, particularly those associated with GABA-releasing and glutamatergic signaling. Integrative analysis further revealed convergent programs involving RNA processing, chromatin organization, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cellular stress responses. Proteomic and multiomic analyses also identified changes in RNA binding proteins, including CIRBP, consistent with altered posttranscriptional regulatory networks under spaceflight conditions. These exploratory findings indicate that spaceflight reshapes neuronal regulation in human brain organoids, revealing coordinated molecular responses relevant to AD biology.

title: The circSRSF5 -FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition
abstract:
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of
                    circSRSF5
                    . Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for
                    circSRSF5
                    in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly
                    circSRSF5
                    , in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

title: How far are we from a critical salinity in the North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre?
abstract:
The North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre (SPG) can undergo abrupt cooling associated with a loss of deep convection, yet the hydrographic conditions that drive this transition remain uncertain. While some CMIP6 models simulate an abrupt SPG cooling, others do not. Here, we identify a critical sea surface salinity (SSS) that separates these contrasting behaviors. Models without abrupt cooling either remain above this threshold because they project weak freshening or already lie below it under present-day conditions, inconsistent with observations. Observed SSS exceeds the critical threshold by 0.3 to 0.8 g kg
                    −1
                    , depending on the exact threshold definition. Although no declining trend is currently detected, observations remain consistent with models that simulate abrupt cooling. In these models, SSS begins to decline rapidly and crosses the critical threshold about 20 years after the onset of freshening. These results highlight the importance of sustained salinity observations for detecting the approach to this critical threshold, providing a physically based early warning of an abrupt SPG cooling.

title: Errors in social network knowledge predict how ties evolve in the future
abstract:
A notable feature of people’s social knowledge is that it is riddled with errors. These errors, e.g., making mistakes about who are actually friends in a social network, has typically been attributed to cognitive limitations or heuristics that prioritize knowledge of general social patterns over details about specific ties. Here, we demonstrate that such errors instead reflect an adaptive link prediction process that anticipates how the network will evolve far into the future. By longitudinally following a large, real-world social network (
                    n
                     = 196) and tracking the formation and dissolution of social ties over the course of a year, we show that judgments that are wrong in the moment accurately forecast which relationships will emerge or dissolve up to 6 months later. On average, participants’ errors predicted tie formation nearly 3× and tie loss more than 1.2× above chance levels. Beyond the use of simple heuristics like triadic closure and homophily, computational modeling reveals that successful link prediction relies on mental representations of the social network that integrates information about both direct and indirect, long-range ties between individuals. Having a social network representation that is future-oriented yields distinct social advantages: Those who are better able to predict changes in the network become more centrally positioned over time, contingent on their initial position.

title: Dual-cation solvation-tailored electrolyte solutions for low-temperature 48-V/30-Ah lithium-ion battery modules
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution forms a hierarchical primary solvation sheath with a dual-Li+ inner core, enabling stable Li-based battery operation down to −50 °C across coin cells and Ah-scale modules with different electrode chemistries.

title: Ubiquitination of USP5 by a bacterial effector inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation
abstract:
The intracellular pathogen
                    Legionella pneumophila
                    employs a repertoire of effector proteins to manipulate the host ubiquitin signaling and subvert host immune responses. In this study, we reported that the
                    L. pneumophila
                    effector GobX (Lpg2455) functions as a ubiquitin ligase to target the host deubiquitinase USP5. Ubiquitination of USP5 by GobX inhibits its deubiquitination activity. Furthermore, this ubiquitination enhances the interaction between USP5 and the host E3 ligase MARCHF7, thereby facilitating MARCHF7-dependent ubiquitination of NLRP3. This modification targets NLRP3 for autophagic degradation, ultimately suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. Our findings uncover a sophisticated strategy in which a bacterial effector hijacks the host ubiquitination machinery to dampen inflammasome signaling.

title: Characterizing ocean flows with the scattering transform
abstract: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a useful statistical descriptor of these flows, it cannot always distinguish between different types of motion. We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics. Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

title: Tyre wear particles as important contributors to cryosphere darkening
abstract: The abrasion of tyres leads to the emission of particulate matter to the atmosphere. Here the authors quantify the effect that these tyre wear particles have on snow and ice, showing that they contribute to melting in some regions.

title: Hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on off-diagonal Peltier and Ettingshausen effects in a junction-less single material
abstract:
Transverse thermoelectric conversion, which interconverts heat and charge currents in orthogonal directions, is gaining attention as a driving principle for next-generation thermal management devices that do not require dissimilar material junctions or complex module structures. Transverse thermoelectric conversion is driven by various principles stemming from the breaking of structural symmetry or time-reversal symmetry, and substantial performance improvements are anticipated by simultaneously utilizing multiple principles. This study demonstrates hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on multiple phenomena within a junction-less single material. Using an active thermoelectric imaging technique based on lock-in thermography, the charge-to-heat current conversion characteristics in Mg
                    3
                    Bi
                    2
                    crystals showing anisotropic transport properties were visualized and evaluated. We successfully separated the contributions of the off-diagonal Peltier effect due to the electronic structural symmetry breaking and the ordinary Ettingshausen effect due to the time-reversal symmetry breaking under a magnetic field. These contributions operate additively within the same material, leading to the notable enhancement of the transverse thermoelectric conversion performance.

title: Multimodal motion and behavior switching of multistable ciliary walkers
abstract: The collective motion of arrays of cilia—tiny, hairlike protrusions—drives the locomotion of numerous microorganisms, enabling multimodal motion and switching between gaits to navigate complex environments. Inspired by this multimodal motion, we introduce multistable soft walkers with millimeter-scale flexible cilia that buckle under the walkers weight, coupling multistability and actuation within a single physical mechanism. When placed on a vibrating surface, the propulsion direction of ciliary walkers is selected through the buckled states of their cilia, allowing multimodal motion and switching between modes in response to perturbations. We first show that bimodal walkers with left-right symmetric cilia can reverse direction upon encountering obstacles. Next, we demonstrate that walkers with isotropic cilia exhibit both translational and rotational motion and switch between them in response to environmental interactions. At increasing densities, swarms of such walkers collectively transition from predominantly spinning to translational motion. Last, we show that the shape, placement, and number of cilia controls the modes of motion of the walkers. Our results establish a rational, physically grounded strategy for designing minimalist soft robots where complex behaviors emerge from feedback between internal mechanical states and environmental interactions, laying the foundation for soft robotic collectives that operate without onboard sensing or centralized control.

title: Fa‐Jie Chen
abstract: "My long-term goal is to develop "click" methods for peptide cyclization and library construction for high-throughput screening and drug discovery… If I were a piece of lab equipment, I would be a thin-layer chromatography (TLC) plate, because I could be the eyes for chemists to see what is going on in organic reactions…" Find out more about Fa-Jie Chen in his Introducing… Profile.

title: Sustainable Depolymerization of Polyurethane Waste via Base‐Free Catalytic Hydrogenolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyurethane (PU), the sixth most produced polymer globally, poses significant environmental challenges due to its stable cross‐linked structure, which hinders degradation and recycling. Although catalytic hydrogenolysis offers a promising route for recovering valuable monomers, current systems generally require strongly alkaline conditions and homogeneous catalysts, limiting their practical applicability. Herein, we report an efficient base‐free hydrogenolysis system using a supported amorphous molybdenum sulfide catalyst (a‐MoS x /Al 2 O 3 ) for the closed‐loop recycling of PU, achieving recovery rates of 94.6% for aromatic amines and 99.9% for polyols. Mechanistic investigations reveal that abundant sulfur vacancies not only promote the depolymerization of PU to generate isocyanates and polyols, but also catalyze the hydrogenation of isocyanates to amines. This suppresses repolymerization with polyols, ensuring complete depolymerization. The catalyst exhibits broad applicability across diverse PU types and real‐world PU waste, while maintaining its activity after regeneration. This work establishes a sustainable catalytic route for converting PU waste into high‐value monomers.

title: Sequence‐Retentive Upcycling of Polyamide 66 Into Quasi‐Alternating Biodegradable Polyesteramides With Closed‐Loop Recyclability
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyamide 66 (PA66) is a durable engineering plastic with poor biodegradability and limited energy‐efficient recycling options, posing environmental challenges. Herein, we report a sequence‐retentive, one‐pot, two‐step depolymerization‐repolymerization strategy for the upcycling of waste PA66 into biodegradable polyesteramides (PA66‐EX). Rather than depolymerizing PA66 into constituent monomers, adipic acid‐assisted acidolysis selectively converts PA66 into carboxyl‐terminated polyamide oligomers with tunable amide sequence lengths, which are reconnected through ester‐containing segments via in situ melt polycondensation with ethylene glycol. This sequence‐retentive strategy generates quasi‐alternating polyesteramide backbones that preserve PA66‐derived amide‐rich domains while uniformly introducing hydrolysis‐sensitive ester linkages. The resulting PA66‐EX materials combine biodegradability with high thermal and mechanical performance, showing melting temperatures of 180°C–197°C, 5% mass‐loss temperatures above 356°C, tensile strengths of 27–35 MPa, and elongations at break of 414%–745%. Enzymatic degradation increases systematically with ester content, confirming the role of ester linkages as accessible degradation sites. Moreover, PA66‐EX demonstrates polymer‐to‐polymer closed‐loop recyclability, largely retaining its molecular sequence characteristics, thermal properties, and mechanical performance over five consecutive, catalyst‐free hydrolysis‐repolymerization cycles. This work establishes a practical strategy for transforming waste PA66 into high‐performance biodegradable polyesteramides and provides a general sequence‐retentive molecular design principle for achieving circularity in condensation polymers.

title: Biomimetic Reversible Phase Transition in Scandium‐Based Metal Halides for Environment‐Interactive Information Security
abstract: ABSTRACT Inspired by the dynamic adaptive coloration of cephalopods, mimicking their reversible, environment‐interactive response behavior is essential for biomimetic material design. The high color purity, multi‐wavelength tunability, long luminescence lifetimes, excellent stability, and reversible stimuli‐responsive behavior of lanthanide‐based emitters render them indispensable in biomimetic camouflage, intelligent sensing, electronic skin, and adaptive optical materials. In this study, we develop a biomimetic system based on zero‑dimensional Cs 4 ScCl 7 ·H 2 O and its interconvertible counterpart Cs 2 ScCl 5 ·H 2 O via a simple “dissolve–dry” method. Bidirectional phase transitions are achieved by facile alternating ScCl 3 and CsCl treatment. Density functional theory calculations rationalize this phase selectivity and the resultant color switching via a kinetic–thermodynamic competition. Doping with antimony and lanthanide enables self‐trapped exciton emission, downshifting luminescence, and upconversion luminescence, with the capability of reversible cyclic switching upon structural transformation. Utilizing this capability of reversible color switching in response to external stimuli, two complementary applications are demonstrated: physically unclonable function labels for medicines anti‑counterfeiting, and stimuli‑responsive luminescence for dynamic information encryption (integrating dynamic encoding with a secret‐sharing hierarchical authorization framework). Together, these strategies achieve zero‑error authentication and strong cloning resistance. This work establishes rare earth‑based low‑dimensional metal halides as a biomimetic, environment‑interactive system for next‑generation, highly secure anti‑counterfeiting and encryption technologies.

title: Evolution of Color in Highly Transparent Emulsions
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents highly stable, dynamically tunable and transparent colored emulsions. A typical system is formulated with 1‐octadecene droplets (0.5–1.0 µm) dispersed in a water–glycerol (volume ratio of 21:79) continuous phase stabilized by ethylene‐1,2‐bis(dodecyldimethylammonium bromide). By precisely engineering the refractive index matching between the two phases, the emulsion achieves nearly 100% transmittance at the matching wavelength λ c , exhibiting saturated, wavelength‐selective coloration. Owing to the distinct thermo‐optic coefficients (d n /d T ) of the two phases, the macroscopic color reversibly shifts from blue to purple, purplish‐red and orange–yellow ultimately reaching yellow, covering almost the entire visible spectrum between 25°C and 43°C. Composition titration experiments showed the relationship between the macroscopic color shift of the emulsion and the microscopic refractive index matching of the two phases. The scattering efficiency of a single emulsion droplet is calculated based on the van de Hulst approximation. The result reveals that the macroscopic vividness of colors originates from the cumulative scattering effects of a large number of droplets. As water and glycerol can mix in any ratio, this designing principle can not only be successfully applied to other olefins and diverse multi‐component oil combinations, exhibiting exceptional formulation adaptability, but also opens up potential applications for optical filters and sensors.

title: Dense Metalloporphyrin Arrays Enable Binuclear Cooperativity for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is central to clean energy technologies like fuel cells and metal‐air batteries, yet its efficiency relies on costly platinum catalysts. In nature, cytochrome c oxidase achieves efficient ORR at a heme iron‐copper binuclear center, where hydrogen bonding stabilizes key intermediates. Here, by mimicking this concept, we constructed a gallium–pyrazolate framework (Ga‐TPzP) with densely packed Co(II)‐porphyrin arrays. The precise arrangement of these sites at an optimal distance of 6.53 Å creates confined nanoreactors, enabling strong hydrogen bonds between coordinated H 2 O and adsorbed O 2 on two adjacent Co(II) centers. This unique binuclear cooperativity facilitates O 2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier and significantly enhancing the ORR performance. As a cathode in a zinc‐air battery, Ga‐TPzP(Co) achieves a peak power density of 185 mW cm − 2 and can operate steadily for 150 h at 10 mA cm −2 , representing one of the best performance among all reported MOF‐based catalysts for this application.

title: Protein Secondary Structure From Infrared Spectroscopy—Tricks to Use and Traps to Avoid
abstract: ABSTRACT Secondary structure analysis of proteins is one of the major applications of infrared spectroscopy in the life sciences. It requires high quality spectra and their adequate interpretation. This article aims to guide practitioners in generating and interpreting protein infrared spectra, as well as help readers and reviewers assess the quality of the resulting articles. It addresses common problems and mistakes, simple quality criteria and measures for improved spectrum quality and interpretation. Regarding experimental procedures, the text discusses avoidance of water vapor, effects of air bubbles, reduction of noise, and criteria for judging spectrum quality. The secondary structure analysis section focuses on a particular approach in which the amide I region of the spectrum is represented by fitted component bands. The following aspects of the approach are considered: application of band‐narrowing techniques, fitting of spectra, assignment of component bands and the accuracy of secondary structure analysis. The purpose is not to provide a single best practice protocol but to make the reader aware of the implications, limitations, pitfalls, and improvement potentials of the used procedures.

title: Continuous Tuning of Magnetic Bistability via Consecutive Desolvation and Decoupled Structural Phase Transition
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving precise and continuous modulation of magnetic bistability remains a key challenge in advancing the practical utility of molecular magnetic materials. Herein, we exploit the consecutive desolvation and the following decoupled, thermally induced structural phase transition (SPT) to finely regulate the magnetic bistability in a mononuclear Fe III SCO complex. This complex evolves from an abrupt SCO with a transition temperature ( T 1/2 ) of 264 K to a hysteretic two‐step transition ( T 1/2 ↓ = 132 K, T 1/2 ↑ = 155 K, ∆ T = 23 K), and finally to a locked high‐spin (HS) state, which occurs via single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformations. More importantly, a quantitative linear correlation between the SPT progression and the HS/LS ratio is established by fine‐tuning the annealing temperature and duration. This work demonstrates that the consecutive desolvation and decoupled SPT offer a new strategy for the continuous regulation of the key parameters of SCO‐based magnetic bistable materials.

title: Dissociation‐Migration Trade‐Off in Gel Polymer Electrolytes Enables Extreme‐Condition Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) are promising for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) under extreme conditions due to their relatively high ionic conductivity, enhanced safety, and intimate electrode contact. Despite these advantages, how polymer chemistry governs Li + transport and interfacial reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a dissociation‐migration trade‐off principle using GPEs incorporating polymer motifs with distinct Li + affinities, revealing that intermediate polymer–Li + interactions balance carrier generation with Li + migration. The optimized GPE achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.78 mS cm −1 and a Li + transference number of 0.88 at 30°C, while suppressing excessive electrolyte decomposition and promoting stable electrode–electrolyte interphases with reduced organic accumulation and more uniform depth distributions of inorganic components. Consequently, Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cells operate across extreme conditions including −40–80°C, 4.6 V, and 4 C, retaining 80.8% capacity after 1100 cycles at −20°C. Furthermore, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers 342.7 Wh kg −1 and retains 80.3% capacity after 200 cycles. This work provides a molecular framework for the rational design of GPEs that integrate efficient ion transport with interfacial stability.

title: Unlocking Fast and Durable Li + Transport Beyond Polymer Segmental Dynamics for High‐Rate and Long‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer electrolytes are promising for safe lithium metal batteries, yet their ionic transport is fundamentally limited by polymer segmental dynamics, hindering fast charging and long‐term cycling. Here, we report a microphase‐separated quasi‐solid‐state polymer electrolyte that enables rapid and durable Li + transport through localized coordination regulation. Covalently tethered pyrrolidinium ionic liquid moieties promote lithium salt dissociation while suppressing anion migration, whereas in situ generated thioether linkages weaken Li + ‐polymer interactions and enhance chain flexibility. Their synergistic integration creates a dynamic coordination environment that facilitates low‐energy Li + hopping between adjacent coordination sites, substantially reduced ion transport dependence on polymer segmental dynamics. As a result, the optimized electrolyte delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 1.13 mS cm −1 , a high Li + transference number of 0.82, and a low activation energy of 0.17 eV. The accelerated and homogeneous Li + transport promotes stable lithium deposition, enabling lithium metal batteries with 97.9% capacity retention after 2500 cycles at 10C and stable operation for 400 cycles at 5C even at 120°C. More broadly, this work demonstrates a viable pathway to break the conventional trade‐off between polymer processability and ion‐transport kinetics, offering a new paradigm for high‐performance solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Cyanoethyl Cellulose‐Mediated Polymer Electrolyte With Fast Li + Transport and Stable Interface for Long‐Cycle Solid‑State Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are promising for solid‐state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) owing to their safety, flexibility, and processability. However, simultaneously achieving fast Li + transport and stable electrode/electrolyte interface remains a great challenge. Herein, a cyanoethyl cellulose (CEC)‐mediated polymer–polymer modulation strategy is proposed to construct high‐performance Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)/lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) composite electrolyte (PL‐CEC). Functional CEC effectively disrupts the ordered stacking structure of PVDF chains, while abundant polar cyano groups in CEC precisely modulate the local Li + coordination environment, promote Li salt dissociation and fast Li + migration. The optimized PL‐CEC exhibits high room‐temperature ionic conductivity and superior Li + transference number. Moreover, PL‐CEC stabilizes both electrode interfaces, suppressing Li dendrite growth and high‐voltage electrolyte decomposition. Consequently, Li|PL‐CEC|Li cells realize stable Li plating/stripping for 1400 h at 0.4 mA cm −2 and 0.4 mAh cm −2 . Li|PL‐CEC|LiFePO 4 full cells retain 74.2% capacity after 5000 cycles at 2 C and Li|PL‐CEC|LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells deliver excellent cycling durability and high‐rate capability. Notably, multilayer Li|PL‐CEC|NCM811 pouch cell achieves Ah‐level capacity, demonstrating the practical scalability of PL‐CEC. This work establishes a molecular‐chain engineering strategy to enhance Li + transport and electrode interfacial stability for advanced SPEs toward long‐cycle SSLMBs.

title: Interphasial Li + Flux Engineering via Anchoring Vertically Oriented Fluorinated Covalent Organic Frameworks Toward Long‐Cycling Li‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Unstable solid electrolyte interphases and uncontrollable Li‐dendrite growth largely hamper the practical application of metallic Li anode in rechargeable batteries. Constructing a reliable and steady Li interphase is critical to promote commercialization of Li‐metal batteries. In this study, we propose to directionally anchor 2D fluorinated covalent organic frameworks on Li metal to build artificial solid electrolyte interphases, aiming to homogenize and accelerate the interphasial Li + flux and regulate uniform Li plating/stripping. Theoretical calculations reveal that active fluorine sites with negative electrostatic potential facilitate fast LiTFSI dissociation and strong Li + adsorption, and oriented 2D channels with low diffusion energy barrier endow high Li + flux and fast Li + transport. The obtained interphase has a homogeneously amorphous structure with high mechanical elasticity and thermodynamic stability, exhibiting high compatibility with metallic Li and enabling excellent electrochemical properties. Consequently, its symmetrical cell demonstrates an ultralong cycle life over 1300 h. When paired with commercial cathodes, LiFePO 4 cell and LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 cell demonstrate a cycle‐life of 335 and 228 at 5 C, respectively. Notably, 1 Ah LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 //modified Li pouch‐cell exhibits a long cycle‐life over 325 at 1 C. This study offers an effective method for enhancing Li metal interphase stability of high‐energy‐density Li‐metal batteries.

title: Tandem Solar Cells Based on Si and Stable Cu(In,Ga)S 2 With Efficiency Beyond the Bottom Cell
abstract: ABSTRACT Tandem solar cells require stable, highly efficient top cells with a band gap above 1.6 eV. We present a semitransparent solar cell with an efficiency of 15.52% and an open‐circuit voltage of 1.014 V, based on an environmentally stable sulfide chalcopyrite absorber and ITO back contact. Solar cells are prepared by industrially scalable processes of co‐evaporation, sputter and atomic layer deposition. The progress in efficiency is achieved by alloying with small amounts of Ag (less than 10% of Cu replaced by Ag). Optimum amount of Ag alloying is shown to depend on the amount of Cu‐excess during absorber growth. Ag alloying leads to larger grains, avoids high Ga phases, and reduces non‐radiative recombination, which improves open circuit voltage. Whether the reduction in non‐radiative recombination is due to an increase in net doping or due to a longer minority carrier lifetime appears to depend on the Cu‐excess during process. The efficiency of the top cell remains stable over several months’ storage in a non‐controlled atmosphere. We combine this new top cell in a tandem cell with both Si and CuInSe 2 bottom cells, in both cases, the efficiency beyond the bottom cell alone by between 2.5% and 5% absolute.

title: Dual Charge Extraction Pathways at Perovskite/Organic Hetero‐Contacts for Optoelectronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Charge extraction at the hetero‑contact between perovskites and organic charge‑transport layers (OCTLs) is central to the performance of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process remain insufficiently resolved. Here we indicate a hybrid interfacial state that emerges broadly at perovskite/OCTL hetero‐contacts containing heteroatoms capable of coordinating to surface Pb 2+ sites. Using ultrafast spectroscopy supported by electronic‑structure calculations, we determine the energetic position and temporal evolution of this state and show that it mediates an additional, fast charge‑extraction pathway alongside the conventional valence‑band route. This dual‑pathway mechanism helps overcome interfacial energy barriers and large valence band maximum‐highest occupied molecular orbital (VBM‐HOMO) offsets that typically limit extraction efficiency. Our findings establish a general coordination‑driven origin for hybrid interfacial states and provide design principles for engineering charge‑selective contacts in next‑generation perovskite optoelectronic devices.

title: Spatially Synchronized Ion‐Electron Transport Enables Millimeter‐Thick Cathodes for Ah‐Level Aqueous Cu‐S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Thick conversion electrodes are essential for practical high‐energy aqueous batteries, yet their electrochemical reactions become increasingly heterogeneous when ionic and electronic pathways are spatially decoupled across the electrode depth. Here, sulfated cellulose nanofibrils (SCNFs) and PEDOT:PSS are integrated to construct a nanocellulose‐enabled architecture that synchronizes ionic and electronic transport in millimeter‐thick aqueous Cu‐S cathodes. The SCNF framework directs conformal PEDOT:PSS assembly along continuous nanofibrils, creating collocated electronic pathways and hydrophilic Cu 2+ ‐transport channels within one fibrillar scaffold. Electrochemical analysis, Raman mapping, and X‐ray computed tomography reveal that this integrated network converts localized sulfur conversion into a homogeneous and reversible through‐thickness reaction. Consequently, the optimized cathode retains 98.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g −1 and delivers an areal capacity exceeding 179 mAh cm −2 at an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 112 mg cm −2 . In a high‐loading pouch‐cell configuration, the optimized cathode further achieves a capacity of approximately 3 Ah. Furthermore, a decoupled Zn‐S configuration design delivers an energy density of 651 Wh kg −1 based on sulfur and zinc active materials. This work establishes spatial synchronization of ionic and electronic transport as a broadly applicable design principle for practical high‐loading conversion electrodes.

title: Alloy Engineering of Chiral‐Anomaly Transport Signatures into a Group‐IV Semiconductor
abstract: ABSTRACT Integration of chiral transport phenomena into the CMOS platform underlying modern computation has the potential to transform information processing. However, transport signatures associated with the chiral‐anomaly have remained confined largely to low‐symmetry, difficult‐to‐process materials and have been essentially unexplored in conventional CMOS‐compatible semiconductors. Here, we show that dilute carbon alloying drives the group‐IV semiconductor germanium–tin (GeSn) into a distinct magnetotransport regime. Carbon‐alloyed GeSn (CGeSn) films exhibit pronounced negative longitudinal magnetoresistance together with a robust planar Hall effect. The magnetic field, angular, temperature, and composition dependence of these responses follow the transport phenomenology of the chiral‐anomaly and closely mirror that reported for established topological materials. Remarkably, these signatures emerge in a material whose global topological electronic structure is as of yet unexplored, revealing an unexpected transport regime beyond current theoretical descriptions of GeSn‐based alloys. The systematic evolution of this behavior with carbon incorporation demonstrates that material design approaches focused on dilute alloy engineering provide a powerful route to realizing chiral‐anomaly transport signatures in conventional semiconductors. These results establish CGeSn as a CMOS‐compatible platform for exploring emergent chiral transport phenomena and motivate the development of a microscopic theory capable of explaining their origin.

title: Chloride‐Induced Microstructure–Covalency Coupling Enables Ultrafine Nanoparticle Exsolution for High‐Performance CO 2 Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires active cathode catalysts that combine abundant active interfaces, rapid charge transfer, and long‐term structural stability. Perovskite exsolution can generate robust metal nanoparticles (NPs), but achieving a dense population of ultrafine nanocatalysts remains challenging. Here, we report a chloride‐assisted exsolution strategy in Sr 2 Fe 1.3 Ni 0.2 Mo 0.5 O 6‐δ (SFNM)‐based cathodes, demonstrating for the first time that Cl doping links grain‐boundary (GB) engineering with metal–oxygen covalency regulation to direct FeNi NP exsolution. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis shows that the SrCl 2 ‐derived molten‐salt flux effect creates a faceted, GB‐rich perovskite morphology, increasing the GB density by approximately 78.9% and providing abundant nucleation sites for exsolution. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and theoretical calculations further reveal that Cl substitution attenuates metal–oxygen hybridization, promotes oxygen‐vacancy formation, and facilitates outward segregation of Fe and Ni. This chloride‐triggered dual regulation yields a highly populated FeNi NP surface, accelerating CO 2 electroreduction and lowering polarization resistance. Consequently, the reduced Cl‐doped SFNM cathode (R‐SFNMCl2) achieves 2.73 A cm −2 at 800°C and 1.5 V, while sustaining stable operation for 400 h with only minor degradation. This work establishes a new halogen‐mediated exsolution design paradigm for developing high‐performance SOEC cathode catalysts.

title: Polarity‐Directed Assembly of in‐Plane Oriented Covalent Organic Framework Films on Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are promising crystalline porous materials for optoelectronic applications; however, controlled growth of COF thin films on substrates remains a significant challenge. Here, we develop a polarity‐directed solution assembly strategy for the fabrication of 2D COF thin films on various substrates. This approach leverages polarity‐driven solvent–molecule interactions to regulate precursor assembly and oriented polymerization, successfully yielding in‐plane oriented COF films with controllable thickness, smooth surface morphology, and abundant nitrogen active sites. When these films are used as templates for perovskite growth, the resulting heterojunction interfaces effectively passivate buried interfacial defects and suppress non‐radiative recombination. Integrated into light‐emitting diodes (LED), the devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 30.88%, a peak luminance of 1.7 × 10 5 cd/m 2 , and an operational half‐lifetime (T 50 ) of 12.74 h at an initial luminance of 9206 cd/m 2 (equivalent to >6238 h at 100 cd/m 2 ), surpassing most previously reported counterparts. This work opens a new molecular regulation avenue toward the preparation of highly oriented COF films for versatile optoelectronic applications.

title: Micro 3D Printing of Silica Aerogels via Bath‐Mediated In Situ Sol–Gel Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Silica aerogels are attractive thermally insulating materials owing to their extremely low density and nanoporous silica networks, but their integration into miniaturized devices for thermal management remains limited by the difficulty of patterning fragile aerogel structures at microscale resolution. Here, we report a bath‐mediated in situ sol–gel reaction printing process for microscale 3D printing of silica aerogel architectures. In this strategy, a pre‐hydrolyzed, silanol‐rich precursor solution stabilized in an acidic medium is deposited into a basic bath, where an abrupt pH change triggers instantaneous siloxane condensation and forms silica gel filaments. This pH‐mediated sol–gel printing process enabled the fabrication of silica aerogel structures with filament linewidths as small as 8 µm in single‐layer patterns and approximately 20 µm in multilayer 3D structures. The printed filaments exhibited an interconnected nanoparticle network with a high specific surface area of 988.3 m 2 g −1 , an average pore size of 18.4 nm, and a low thermal conductivity of 0.023 W m −1 K −1 . On microheater device platforms, the printed aerogels provided localized thermal insulation that could be modulated by adjusting the printed architecture. This work provides a route for integrating nanoporous silica aerogels as spatially controlled thermal insulation components in miniaturized thermal management systems.

title: Halide‐Based Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors Deliver High‐Rate and Long‐Life All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial side reactions and degradation of solid–solid contact limit the rate capability and cycling stability of composite cathodes in all‐solid‐state lithium batteries. Here, we introduce C5.5Mo (LiMo 2 O 2.75 Cl 5.5 ), a functional halide oxide additive designed to maintain solid–solid contact, improve charge transport, and regulate the composite‐cathode interface. Its mixed ionic‐electronic conductivity and low Young's modulus promote a dense cathode microstructure and stable interparticle contact during cycling. Bias‐dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy of composite‐cathode symmetric cells reveals lower interfacial resistance and reduced bias sensitivity, suggesting partial alleviation of space‐charge‐layer‐related transport limitations. The full‐cell system still provides a specific capacity of approximately 100 mAh g −1 at 6 C and maintains stable cycling for 20 000 cycles (capacity retention of 85.84%). This work establishes a practical additive strategy for constructing high‐rate and long‐life composite cathodes.

title: A self-oscillator expands the recordable radius of deep and local biosignals
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Visceral physiological signals are pivotal for both disease monitoring and elucidating complex biological processes, but localized physiological signals rapidly attenuate as they propagate through biological tissue. As a result, noninvasive epidermal recording of localized biosignals originating from deep tissues remains highly challenging, particularly in obese individuals. title: Dual-q chirality from chirality-polarity coupling in polar nematic fluids
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Tuning delicate polar domain structures with chirality offers a promising route to exploring emergent states in condensed-matter physics. Here, we report the emergence of counterintuitive dual- q chirality and its tunability in domain structures of chiral ferroelectric fluids with nematic order. The dual- q chiral domains are composed of asymmetric twisting wave numbers (or wavelengths) in neighboring twisted domains, in contrast to the common understanding that a single system with a specific chirality favors only one wavelength of helix. This dual- q chirality arises from the formation of periodic twist polar domains with opposite chiral signs to reduce electrostatic energy, while the different twisting wave numbers of the helices in neighboring domains balance the chiral and electrostatic energies. We observe a crossover with inherent hysteresis from an electrostatics-dominant to a chirality-dominant region, triggering a transition from a dual- q chiral to a homo -chiral state.
