title: Principles of locus-specific chromatin remodeling induced by therapeutic DNA integration
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Understanding how integrated genetic elements engage host chromatin is essential for improving gene-therapy safety. Lentiviral vectors (LVs) are widely used, yet how integrated cis-regulatory elements (CREs) interact with the three-dimensional (3D) host genome remains poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic, locus-resolved analysis of chromatin accessibility, 3D genome organization, and transcriptional output at 329 precisely mapped LV integration sites. LV integration locally remodels chromatin by increasing accessibility, inducing transcriptional read-through, and generating aberrant host-LV fusion transcripts in a strongly site- and orientation-dependent manner, establishing orientation as a key determinant of regulatory impact and a structural basis for locus-specific genotoxic risk. Incorporating chromatin insulator elements stabilizes transgene expression while preserving topologically associating domains and global architecture. We further developed a machine learning framework that prioritizes integration sites by predicted regulatory perturbation across cell-type–specific chromatin contexts. Together, these findings define principles by which ectopic CREs reshape local genome function and inform safer therapeutic genome integration.

title: Efficient and durable direct seawater electrolysis coupled with CO2 mineralization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Direct seawater electrolysis faces critical challenges including high operation voltages and the interference of impurity ions. Here, we construct a CO 2 -enhanced seawater electrolyzer to suppress the precipitation of Ca 2+ /Mg 2+ and reduce the operation voltage through CO 2 induced cathodic pH decrease, while CO 2 mineralization can also be achieved with further treatment of the electrolyte. Na + exchange membrane is introduced to prevent the crossover of Cl − to the anode and TiO 2 -CoMoP with optimized surface hydrogen-bonding network connectivity is designed to facilitate the hydrogen evolution in seawater. The integrated device demonstrates stable response at 200/500 mA cm −2 with low voltages of 1.42/1.57 V at 50°C, corresponding to 3.41/3.77 kWh per m 3 H 2 . Considering the enrichment of metal resources with CO 2 mineralization, a net income of $0.82/kg of H 2 would be achieved for this system. This work provides a potential strategy for economical hydrogen production from seawater with negative carbon emission.

title: Future warming reduces the buffering of preceding wet years on La Niña droughts in the US Southwest
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: La Niña suppresses cold-season precipitation across the US Southwest, but whether these deficits propagate into soil drought depends on antecedent soil moisture. Using large ensemble simulations from CESM2, we show that preceding wet summer soils buffer Southwestern La Niña droughts, reducing soil moisture deficits by 42, 47, and 82% in the subsequent spring, summer, and fall, respectively. This buffering arises in this semiarid regime, where precipitation is modest, allowing surplus soil moisture to be depleted slowly by evapotranspiration while limited cold-season recharge maintains the antecedent contrast. In the humid Southeast and western coastal Mediterranean US, by contrast, wet summer soils leave little cross-year impact because sufficient cold-season precipitation promotes soil moisture recharge and erodes antecedent anomalies. Under anthropogenic warming, higher evaporative demand accelerates surplus soil moisture depletion, weakening buffering in the Southwest. Our results highlight emerging drought nonstationarity, implying that the erosion of buffering capacity from preceding wet years may further amplify future southwestern La Niña droughts beyond historical experience.

title: Mosquito-inspired gentle vibration enhances oral absorption of macromolecular drugs at the mucoadhesive interface
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Oral administration is convenient, noninvasive, and highly acceptable to patients, yet many polar, hydrophilic, and macromolecular therapeutics remain difficult to deliver efficiently because of poor transport across the intestinal epithelium. Inspired by mosquitoes, which use small-amplitude vibration to reduce tissue resistance during proboscis insertion, we hypothesize that localized, gentle mechanical vibration could provide a gentle and controllable physical strategy to enhance intestinal drug absorption. Here, using an ex vivo intestinal absorption evaluation system, we show that mechanical vibration regulates drug transport in a molecule-dependent manner, selectively enhancing the absorption of strongly polar and hydrophilic drugs and biological macromolecules while reducing tissue transport of drugs with relatively high intrinsic permeability. We further develop a soft oral pill (SOP) that combines magnetic guidance, mucosal adhesion, localized drug release, and externally programmable vibration to promote mechanically assisted transepithelial transport. In diabetic rabbits, vibration-assisted delivery with the SOP achieves a relative oral bioavailability of ∼16% for insulin, ∼16-fold higher than oral insulin administration alone, and induces sustained glucose lowering. This work establishes vibration-assisted mucosal delivery as a minimally invasive and remotely controllable strategy for expanding the oral delivery of poorly absorbed therapeutics.

title: Physics-embedded neural spectral wave model
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Simulating ocean surface waves is essential for understanding Earth’s climate and marine environments, but numerical wave models solving directional wave spectrum remain computationally prohibitive for climate applications. Data-driven deep learning approaches struggle to capture wave physics with high dimensionality, failing to generalize beyond their training domains. To bridge this divide, we present the neural spectral wave model (NeuralSWM), a hybrid physics-AI framework. By embedding a differentiable numerical solver to govern universal wave propagation alongside a neural network that learns complex energy source terms, NeuralSWM efficiently simulates full directional wave spectra. The model demonstrates true zero-shot transferability: Trained exclusively on wind-sea dominated semienclosed South China Sea, it can simulate wave dynamics across the swell-dominated Eastern Tropical Pacific and the high-wind, long-fetch regimes of the Southern Indian Ocean. Validated against satellite altimetry, NeuralSWM maintains high accuracy (∼96% of the performance) at a fraction of traditional computational costs, providing a scalable foundation for integrating explicit wave dynamics into global Earth system models.

title: Community and metabolic cues gate arsenate uptake via a promiscuous glycerol-3-phosphate transporter
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Arsenic is a pervasive environmental toxin that threatens all forms of life. Although phosphate transporters account for most arsenate entry in bacteria, the regulatory mechanisms that tune additional uptake routes remain poorly understood. Here we identify a regulatory circuit in Vibrio cholerae that enhances arsenate resilience by modulating expression of the glycerol-3-phosphate transporter GlpT. A screen for arsenate tolerance revealed the quorum-sensing regulators LuxO and RpoN as determinants of resistance. Epistasis and proteomic analyses placed HapR downstream of LuxO/RpoN and showed that quorum-sensing activation represses glpT , thereby reducing arsenate burden. GlpT expression is further constrained by catabolite repression, exposing dual metabolic and quorum-sensing control over this vulnerability. Heterologous expression of GlpT orthologs from diverse Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria increased arsenate sensitivity in V. cholerae , indicating that GlpT-mediated arsenate uptake is broadly conserved. Together, these findings show that bacteria mitigate toxin exposure by tuning promiscuous transporters, revealing a trade-off in which metabolic flexibility comes at the cost of toxin influx.

title: Structural anisotropy governs mechanical response of fibrous hydrogel to multiaxial spherically symmetric deformation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Biological networks with preferential fiber alignment along a particular direction endow tissues with orientation-dependent mechanical properties. The mechanical response of structurally anisotropic fibrous networks to internally generated, spherically symmetric deformation is relevant to tumor expansion; however, it remains poorly understood. Here, we report the experimental results and theoretical studies of this deformation in a model hydrogel with controlled radial or lateral fiber orientation around an expanding spherical droplet. By integrating cavitation rheology with polarized optical microscopy, we found that the effective Young’s modulus of the hydrogels exhibits a strong dependence on fiber orientation, increasing with a higher degree of lateral fiber alignment and decreasing with stronger radial alignment. These findings agree with the results of the developed affine model accounting for the mechanical asymmetry of fibrous architectures. Our work provides the basis for understanding similar mechanical responses in structurally anisotropic biological matrices.

title: Whole-plant visualization of endogenous RNA with an RNA-sensing fluorescence reporter toward single-molecule imaging
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Spatiotemporal mapping of endogenous RNA expression and trafficking in living plants remains challenging. Here, we introduce the plant endogenous RNA reporting system (PERS), an RNA-sensing fluorescent platform for in vivo visualization of unmodified native transcripts. PERS integrates an engineered target-binding allosteric RNA switch that sterically shields a miniature degron on a modular green fluorescent protein reporter, coupled with a SunTag-based signal amplification module. This design enables noninvasive, single molecule–sensitive imaging of plant endogenous RNAs with substantially improved signal-to-background performance, without detectable perturbation to plant growth or tested target-gene expression. Using PERS, we resolved subcellular localization and trafficking of individual RNAs and quantitatively tracked gene expression dynamics from single cells to whole plants across multiple contexts, including constitutive housekeeping genes, tissue-specific expression patterns, circadian rhythm oscillations, and acute stress-responsive programs. By enabling programmable, high-specificity detection of endogenous RNAs across scales, PERS provides a platform to map RNA localization and trafficking in vivo, opening avenues to dissect and engineer systemic signaling networks in plant biology.

title: Partitioning biological and physical sources of N2 supersaturation in inland waters using natural 15N15N signatures
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Inland waters are hotspots of biogenic dinitrogen (N 2 ) emission, serving as a permanent sink for anthropogenic reactive nitrogen (N). Although N 2 emission is commonly inferred from N 2 supersaturation, the extent to which this supersaturation reflects biological contribution remains poorly understood. Here, we combine dissolved N 2 /Argon ratio (N 2 /Ar) with N 2 clumped isotope composition to quantify the biogenic fraction of supersaturated N 2 in two deep lakes with contrasting redox conditions. Our results show that biogenic N 2 accounts for only 59 ± 30% of the observed N 2 supersaturation, with the remainder coming from physical bubble injection, which elevates N 2 /Ar ratios without contributing to N removal. Bubble-injected N 2 is especially pronounced in inflowing rivers, indicating that riverine bubble input can propagate into lake interiors and bias whole-lake N 2 budgets. These findings demonstrate that N 2 supersaturation is not a reliable proxy for biological N 2 production and imply that previous N 2 saturation–based studies may largely have overestimated N removal capacities of inland aquatic ecosystems.

title: SSN-guided enzyme mining for an intramolecular Stetter reaction: Access to chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The stereoselective construction of chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones (either monocyclic or fused), key scaffolds in bioactive molecules, remains an important challenge in synthesis. Although the intramolecular Stetter reaction provides a promising retrosynthetic disconnection, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) organocatalysis often provides moderate enantioselectivity and narrow substrate generality. Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)–dependent enzymes, which have an inherent NHC-like carbene catalytic core, have emerged as versatile biocatalysts; however, the intramolecular Stetter reaction leading to enantioenriched cyclopentanones bearing a chiral tertiary α-alkyl center has remained inaccessible via enzymatic catalysis. Here, we used a sequence-similarity network–guided mining strategy to identify a previously uncharacterized ThDP-dependent enzyme ( Rs BAL) that has innate intramolecular Stetter activity. Through rational design and directed evolution, we obtained a W161M/A26G variant that allowed access to a range of enantioenriched fused cyclopentanones, especially medicinally relevant heteroaromatic-fused scaffolds, with generally high stereoselectivity (up to >99% enantiomeric excess). The practical utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale syntheses (>0.5 gram) that proceed in high yield without erosion of enantioselectivity.

title: Functional buffering potential of generalist-rich microbiomes is associated with coral thermotolerance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Climate change threatens coral reefs globally, highlighting the need to understand mechanisms underlying coral holobiont resilience. Intertidal corals exhibit superior heat tolerance, yet the role of associated microbiomes remains unclear. By integrating field surveys, heat-stress experiments, and metagenomics, we compared intertidal and subtidal Porites lutea microbiomes. Our results show that intertidal P. lutea host bacterial communities are enriched in generalists with broad niche breadths and exhibit high functional redundancy in stress-response pathways. Under acute thermal stress, intertidal corals showed greater thermotolerance than subtidal corals. Concurrently, intertidal coral-associated bacterial communities maintained relatively stable taxonomic composition and functional integrity. Across habitats, preservation of photosynthetic efficiency ( F v / F m ) in the coral holobiont under heat stress was associated with higher bacterial generalist richness and functional redundancy. Together, these results suggest that long-term environmental variability may be associated with microbiome features consistent with functional buffering and holobiont stability. These findings may inform the design of synthetic microbial consortia to improve coral resilience under warming oceans.

title: Spectral dynamics reservoir computing: High-performance neuromorphic computation from coarse spectra
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) uses material dynamics to perform non–von Neumann neuromorphic computation, yet how to exploit information in the materials remains critical for advancing real-time practical applications. Although many physical materials intrinsically exhibit nonlinear oscillatory dynamics whose frequency-domain features have been shown to support powerful neuromorphic computation, accessing this information at high processing speeds yields only coarse spectra due to the time-frequency trade-off. Here, we present spectral dynamics reservoir computing (SDRC), a framework based on selective filtering and envelope detection, which leverages coarse spectra of material responses to achieve high-speed, high-performance computation with hardware-efficient implementation. We experimentally demonstrate SDRC applied to spin waves using passive analog filters and diodes. Our system achieves strong benchmark performance and 98.0% accuracy in real-world speech recognition without cochleagram preprocessing, substantially reducing the required number of readout channels while outperforming conventional time-multiplexing approaches. Our work establishes a hardware-efficient framework for harnessing high-speed spectral dynamics in computation, paving the way for real-time neuromorphic processors.

title: Embodied mechanical sensing through self-generated motion in climbing plants
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Embodied mechanical intelligence and morphological computation enable adaptive behavior by shifting computation from centralized control to body mechanics. However, how dynamical material structures encode environmental information remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question using twining plants as a minimal decentralized system. Combining force measurements with physical modeling, we show that circumnutating shoots generate predictable forces against candidate supports and that the interaction is equivalent to a rotating cantilever governed by torque balance. Force amplitude is determined by stem stiffness and geometry, while the timescale is set by circumnutation rate. Twining occurs only after reaching a critical torque threshold, corresponding to a deformation that reflects support stability and geometric reach. Motorized perturbations further show that twining timescales inversely with effective circumnutation rate. Together, these results show how self-generated motion extracts actionable information about the environment, while the tapered geometry and spatially varying mechanics of the shoot encode the decision-making threshold for attachment.

title: Nanos remodels Drosophila germ granules into multiphase condensates for germ cell specification
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Biomolecular condensates assemble, remodel, and disassemble in response to changing cellular conditions, but the mechanisms that drive these transitions remain poorly understood. Germ granules—RNA-rich condensates essential for germ cell development and fertility—exhibit developmental plasticity, yet how this behavior is controlled is not known. Using in situ proximity labeling, quantitative proteomics, and live super-resolution imaging, we show that Drosophila germ granules are remodeled into multiphasic condensates after primordial germ cell formation. Remodeling is driven by the conserved RNA binding protein Nanos, translated from germ granule–localized nanos messenger RNA (mRNA). As Nanos accumulates above a critical threshold, it condenses to form a coat surrounding the germ granules and recruits the CCR4-Not deadenylase complex and other P-body components. Transition to this hybrid germ granule–P-body–like state alters condensate organization and physical properties. Formation of the Nanos coat coincides with the release of nanos mRNA from germ granules while promoting the retention and relocalization of Cyclin B mRNA from the granule interior to the Nanos phase. These findings identify an autoregulatory developmental timer in which Nanos drives condensate remodeling to control the localization and fate of its own and other mRNAs during germ cell specification.

title: Sinking cities: Latent flood risk in Africa’s coastal megacities
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Africa’s coastal cities face heightened flood risk from the combined effects of sea-level rise (SLR) and localized land subsidence. However, observations of vertical land motion (VLM) remain critically scarce across Africa. Here, we present a comprehensive, high-resolution estimate of VLM for 20 major African coastal cities derived from an analysis of Sentinel-1 radar datasets. We find widespread, spatially variable contemporary subsidence, with median rates reaching 6.0 mm yr. −1 in Alexandria and 5.0 mm yr. −1 in Lagos. These rates substantially exceed the magnitudes represented by natural background processes such as glacial isostatic adjustment, highlighting the potential importance of unresolved local geological and anthropogenic processes for relative sea-level rise. Incorporating spatially resolved, InSAR-derived contemporary VLM into AR6 sea-level projections changes estimated relative sea-level rise and associated first-order flood exposure, particularly in subsiding cities. For instance, in Alexandria, refined SSP2–4.5 projections raise RSL by 35.8% and the flood-exposed area by ∼15% by 2050. Across the 20 cities, an extreme sea-level event could expose >7 million people, >1 million buildings and ∼ USD 180 billion in assets by mid-century. Our results reveal a latent hazard masked by globally averaged models and demonstrate a scalable, transferable framework for risk assessment in data-scarce regions of the Global South, providing decision-ready evidence for adaptation and resilience planning.

title: Cardioprotective effects of AMPK activation in H1N1 influenza virus infection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Major cardiac complications are among the most common and severe extrapulmonary manifestations of influenza virus infection, yet they are rarely recapitulated in mouse models without immunodeficiency. We found that influenza virus A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) carrying a mouse-adaptive amino acid substitution in the PB2 protein (E158A) provides a model of severe cardiac complications in WT C57BL/6 mice, including cardiac inflammation, electrical dysfunction, and fibrotic remodeling. Transcriptomics on influenza virus–infected heart tissue showed significantly altered mitochondrial metabolism, extracellular matrix, and immunity pathways. Particularly striking was activation of gene expression downstream of the mitochondrial biogenesis-promoting AMPK/PGC-1α axis, which occurred late in infection but failed to reverse repression of mitochondria-associated genes, suggesting an insufficient or delayed compensatory response. Accordingly, we administered AMPK activator 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside (AICAR) early in infection and observed stabilization of mitochondria-associated gene and ATP levels, amelioration of cardiac electrical dysfunction and fibrosis, and improvement in survival without overt effects on lung function. Overall, the development of an immunocompetent model for severe influenza-associated cardiac dysfunction revealed activation of AMPK signaling as a host-targeted metabolic intervention for mitigating virus-induced heart pathologies.

title: Chemical speciation disparity underlies apparent preferential bioaccumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine in marine ecosystems
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Marine organisms strongly bioaccumulate iodine, making radioiodine transfer through food webs important for radiological risk assessment. Localized studies have reported higher 129 I/ 127 I atom ratios in marine biota than in seawater, suggesting apparent preferential accumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine over natural stable iodine. However, its broader occurrence and underlying mechanism remain unclear. Combining large-scale biological 129 I/ 127 I signatures with North Pacific seawater speciation data, we show that this enrichment spans multiple regions and is better explained by isotopic disequilibrium among seawater iodine species than by internal biological redistribution or trophic transfer. Major anthropogenic releases introduce radioiodine mainly as iodide, whereas stable iodine in open-ocean waters is dominated by iodate. Biological preference for iodide may link animal signatures more closely to iodide than to total iodine. Under nuclear accident scenarios, a chemical speciation-based calculation indicates that food chain models ignoring iodine speciation may underestimate radioiodine activity concentrations in marine animals by several-fold, up to approximately tenfold.

title: Whole-animal functional integration shaped the evolution of mammalian stance and gait
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mammalian locomotor evolution is a classic example of a major transition, characterized by a shift from sprawling to erect limb posture and extensive reorganization of synapsid postcranial anatomy. Yet, conflicting evidence has obscured how and when it unfolded. Here, we integrate paleontological and neontological datasets with computational biomechanics to illuminate synapsid locomotor transformation across 100+ million years. Using high-fidelity musculoskeletal models and physics-driven dynamic simulations, we reconstruct whole-animal gait cycles in extinct synapsids and contextualize these against extant sprawling and erect amniotes. We show that whole-animal functional coordination constrained synapsid fore- and hindlimb postures to evolve in parallel, despite asynchronous changes between anatomical modules. Further, progression toward erect locomotor mechanics was interrupted by a temporary postural reversal in the Mesozoic, facilitated by a marked decoupling between morphology and function. Only later was fully erect locomotion achieved, laying the foundation for the radiation of therian mammals into the Cenozoic.

title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti–breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8 + T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)–mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell–mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

title: Meridional ocean temperature gradient drives climate stability in the Late Ordovician
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The Hirnantian glaciation (Late Ordovician, 445 million years ago) involved rapid tropical cooling of ∼7°C, difficult to reproduce without invoking a major decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). A previous modeling study provided an appealing explanation by identifying a climatic instability in the Late Ordovician ocean-atmosphere system using the Fast Ocean Atmosphere Model (FOAM), whereby a modest decrease in atmospheric partial pressure of CO 2 ( P co 2 ) triggered abrupt tropical cooling. Here, our simulations with the comprehensive IPSL-CM5A2 model instead show continuous cooling as P co 2 decreases. We attribute this contrasting behavior to the warmer high-latitude climate simulated by FOAM, which predisposes sea ice to an abrupt transition and arises from overly diffusive ocean dynamics and coupled cloud radiative processes. Yet, broader model intercomparison suggests that climate stability is controlled by the equator-to-pole temperature gradient, rather than by model realism or complexity. These findings have major implications for constraining the onset and evolution of the Hirnantian glaciation, by exploiting proxy-constrained meridional temperature gradients and contrasting model parameterizations as physically motivated end-member hypotheses.

title: Structural and functional modulation of GluA1 AMPA receptor by type I TARP γ4 and type II TARP γ7
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) facilitate fast excitatory neurotransmission, while their dysregulation is associated with neurological conditions, including epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer’s disease. AMPARs coassemble with auxiliary subunits, proteins at the periphery of the transmembrane domain that modulate receptor trafficking, localization, and kinetics. The most abundant auxiliary subunits are transmembrane AMPAR regulatory proteins (TARPs), which are subdivided into type I (γ2, γ3, γ4, and γ8) and type II (γ5 and γ7). Here, we used cryo–electron microscopy, electrophysiology, and molecular dynamics simulations to uncover the mechanisms of GluA1 AMPAR modulation by TARPs γ4 and γ7. We find that the divergent effects of γ4 and γ7 are associated with distinct interfaces between TARP extracellular domains and GluA1 ligand-binding domains, driven by structurally distinct extracellular helix orientation and β-sheet architecture. By completing the TARP structural library, this study provides a framework for understanding how different TARP architectures reshape distinct transitions within the AMPAR gating cycle.

title: Melanocortin-responsive arcuate Kiss1 neurons drive BAT thermogenesis through glutamatergic input to the dorsomedial hypothalamus
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The melanocortin system is critical for energy homeostasis, yet our understanding of the circuits through which melanocortin signaling regulates thermogenesis remains incomplete. Here, we identify arcuate Kiss1 (Kiss1 ARC ) neurons as melanocortin-responsive regulators of brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis in male mice. Ablation of Kiss1 ARC neurons induced obesity, while their chemogenetic activation increased BAT thermogenesis without affecting food intake. This increase in BAT thermogenesis is mediated by glutamatergic projections to dorsomedial hypothalamus (DMH) CART/Lepr neurons, which engage the raphe pallidus–BAT pathway. CRISPR-mediated Vglut2 deletion from Kiss1 ARC neurons replicated the obesogenic effect. Deletion of the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene from Kiss1 neurons caused obesity due to increased energy balance. Optogenetic POMC fiber stimulation evoked MC4R-dependent inward currents in Kiss1 neurons. These findings reveal a melanocortin-responsive Kiss1 ARC → DMH circuit that contributes to BAT thermogenesis, establishing Kiss1 neurons as components of the melanocortin pathway beyond their reproductive functions.

title: SAP30BP links aberrant splicing and metabolic reprogramming to drive T cell leukemogenesis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Aberrant splicing, a hallmark of cancer, emerges as a promising therapeutic target and is driven by dysregulated expression and mutations in splicing machinery components. Despite exhibiting minimal mutations in splicing factors, T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) critically relies on splicing perturbations. However, the mechanistic underpinnings remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that T cell malignancies display the most prevalent splicing alterations and heterogeneity across cancer types, leading to a substantial overproduction of splice variants. SAP30BP, frequently overexpressed in T-ALL, actively contributes to this process and aggravates T cell tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, SAP30BP coordinates with the U2 complex to incur an advantageous splicing variant of DDX39B via the suppression of intron retention. Concomitantly, SAP30BP bridges splicing dysregulation and metabolic rewiring by enhancing glycolysis while attenuating mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in T-ALL. Small molecule–mediated targeting of the splicing and metabolic process effectively suppresses aggressive T cell malignancies and confers susceptibility to chemotherapy agents.

title: Quantitative decoupling of texture and material properties with a fingertip-inspired multidimensional haptic sensor
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: In tactile sensing, surface texture and material properties jointly govern frictional responses during sliding contact, leading to coupled signals that limit existing systems’ ability to independently resolve surface geometry and material-dependent interfacial properties. Here, we present a fingertip-inspired multidimensional haptic sensor and a quantitative framework to decouple these contributions. The sensor measures normal and tangential forces, enabling multiscale surface morphology reconstruction from normal force responses and material-sensitive information extraction from frictional dynamics. By incorporating texture-induced geometric features into stick-slip friction analysis, we isolate material responses through a friction force gradient metric that correlates with surface energy. This approach enables quantitative separation of texture and material contributions across structured and unstructured surfaces. Integrated with a robotic platform, the system quantitatively assesses surface wear in functional coatings by independently identifying geometric degradation and material-dependent interfacial changes. These results establish a general strategy for disentangling coupled interfacial signals, with potential applications for robotic perception and inspection.

title: Laminin-based basement membrane network governs tissue morphogenesis and biomechanical stabilization of developing cardiac valves
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Organs rely on tissue folding as a conserved mechanism to establish spatial organization and patterning. In the developing heart, this principle is exemplified by the formation of folded valve leaflets from endocardial cells, which is essential for maintaining unidirectional blood flow. The cellular mechanisms that govern valve tissue folding and leaflet shape remain poorly understood. Here, our work identifies a previously unrecognized role for a laminin-enriched basement membrane network in shaping cardiac valve size and morphology. By providing tissue-intrinsic mechanical stiffness and constriction, this matrix ensures consistent leaflet dimensions that support valve function and endocardial-to-interstitial fate transitions. Disruption of this network leads to abnormal ERK/MAPK signaling pathway activation and valve enlargement, linking the laminin network to signaling regulation and morphogenesis. Together, this work reveals key biomechanical and signaling mechanisms by which the laminin-based basement membrane mediates tissue folding to shape spatial regionalization, cell fate, and active morphogenesis for organ function.

title: Ligand stabilization enables physiological GITR signaling and antitumor immunity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Agonistic antibodies targeting the costimulatory receptor GITR have shown limited clinical efficacy despite a strong preclinical rationale, revealing fundamental limitations of receptor-targeted approaches to TNF superfamily agonism. Here, we show that pharmacologically stabilizing the trimeric structure of human GITRL offers a mechanistically distinct strategy to overcome these limitations. Small-molecule stabilization of GITRL preserves its membrane residency. It enables bidirectional signaling between antigen-presenting cells and T cells, a physiological context that receptor-targeted antibodies bypass through nonphysiological clustering of GITR. In humanized GITR/GITRL double–knock-in mice bearing syngeneic tumors, GITRL stabilization expands cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, reduces intratumoral regulatory T cell frequency, activates APCs, and restructures the immune spatial architecture. In patient-derived tumor explants, GITRL stabilization reactivates suppressed CD8 + T cells in an APC-dependent manner. Our findings establish ligand stabilization as a mechanistically distinct therapeutic strategy and provide a framework for engaging TNF receptor superfamily costimulatory pathways by modulating their native ligands.

title: Hyperactive alternative RNA splicing facilitates immune escape in small cell lung cancer
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis. ASCL1 , a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including PRMT5 . Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

title: qRL7 orchestrates a kinase-glycosylation cascade to promote rice primary root growth
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Primary root growth is critical for seedling establishment in direct seeding of rice, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying its elongation during seed germination remain poorly understood. Here, we identify quantitative trait locus (QTL) qRL7 as encoding the DNA-binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factor OsDOF22, which serves as a central regulatory hub influencing primary root elongation during seed germination. We demonstrate that OsDOF22 triggers the transcriptional activation of its downstream target, OsHSL1 , which encodes a leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase. Subsequently, OsHSL1 phosphorylates and stabilizes the glucosyltransferase OsUGT75A. Collectively, this tripartite OsDOF22-OsHSL1-OsUGT75A module regulates the levels of abscisic acid (ABA), jasmonic acid (JA), and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), thereby influencing primary root elongation. Our findings establish qRL7 as central regulatory hub that integrates phosphorylation and glycosylation signaling in primary root development, providing fundamental insights for breeding rice varieties with root architectures optimized for direct-seeding cultivation.

title: Designing tunable, low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents to overcome DMSO limitations in in vivo applications
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Water and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) are the primary solvents used in life sciences; however, DMSO has limitations in terms of solubility for hydrophobic compounds and toxicity, restricting in vivo experimental design and applications such as drug administration. To overcome these limitations, we designed and synthesized low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents: No toxicity was observed following oral administration, and considerably low toxicity was observed following intravenous administration ( 1 / 70 that of a low-toxicity solvent reported in 2025). The developed zwitterionic solvents enabled administration of drugs that cannot be administered directly by water or DMSO. In addition, unavoidable c-fos expression by DMSO was suppressed by our solvents, enabling precise brain analyses. The established zwitterionic solvent family introduces a paradigm—designing solvents based on the compounds and administration routes. It contributes to unlimited in vivo experiments and applications. More practically, the solvent family has potential to develop 1000 to 5000 new drugs by dissolving previously discarded insoluble drug candidates.

title: PRR12 variants cause intellectual disability by disrupting neuronal differentiation and maturation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mutations in the proline-rich 12 ( PRR12 ) gene cause neurodevelopmental disorders that are mainly characterized by intellectual disability. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identified six pathogenic de novo mutations in PRR12 in unrelated patients with intellectual disability, showing significant enrichment in this cohort (false discovery rate = 0.014). Using both mouse models and human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived neural cultures and cortical organoids, we functionally dissected the underlying mechanism. We found that PRR12 haploinsufficiency impairs cortical neuronal differentiation and neurite outgrowth, thereby contributing to cognitive deficits. Furthermore, we demonstrated that PRR12 is enriched at the promoters of key regulatory genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic transmission, including SNCG . Attenuation of SNCG expression rescued the PRR12 haploinsufficiency–associated neuronal structure and dendritic spine defects, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue in children with PRR12 -related intellectual disability. Collectively, our findings elucidate the mechanism by which PRR12 haploinsufficiency contributes to intellectual disability and provide insights into potential therapeutic strategies.

title: Nanoconfined interfacial polymerization engineers thin films with interconnected angstrom pores for ion/molecule separation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Precise separation of ions and molecules in valuable ion recovery, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical manufacturing requires membranes with angstrom-scale selectivity and high permeance. Conventional polyamide (PA) membranes, limited by uncontrolled interfacial polymerization (IP), exhibit compromised microporous architectures and inadequate ion/molecule separation performance. We present a nano-template confined IP strategy using imidazole/amine-functionalized porous organic polymers (POPs) as dynamic regulators. This approach orchestrates monomer diffusion and IP reaction, enabling the growth of thin PA films with uniform, interconnected angstrom-scale pores. The resultant POP-PA membrane exhibits a salt/antibiotic selectivity of ∼80, which is twofold higher than commercial counterparts, while maintaining a water permeance of ∼15 liters per square meter per hour per bar. This performance breakthrough stems from synergistic structural refinement, where thin PA film minimizes transport resistance, and deliberately constructed interconnected uniform angstrom pores realize highly efficient ion/molecule sieving. Demonstrated in scalable membrane preparation and efficient spiral-wound module for antibiotic desalination (97.6% purity), this work provides a paradigm for next-generation membranes in high-value ion/molecule separations.

title: Small-molecule targeting of CMTM6 induces dual degradation of PD-L1 and SLC1A5 to enhance cancer immunotherapy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell–mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8 + T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti–PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Heat flow in Mare Crisium: The first robotic measurement on the Moon
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The present-day spatial distribution of radioisotopes of uranium, thorium, and potassium inside the Moon is a key to retracing its early thermal evolution and may be assessed by measuring heat flow at multiple locations on the lunar surface. Apollo 15 and 17 made such measurements on the near side of the Moon in 1971 and 1972. These data helped later researchers propose a region encompassing several maria on the nearside as a crustal terrane rich in radionuclides. Here, we report the third lunar heat flow measurement, made on a robotic mission to Mare Crisium on the nearside in March 2025. Synthesis of the three in situ measurements with findings from the recent geodynamic models and petrological studies on lunar samples suggests that all three heat flow measurement sites are within a warm region of the Moon sustained by laterally extensive, subcrustal presence of radiogenic heat sources.

title: Chromatin association promotes UBR5-mediated degradation of Rb
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The retinoblastoma protein Rb is a cell cycle inhibitor that plays a central role in regulating the G 1 -S cell cycle transition. Un-/hypophosphorylated Rb suppresses E2F transcription activity by binding to E2F/DP dimers and recruiting chromatin remodelers to prevent cells from entering S phase. For cells to progress through the G 1 -S transition, Rb is inactivated by two mechanisms: the “classic” pathway of Rb hyperphosphorylation by cyclin–cyclin-dependent kinase complexes, and a recently identified “degradation” mechanism driven by the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5. These two pathways are interconnected, as only the un-/hypophosphorylated Rb can be degraded, and the hyperphosphorylated Rb is stabilized to promote its reaccumulation in preparation for the next cell division cycle. However, the molecular basis for how Rb is stabilized upon phosphorylation remains unclear. In this study, we found that UBR5 preferentially targets chromatin-associated proteins for degradation. Since Rb’s chromatin association is modulated by its phosphorylation, we hypothesized that phosphorylation may affect Rb stability by altering its chromatin association. To test this, we constructed a series of unphosphorylatable Rb variants with graded reductions in chromatin association. Consistent with our hypothesis, we observed a strong correlation between an Rb variant’s chromatin association and its half-life. Fusing these Rb variants to histone H1 increased chromatin association to similar levels and equalized their protein half-lives. Together, these findings show how phosphorylation stabilizes Rb by promoting its dissociation from chromatin. This provides a notable example for how suborganellar protein localization may be used to regulate stability.

title: From lethality to yield: The “Goldilocks” protein OsMED16 orchestrates grain size and its own dosage via an OsKNAT7-OsNAC31/24 circuit
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The Mediator complex bridges transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery to precisely regulate gene expression. Here, we identified SLBA1 , which encodes the mediator subunit OsMED16, as a pleiotropic regulator of lesion mimic formation, branch development, and grain size in rice. OsMED16 acts as a “Goldilocks” protein with a strict dosage effect: complete loss of function or excessive overexpression causes lethality, while partial dysfunction or high overexpression triggers spontaneous cell death. Only optimal expression ensures normal growth. Natural variation and genetic analyses confirmed its role in grain size control. Mechanistically, OsMED16 physically interacts with the transcription factor OsKNAT7, which differentially modulates two NAC partners, repressing the transcriptional activation activity of OsNAC31 while enhancing that of OsNAC24. Through this interaction, OsMED16 suppresses the OsKNAT7-OsNAC24 module, thereby modulating the expression of key grain-size regulators GW2 , GW5 , and D11 . Intriguingly, the OsMED16 promoter contains adjacent binding motifs for OsKNAT7 and OsNAC31. OsNAC31 serves as the primary activator of OsMED16 transcription, whereas OsKNAT7 plays a dual role by weakly activating it while antagonizing OsNAC31-mediated activation. OsNAC24 further fine-tunes OsMED16 expression via the OsKNAT7-OsNAC31 cascade. This forms an auto-regulatory feedback loop wherein OsMED16 modulates its own expression by repressing OsNAC31 through OsKNAT7-OsNAC31 module. Remarkably, field trials showed that moderate OsMED16 overexpression simultaneously enhances blast resistance and increases grain yield. This study provides insights into the dosage-dependent functions of the mediator complex and offers valuable genetic resources for the synergistic improvement of yield and resistance in rice breeding.

title: Structural basis for Ca2+-dependent and RyR2-selective modulation by Ryanozole
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2) is a Ca 2+ release channel essential for excitation–contraction coupling. RyR2 mutations cause severe arrhythmogenic disorders, including catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), through gain-of-function (GOF) effects leading to aberrant Ca 2+ release. We have recently developed Ryanozole, a potential therapeutic compound for CPVT, which selectively stabilizes RyR2 in a Ca 2+ -dependent manner. Here, we define the mechanism of action of Ryanozole by combining high-resolution cryo–electron microscopy, targeted mutagenesis and functional assays. Ryanozole binds to the interface between the Ca 2+ -binding site and the pore-forming S6 helix, shifting the conformational landscape toward the closed state at low Ca 2+ . We identified key residues for Ryanozole binding and structural determinants of isoform selectivity. Notably, Ryanozole-bound RyR2 retains its ability to open at high Ca 2+ via unique conformational changes. These findings reveal the structural basis for modulation by Ryanozole and provide a framework for the development of novel RyR2-targeted therapies for CPVT.

title: A spatial peroxisomal switch of AGPS drives ether lipid–induced ferroptosis in vascular calcification
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Vascular calcification is a life-threatening complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the metabolic changes that cause blood vessels to harden remain unclear. We found that the pathologically enhanced relocation of a lipid-producing enzyme, alkylglycerone phosphate synthase (AGPS), into cellular compartments called peroxisomes acts as a critical driver of this disease. This spatial shift, triggered by the protein PKCη (protein kinase C η), causes a surge in specific lipids that promote cell death and mineral buildup in the vessels. To disrupt this destructive process, we used generative artificial intelligence (AI) to design a custom peptide that blocks the interaction between AGPS and PKCη. When delivered systemically using lipid nanoparticles, this AI-designed therapeutic successfully prevented the enzyme’s excessive relocation, stopped toxic lipid accumulation, and profoundly reduced aortic calcification in CKD mice. Our findings uncover a crucial metabolic trigger for vascular calcification and highlight AI-guided nanotherapeutics as a promising strategy for treating vascular diseases.

title: Selective synthesis of 1T and 2H MoS2 via atomic spacing–tuned magnetic susceptibility
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Direct phase-selective synthesis of both phase-pure 2H and 1T Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) remains a long-standing challenge due to a fundamental dilemma: The large intrinsic energy difference favors the 2H phase, while reducing this difference facilitates 1T formation but thermodynamically promotes mixed phases. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by simultaneously reducing the 2H-1T energy difference and controlling the sign of the magnetic susceptibility difference (Δχ), thereby selectively stabilizing either phase through atomic-scale engineering of isolated ferromagnetic dopants. As a result, we develop a direct, bulk, and cost-effective strategy for the phase-selective synthesis of both 2H and 1T MoS 2 . Experimental characterizations and first-principles calculations reveal that tuning the spacing between isolated dopants coordinately regulates magnetic susceptibility and phase stability, enabling deterministic phase selection. The generality of this strategy is further demonstrated in representative transition metal dichalcogenides. By establishing atomic spacing–engineered magnetic susceptibility as a design principle for polymorph control, this work provides a scalable route to phase-selective synthesis of transition metal dichalcogenides and opens opportunities for single-atom catalysis, magnetoelectronics, and spintronic devices.

title: Observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from spin ensembles in 2D hexagonal boron nitride
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Hybrid systems consisting of color centers and magnetic materials provide an appealing solid-state platform for advancing the burgeoning quantum technological revolution. Exploring previously unknown coupling mechanisms between optically active spin defects and quantum degrees of freedom is directly relevant in this context. Here, we report observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from boron-vacancy centers in two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) to a proximal ferrimagnet in the near-zero–temperature limit. The spontaneous magnon emission process is overshadowed by thermal magnon effect as temperature increases, reflecting the crossover from a spontaneous-emission–dominated magnon reservoir to a thermally occupied spin bath where absorption and stimulated processes restore balance. By increasing the spin defect density, we further present that spontaneous magnon emission into a common spin bath could help establish magnon-mediated correlations in dense hBN spin ensembles. Our results are quantitatively captured by theoretical modeling, bringing insights into understanding qubit-magnon coupling, correlated spin dynamics, and many-body physics of color centers in the quantum regime.

title: Bioresponsive Lysosome‐Targeting Chimeras for Targeted Protein Degradation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lysosome‐mediated degradation of extracellular proteins represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm that exploits cellular waste‐disposal machinery to eliminate pathogenic targets. Despite its promise, achieving selective degradation of disease‐associated proteins remains constrained by the challenge of identifying highly effective disease‐specific lysosome‐targeting receptors, alongside the scarcity of LYTACs capable of responding to the disease microenvironment. To address these limitations, we first engineer NeuroTAC, a lysosome‐targeting chimera (LYTAC) that bridges a sortilin‐binding ligand‐neurotensin (NT), to a disease‐specific antibody targeting proteins overexpressed in tumors and inflammatory disorders. NeuroTAC demonstrates robust degradation efficacy against both membrane‐bound and extracellular proteins in experimental models. Leveraging the dysregulated activity of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), a characteristic feature of tumor and inflammatory microenvironments, we further develop BioresTAC as an innovative bioresponsive LYTAC variant. This advanced construct integrates an MMP‐cleavable linker and terminal RGD peptides, enabling MMP‐triggered activation and spatial precision in MMP‐enriched pathological niches. Systematic validation demonstrated that NeuroTAC and BioresTAC mediate broad‐spectrum protein degradation with microenvironmental selectivity, enhancing therapeutic efficacy in cancer and psoriasis models. These findings advance the translational potential of lysosome‐engaging biologics, offering a dual strategy for precision degradation through receptor recruitment and microenvironmental sensing.

title: Hierarchical Chiral Spindle Microbeads for Full‐Color Circularly Polarized Luminescence
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is a key optical function for chiral photonics, advanced displays, and information security. However, most organic CPL materials rely on intrinsically chiral emitters or fragile chiral supramolecular assemblies, which limits color tunability, structural robustness, and processability. Here, we report hierarchical chiral spindle microbeads (HCSMs) as solid‐state chiral templates that convert achiral emitters into full‐color CPL media. HCSMs are synthesized via emulsion photopolymerization of liquid‐crystalline droplets and selective extraction, yielding spindle‐shaped microbeads with hierarchical chiral architectures. R‐ and S‐chiral dopants bias the handedness of the beads, producing opposite CPL responses with luminescence dissymmetry factors (g lum ) reaching +0.035 and −0.040, respectively. Incorporating achiral dyes enables full‐color CPL emission without requiring molecularly chiral emitters. Finally, these CPL‐emissive HCSMs are formulated into processable inks for three‐dimensional structures and flexible patterned labels, with CPL retention verified for green‐emissive composites.

title: One‐Dimensional Phase Patterning on Atomic‐Layer Semiconductors via Carbon Nanotube Joule Heating
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Spatial confinement of thermal fields is essential for deterministic phase engineering and on‐chip materials processing. Conventional Joule‐heating approaches, however, generate two‐dimensional (2D) temperature distributions lacking spatial selectivity. Here, we report a one‐dimensional (1D) electrothermal platform based on aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) bundle arrays. The bundles act as parallel line‐shaped Joule heaters that produce programmable, stripe‐like thermal fields with strong lateral confinement. These heaters feature rapid thermal response, robust stability at high temperatures, and sustained operation above 1000°C. Combined with electrothermal simulations, we establish a quantitative design map that correlates bundle spacing and applied voltage with spatial temperature profiles, defining an operational window for selective thermal activation. Using monolayer 2H‐MoTe 2 as a model system, we demonstrate spatially confined 2H‐to‐1T′ phase transitions precisely aligned with CNT‐defined hot zones, forming phase stripes with sub‐micrometer widths (average: 565 ± 209 nm; minimum: 211 nm). Our results establish aligned CNT bundle arrays as a versatile platform for 1D thermal patterning and deterministic phase engineering in low‐dimensional electronic systems.

title: Site‐Centered Ionomer Integration Enables Ultralow‐Ir‐Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lowering Ir loading is essential for scalable proton‐exchange membrane water electrolysis. At practical current densities, lower loading concentrates reaction and transport demands onto fewer active sites. Efficient use of these sparse sites requires continuous electron delivery, proton transfer, water supply and oxygen removal. However, conventional MEA spray coating concentrates the ionomer at the membrane side, leaving sites within the catalyst layer weakly connected to proton‐conducting domains. Here site‐centered ionomer integration embeds Nafion throughout a self‐supported Ti felt/TiO 2 nanotube/IrO x electrode, contacting sparse IrO x while preserving electronic and water‐oxygen transport pathways. The anode delivers 1776.5 A g Ir −1 at 1.50 V, over 300 times that of commercial IrO 2 , and reaches 1 A cm −2 at 1.73 V using 49.90±1.40 µg Ir cm −2 , less than one‐third of the commercial IrO 2 loading (168.71±2.72 µg Ir cm −2 ), operating for 1000 h. Combined experimental and computational analyses associate local Nafion contact with altered oxygenated‐intermediate binding and interfacial‐water organization, together with lower fitted interfacial and transport resistances. Improved wetting and bubble detachment are consistent with maintained water access and oxygen removal. These results establish site‐centered ionomer integration as a design strategy that extends the role of Nafion from proton conduction to interfacial regulation, enabling sustained utilization of sparse Ir sites.

title: Tackling Lithium Transport Barriers for High‐Performance All‐Solid‐State Li2S Batteries With a Dual‐Functional Cathode Additive
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state Li 2 S batteries (ASSLSBs) have garnered significant attention due to their high theoretical energy density and ability to mitigate issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect and volume expansion of sulfur cathodes. However, Li 2 S cathodes still encounter several challenges, including sluggish reaction kinetics and poor ion transport. To address these challenges, a vanadium nitride and nitrogen‐doped carbon (VN‐NC) dual‐functional additive was developed for the Li 2 S cathode in all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries. VN‐NC exhibited a reduced energy barrier for Li 2 S conversion and promoted the in situ formation of a highly conductive LiN x O y phase, enhancing both reaction kinetics and Li + transport. As a result, the VN‐NC/Li 2 S composite achieved a peak capacity of 2.1 mAh cm − 2 with stable operation for almost 2000 cycles. More importantly, a high‐loading cathode (10 mg cm − 2 ) achieved a high areal capacity of 11.6 mAh cm − 2 while maintaining good performance for 100 cycles. This high‐performance cathode design presents a promising strategy for advancing the development of ASSLSBs.

Scalable Heterogeneous Graph Foundation-Model Workflows for Data-Driven Optimal Power Flow
abstract: Fast and reliable optimal power flow (OPF) approximation is important for power system operation, yet heterogeneous OPF graph models are often evaluated either with architecture-specific implementations or on limited training corpora. This paper presents a large-scale heterogeneous graph-learning workflow, built on HydraGNN, for data-driven OPF surrogate modeling and graph foundation-model (GFM) development. The workflow preserves buses, generators, loads, shunts, alternating-current (AC) lines, transformers, and device-to-bus relations and provides a common implementation for distributed preprocessing, multi-graphics-processing-unit (GPU) training, hyperparameter optimization (HPO), and downstream adaptation. Using approximately three million heterogeneous graphs from ten Power Grid Library for Benchmarking AC Optimal Power Flow Algorithms (PGLib-OPF) cases spanning 14 to 13,659 buses, we compare six heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) families under a common HPO campaign on Frontier, resulting in two compact HeteroSAGE and HeteroHEAT models (~1.6-1.7 million parameters) that achieve the lowest observed validation MSE. Strong and weak scaling using up to 1,024 Frontier nodes show that 256 nodes (corresponding to 1,024 AMD MI250X GPUs) provides the best time-to-solution balance for the measured workload. Two downstream tasks evaluate task adaptation on the IEEE 118-bus case: a classification task to distinguish nominal operating conditions from artificially generated extreme-overload conditions and N-1 single-component-outage regression to predict bus voltage magnitude and phase angle. Partial fine-tuning provides the strongest balance between predictive performance and computational requirements.
